section: 4.2 Fundamental Labeled Operators (\(\operatorname{SEQ}, \operatorname{SET}, \operatorname{CYC}\)), Connected Components (\(\exp/\ln\)), & Parity Filters
text:
4.2 Fundamental Labeled Operators (\(\operatorname{SEQ}, \operatorname{SET}, \operatorname{CYC}\)), Connected Components (\(\exp/\ln\)), & Parity Filters
Suppose \(\mathcal{A}\) is a labeled combinatorial class with no objects of size \(0\) (\(a_0 = 0\), which algebraically means \(\operatorname{val}(\widehat{A}) \ge 1\)). How do we count composite structures built by assembling \(k\) non-empty \(\mathcal{A}\)-components?

Single-Step Verbalized Derivations of \(\operatorname{SEQ}\), \(\operatorname{SET}\), and \(\operatorname{CYC}\)

1. Labeled Sequences (\(\operatorname{SEQ}_k(\mathcal{A})\) and \(\operatorname{SEQ}(\mathcal{A})\))

Concrete Object: An ordered \(k\)-tuple \((\alpha_1, \alpha_2, \dots, \alpha_k)\) of \(\mathcal{A}\)-structures whose label sets \(U_1 \sqcup U_2 \sqcup \dots \sqcup U_k = [n]\) partition \(\{1, 2, \dots, n\}\).
Single-Step Derivation: By iterating the binary labeled product \(\mathcal{A} \star \mathcal{A}\) exactly \(k\) times, the EGF of \(\operatorname{SEQ}_k(\mathcal{A})\) is \(\widehat{A}(x)^k\). Summing over all sequence lengths \(k \ge 0\) (which converges formally in \(K[[x]]\) because \(\operatorname{val}(\widehat{A}) \ge 1 \implies \operatorname{val}(\widehat{A}^k) \ge k\)): \[\widehat{\operatorname{SEQ}(\mathcal{A})}(x) = \sum_{k=0}^{\infty} \widehat{A}(x)^k = \frac{1}{1 - \widehat{A}(x)}\]



2. Labeled Sets (\(\operatorname{SET}_k(\mathcal{A})\) and the Exponential Formula \(\operatorname{SET}(\mathcal{A})\))

Concrete Object: An unordered collection \(\{\alpha_1, \alpha_2, \dots, \alpha_k\}\) of \(k\) non-empty \(\mathcal{A}\)-structures whose label sets partition \(\{1, 2, \dots, n\}\). For example, a graph is an unordered set of its connected components; a forest is an unordered set of its component trees; a set partition of \([n]\) into \(k\) blocks is an unordered set of \(k\) non-empty subsets.
Single-Step Derivation:

Start with an ordered \(k\)-tuple \((\alpha_1, \dots, \alpha_k) \in \operatorname{SEQ}_k(\mathcal{A})\), counted by \(\widehat{A}(x)^k\).
Because \(a_0 = 0\), each component \(\alpha_i\) has a non-empty label set \(U_i \neq \emptyset\). Since \(U_1, \dots, U_k\) are pairwise disjoint and non-empty, the \(k\) components \(\alpha_1, \dots, \alpha_k\) are guaranteed to be pairwise distinct (for instance, their minimum labels \(\min U_1, \dots, \min U_k\) are \(k\) distinct integers!).
Therefore, every unordered set \(\{\alpha_1, \dots, \alpha_k\}\) corresponds to exactly \(k!\) ordered \(k\)-tuples in \(\operatorname{SEQ}_k(\mathcal{A})\) obtained by permuting the \(k\) components.
Dividing by \(k!\) and summing over all \(k \ge 0\) yields the Exponential Formula: \[\widehat{\operatorname{SET}_k(\mathcal{A})}(x) = \frac{\widehat{A}(x)^k}{k!}, \qquad \widehat{\operatorname{SET}(\mathcal{A})}(x) = \sum_{k=0}^{\infty} \frac{\widehat{A}(x)^k}{k!} = \exp\bigl(\widehat{A}(x)\bigr)\] (Local Algebraic Hypothesis: Requires \([x^0]\widehat{A}(x) = 0\) for formal convergence and \(1, 2, \dots, N \in K^\times\)—i.e., \(p > N\) over \(\mathbb{F}_p\)—when computing modulo \(x^{N+1}\).)




3. Labeled Directed Cycles (\(\operatorname{CYC}_k(\mathcal{A})\) and \(\operatorname{CYC}(\mathcal{A})\))

Concrete Object: A directed cycle of \(k \ge 1\) non-empty \(\mathcal{A}\)-structures arranged around a circle, where two arrangements are identical if and only if one is a cyclic rotation of the other.
Single-Step Derivation:

Start with an ordered \(k\)-tuple \((\alpha_1, \dots, \alpha_k) \in \operatorname{SEQ}_k(\mathcal{A})\), counted by \(\widehat{A}(x)^k\).
Because \(\alpha_1, \dots, \alpha_k\) have disjoint non-empty label sets, all \(k\) cyclic shifts \((\alpha_1, \dots, \alpha_k), (\alpha_2, \dots, \alpha_k, \alpha_1), \dots\) are pairwise distinct (no periodic symmetry can occur in a labeled cycle!).
Thus every directed \(k\)-cycle corresponds to exactly \(k\) ordered \(k\)-tuples. Dividing by \(k\) and summing over \(k \ge 1\) yields the formal logarithm: \[\widehat{\operatorname{CYC}_k(\mathcal{A})}(x) = \frac{\widehat{A}(x)^k}{k}, \qquad \widehat{\operatorname{CYC}(\mathcal{A})}(x) = \sum_{k=1}^{\infty} \frac{\widehat{A}(x)^k}{k} = \ln\left(\frac{1}{1 - \widehat{A}(x)}\right)\] (Local Algebraic Hypothesis: Requires \([x^0]\widehat{A}(x) = 0\) for formal convergence and \(1, 2, \dots, N \in K^\times\)—i.e., \(p > N\) over \(\mathbb{F}_p\)—when computing modulo \(x^{N+1}\).)




4. Labeled Undirected Simple Cycles (\(\operatorname{UCYC}_{\ge 3}(\mathcal{A})\))

Concrete Object: An undirected simple cycle of \(k \ge 3\) non-empty \(\mathcal{A}\)-components (such as a simple cycle of vertices in a cactus graph or \(2\)-regular simple graph), where reversing the orientation of the cycle produces the same undirected cycle.
Single-Step Derivation: For every \(k \ge 3\), a cycle of length \(k\) has \(2\) distinct orientations (clockwise and counterclockwise), whereas \(k = 1\) (a self-loop) and \(k = 2\) (a double edge) are excluded in simple undirected graphs and do not have \(2\) distinct orientations. Subtracting \(k = 1\) and \(k = 2\) from \(\operatorname{CYC}(\mathcal{A})\) and dividing by \(2\) gives: \[\widehat{\operatorname{UCYC}_{\ge 3}(\mathcal{A})}(x) = \sum_{k=3}^{\infty} \frac{\widehat{A}(x)^k}{2k} = \frac{1}{2}\ln\left(\frac{1}{1 - \widehat{A}(x)}\right) - \frac{\widehat{A}(x)}{2} - \frac{\widehat{A}(x)^2}{4}\]





The Connected-to-General Bridge: \(\widehat{G}(x) = \exp\bigl(\widehat{C}(x)\bigr) \iff \widehat{C}(x) = \ln \widehat{G}(x)\)
The Exponential Formula works in both directions:

Forward (\(\exp\): Connected \(\to\) General): If we know the EGF \(\widehat{C}(x)\) of connected components (with \(c_0 = 0\)), then \(\widehat{G}(x) = \exp\bigl(\widehat{C}(x)\bigr)\) counts all structures whose connected components belong to \(\mathcal{C}\).

Example 1 (Set Partitions & Bell Numbers): A non-empty set of labeled atoms has \(c_n = 1\) for all \(n \ge 1\), so \(\widehat{C}(x) = \sum_{n=1}^\infty \frac{x^n}{n!} = e^x - 1\). A set partition of \([n]\) into \(k\) blocks has EGF \(\frac{(e^x - 1)^k}{k!}\) (counting Stirling numbers of the second kind \(\left\{\begin{matrix} n \\ k \end{matrix}\right\} = n!\,[x^n]\frac{(e^x-1)^k}{k!}\)), and a set partition into an arbitrary number of blocks has EGF \(\widehat{B}(x) = \exp(e^x - 1)\) (counting the Bell numbers \(B_n = n!\,[x^n]\exp(e^x - 1)\)).
Example 2 (Permutations via Cycle Decomposition): Every permutation is an unordered \(\operatorname{SET}\) of directed cycles \(\operatorname{CYC}(\mathcal{Z})\): \[\mathcal{P} = \operatorname{SET}\bigl(\operatorname{CYC}(\mathcal{Z})\bigr) \quad \Longrightarrow \quad \widehat{P}(x) = \exp\!\left(\ln\frac{1}{1 - x}\right) = \frac{1}{1 - x}\] More powerfully, if a problem restricts the allowed cycle lengths of a permutation to a subset \(S \subseteq \{1, 2, \dots, N\}\), we simply filter the cycle EGF to \(\widehat{C}_S(x) = \sum_{k \in S} \frac{x^k}{k}\) and take a single polynomial exponential: \[\widehat{P}_S(x) = \exp\!\left(\sum_{k \in S} \frac{x^k}{k}\right)\]

Backward (\(\ln\): General \(\to\) Connected): Often it is trivial to count all labeled graphs \(\mathcal{G}\) (disconnected or not), while counting connected labeled graphs \(\mathcal{C}\) directly seems intractable. Since \(\mathcal{G} = \operatorname{SET}(\mathcal{C}) \iff \widehat{G}(x) = \exp\bigl(\widehat{C}(x)\bigr)\) with \([x^0]\widehat{G}(x) = g_0 = 1\), applying the formal logarithm poly_ln inverts the construction in \(O(N \log N)\) time: \[\widehat{C}(x) = \ln \widehat{G}(x)\]


Hand-Checkable Trace (\(N \le 4\)): Connected Simple Labeled Graphs
On \(n\) labeled vertices \(\{1, 2, \dots, n\}\), there are \(\binom{n}{2}\) potential undirected edges, so there are \(g_n = 2^{\binom{n}{2}}\) simple labeled graphs in total (\(g_0 = 1, g_1 = 1, g_2 = 2, g_3 = 8, g_4 = 64\)). Thus: \[\widehat{G}(x) = 1 + x + 2\frac{x^2}{2!} + 8\frac{x^3}{3!} + 64\frac{x^4}{4!} + O(x^5) = 1 + x + x^2 + \frac{4}{3}x^3 + \frac{8}{3}x^4 + O(x^5)\] Let \(U(x) = \widehat{G}(x) - 1 = x + x^2 + \frac{4}{3}x^3 + \frac{8}{3}x^4 + O(x^5)\). Expanding \(\widehat{C}(x) = \ln(1 + U(x)) = U - \frac{U^2}{2} + \frac{U^3}{3} - \frac{U^4}{4} + O(x^5)\): \[\begin{aligned}
U(x) &= x + x^2 + \frac{4}{3}x^3 + \frac{8}{3}x^4 \\
-\frac{1}{2}U(x)^2 &= -\frac{1}{2}x^2 - x^3 - \frac{11}{6}x^4 \\
+\frac{1}{3}U(x)^3 &= \frac{1}{3}x^3 + x^4 \\
-\frac{1}{4}U(x)^4 &= -\frac{1}{4}x^4
\end{aligned}\] Summing the columns gives \(\widehat{C}(x) = x + \frac{1}{2}x^2 + \frac{2}{3}x^3 + \frac{19}{12}x^4 + O(x^5)\), so \(c_n = n!\,[x^n]\widehat{C}(x)\) is:

\(c_1 = 1! (1) = 1\) (single vertex).
\(c_2 = 2! \left(\frac{1}{2}\right) = 1\) (the single edge \(K_2\)).
\(c_3 = 3! \left(\frac{2}{3}\right) = 4\) (out of \(8\) graphs on \(3\) vertices, \(1\) is \(K_3\) and \(3\) are paths of length \(2\)).
\(c_4 = 4! \left(\frac{19}{12}\right) = 38\) (out of \(64\) graphs on \(4\) vertices, \(38\) are connected).







NoteAlgorithm Contract 4.1: Connected Labeled Enumeration via EGF Logarithm




Input: Sequence \((g_0, g_1, \dots, g_N)\) counting all labeled structures in class \(\mathcal{G} = \operatorname{SET}(\mathcal{C})\) of size \(0 \le n \le N\), modulus \(p > N\).
Preconditions: \(g_0 = 1\) (unique empty structure of size \(0\)), and \(p > N\) so that \(1!, 2!, \dots, N!\) are invertible in \(\mathbb{F}_p\).
Output: Sequence \((c_1, c_2, \dots, c_N)\) counting connected labeled structures in \(\mathcal{C}\) of size \(1 \le n \le N\) modulo \(p\).
Algorithm Steps:

Form the truncated EGF \(\widehat{G}(x) = \sum_{n=0}^N \left(g_n \cdot (n!)^{-1} \bmod p\right) x^n \in \mathbb{F}_p[x]/(x^{N+1})\).
Compute \(\widehat{C}(x) \equiv \ln \widehat{G}(x) \equiv \int_0^x \widehat{G}'(t) \widehat{G}(t)^{-1}\,dt \pmod{x^{N+1}}\) using polynomial inversion and formal integration.
Extract \(c_n = n! [x^n]\widehat{C}(x) \bmod p\) for \(1 \le n \le N\).

Complexity: \(O(N \log N)\) time and \(O(N)\) space.
Correctness Invariant: Every structure in \(\mathcal{G}_n\) decomposes into a unique unordered set of \(k \ge 0\) connected components on disjoint non-empty vertex subsets \(U_1 \sqcup \dots \sqcup U_k = [n]\), which matches \([x^n/n!]\sum_{k \ge 0} \widehat{C}(x)^k / k!\) without omission or double counting.







Hyperbolic Parity Filters (\(\cosh x, \sinh x\)) for Labeled Words
Suppose we form a sequence (word) of length \(n\) over an alphabet of \(D\) colors \(\{1, 2, \dots, D\}\). Why is a word of length \(n\) a labeled object? Because the \(n\) positions \(\{1, 2, \dots, n\}\) in the word are distinguishable! Choosing a word of length \(n\) in which color \(i\) appears \(c_i\) times (\(c_1 + \dots + c_D = n\)) is identical to partitioning the position labels \(\{1, 2, \dots, n\}\) into \(D\) ordered buckets \((U_1, \dots, U_D)\) of sizes \((c_1, \dots, c_D)\) in \(\binom{n}{c_1, \dots, c_D} = \frac{n!}{c_1! \cdots c_D!}\) ways.
Consequently, if color \(i\) is only allowed to appear a number of times \(c_i \in S_i \subseteq \mathbb{Z}_{\ge 0}\), its individual EGF is \(\widehat{E}_i(x) = \sum_{c \in S_i} \frac{x^c}{c!}\), and the number of valid words of length \(n\) is: \[\text{Words}_n = n! [x^n] \prod_{i=1}^{D} \widehat{E}_i(x)\]
In particular, when frequency constraints depend on parity (even vs. odd occurrences), we cancel odd or even powers of \(e^x\) and \(e^{-x}\) using the hyperbolic EGF filters: \[\begin{aligned}
\text{Arbitrary frequency } (c \ge 0): &\quad \sum_{c=0}^{\infty} \frac{x^c}{c!} = e^x \\
\text{Even frequency } (2 \mid c): &\quad \sum_{m=0}^{\infty} \frac{x^{2m}}{(2m)!} = \frac{e^x + e^{-x}}{2} = \cosh x \\
\text{Odd frequency } (2 \nmid c): &\quad \sum_{m=0}^{\infty} \frac{x^{2m+1}}{(2m+1)!} = \frac{e^x - e^{-x}}{2} = \sinh x
\end{aligned}\] Because \(e^{ax} \cdot e^{bx} = e^{(a+b)x}\) holds in \(K[[x]]\), products of \(\cosh x\) and \(\sinh x\) expand via the Binomial Theorem into linear combinations of \(e^{kx}\), whose \(\left[\frac{x^n}{n!}\right]\) coefficient is simply \(k^n\)! We will see this technique at full power in Mastery 2 (Luogu P5401 — [CTS2019] 珍珠).



Pointing (\(\Theta \mathcal{A}\)) and Unpointing (\(\Theta^{-1}\)) in the Labeled World
The pointing operator \(\Theta \mathcal{A}\) takes an object \(\alpha \in \mathcal{A}_n\) and marks one of its \(n\) labeled atoms as a distinguished root. Since there are \(n\) choices of which atom to mark, \((\Theta \mathcal{A})_n = n \cdot a_n\). On EGFs: \[\widehat{\Theta \mathcal{A}}(x) = \sum_{n=1}^{\infty} (n a_n) \frac{x^n}{n!} = x \sum_{n=1}^{\infty} a_n \frac{x^{n-1}}{(n-1)!} = x \widehat{A}'(x) = \vartheta \widehat{A}(x)\] Crucially, because all \(n\) atoms carry distinct labels \(1, 2, \dots, n\), the \(n\) pointed versions of any labeled object \(\alpha \in \mathcal{A}_n\) are always pairwise non-isomorphic. Thus unpointing a rooted labeled class \(\mathcal{T} = \Theta \mathcal{U}\) back to its unrooted class \(\mathcal{U}\) simply divides the \(n\)-th count by \(n\): \[u_n = \frac{t_n}{n} \quad (n \ge 1) \quad \Longleftrightarrow \quad \widehat{U}(x) = \int_0^x \frac{\widehat{T}(t)}{t}\,dt\] (Contrast this with the unlabeled setting of Chapter 03, where symmetries can make different vertices indistinguishable; as we will prove in Chapter 10 (§10.4), unpointing unlabeled trees requires Otter’s Dissimilarity Theorem \(U(x) = T(x) - \frac{1}{2}(T(x)^2 - T(x^2))\) instead of division by \(n\)!)

title: Chapter 04: The Labeled Symbolic Method: Exponential Generating Functions (EGFs), Boxed Products & Prüfer Sequences
section: 4.3 The Greene–Wilf Boxed Product (\(\mathcal{C} = \mathcal{A}^{\square} \star \mathcal{B}\)) & Bypassing Characteristic-\(p\) Breakdown
text:
4.3 The Greene–Wilf Boxed Product (\(\mathcal{C} = \mathcal{A}^{\square} \star \mathcal{B}\)) & Bypassing Characteristic-\(p\) Breakdown

Concrete Combinatorial Motivation: Isolating the Minimum Label \(1\)
Suppose we want to decompose a labeled graph or permutation on \(\{1, 2, \dots, n\}\) into two parts: a “first” component \(\alpha \in \mathcal{A}\) of size \(k \ge 1\) and the “rest” \(\beta \in \mathcal{B}\) of size \(n - k\), without overcounting by the number of components. The cleanest combinatorial way to break symmetry between components is to look at the component containing the globally smallest label (atom \(1\))!
Because atom \(1\) is forced to go into the \(\mathcal{A}\)-component of size \(k\), we do not have \(\binom{n}{k}\) ways to choose the label set \(U\) of \(\alpha\): atom \(1\) is already fixed in \(U\), and we only choose the remaining \(k - 1\) labels of \(U\) from the remaining \(n - 1\) labels \(\{2, 3, \dots, n\}\) in \(\binom{n-1}{k-1}\) ways!
This defines the Greene–Wilf Boxed Product (also known in Chinese literature as 有标号定根技巧, the minimum-label pivot technique), written \(\mathcal{C} = \mathcal{A}^{\square} \star \mathcal{B}\): \[c_n = \sum_{k=1}^{n} \binom{n-1}{k-1} a_k b_{n-k} \quad (n \ge 1), \qquad c_0 = 0\]



Diagnostic Signal & Reverse-Engineering the Differential Identity






TipDiagnostic Signal & Reverse-Engineering Scratchpad: The \(\binom{n-1}{k-1}\) Signature




The Diagnostic Signal: A recurrence of the form \(c_n = \sum_{k=1}^n \binom{n-1}{k-1} a_k b_{n-k}\), or a combinatorial transition that isolates the connected component / cycle / subtree containing vertex \(1\) (or the global minimum/maximum element) and distributes the remaining \(n - 1\) labels between \(k - 1\) internal companions and \(n - k\) external elements.
The Reverse-Engineering Scratchpad: Write out \(\binom{n-1}{k-1} = \frac{(n-1)!}{(k-1)!(n-k)!}\) and divide both sides of \(c_n = \sum_{k=1}^n \binom{n-1}{k-1} a_k b_{n-k}\) by \((n-1)!\): \[\frac{c_n}{(n-1)!} = \sum_{k=1}^{n} \left(\frac{a_k}{(k-1)!}\right) \left(\frac{b_{n-k}}{(n-k)!}\right)\] Now ask: what series has \(\frac{a_k}{(k-1)!}\) as the coefficient of \(x^{k-1}\)? Differentiating \(\widehat{A}(x) = \sum_{k=1}^\infty a_k \frac{x^k}{k!}\) with respect to \(x\) shifts the index down by \(1\) and cancels \(k\): \[\widehat{A}'(x) = \sum_{k=1}^{\infty} \frac{a_k}{(k-1)!} x^{k-1}\] Therefore, the right-hand side is the exact \([x^{n-1}]\) coefficient of \(\widehat{A}'(x)\widehat{B}(x)\), and the left-hand side is \([x^{n-1}]\widehat{C}'(x)\)!



This proves the Boxed Product Theorem: \[\mathcal{C} = \mathcal{A}^{\square} \star \mathcal{B} \quad \Longleftrightarrow \quad \widehat{C}'(x) = \widehat{A}'(x) \widehat{B}(x) \quad \Longleftrightarrow \quad \widehat{C}(x) = \int_0^x \widehat{A}'(t) \widehat{B}(t)\,dt\]

Re-deriving \(\mathcal{G} = \operatorname{SET}(\mathcal{C})\) via the Boxed Product
Let \(\mathcal{G}\) be all simple labeled graphs and \(\mathcal{C}\) be connected simple labeled graphs. Every non-empty graph in \(\mathcal{G}_n\) (\(n \ge 1\)) consists of the connected component containing vertex \(1\) (\(\mathcal{C}^{\square}\)) paired with an arbitrary graph on the remaining \(n - k\) vertices (\(\mathcal{G}\)): \[\mathcal{G} = \mathcal{E} + \mathcal{C}^{\square} \star \mathcal{G} \quad \Longleftrightarrow \quad g_n = \sum_{k=1}^{n} \binom{n-1}{k-1} c_k g_{n-k} \quad (n \ge 1)\] By the Boxed Product Theorem, differentiating \(\mathcal{G} = \mathcal{E} + \mathcal{C}^{\square} \star \mathcal{G}\) gives: \[\widehat{G}'(x) = \widehat{C}'(x) \widehat{G}(x) \quad \Longleftrightarrow \quad \widehat{C}'(x) = \frac{\widehat{G}'(x)}{\widehat{G}(x)} \quad \Longleftrightarrow \quad \widehat{C}(x) = \ln \widehat{G}(x)\] Notice how the Boxed Product explains why the formal derivative of \(\widehat{G}(x) = \exp\bigl(\widehat{C}(x)\bigr)\) satisfies \(\widehat{G}'(x) = \widehat{C}'(x)\widehat{G}(x)\): differentiating an EGF with respect to \(x\) removes the minimum label \(1\), rooting the structure at the unique component that held label \(1\)!







WarningFailure Mode & Remedy: Characteristic-\(p\) Breakdown of \(\ln\) and \(\exp\) (\(p \le N\)) Bypassed via the Boxed Product




The Failure Mode: Suppose you need to compute connected labeled graph counts \(c_n \pmod m\) up to \(N = 1000\), where the modulus \(m\) is either a small prime \(p \le N\) (e.g., \(p = 2, 3, 997\)), a composite integer (e.g., \(10^9 + 9\) or \(2^{64}\)), or any commutative ring \(R\) where \(2, 3, \dots, N\) are not invertible. If you attempt to run Algorithm Contract 4.1 (\(\widehat{C}(x) = \ln \widehat{G}(x) = \int \widehat{G}'(x)\widehat{G}(x)^{-1} dx\)), your code crashes immediately at two places:

Forming \(\widehat{G}(x) = \sum_{n=0}^N \frac{g_n}{n!} x^n\) divides by \(n!\), which is \(0 \pmod p\) for all \(n \ge p\).
Even if \(\widehat{G}(x)\) were given, the formal integral \(\int x^{p-1} dx = \frac{x^p}{p}\) divides by \(p \equiv 0 \pmod p\)!

Why the Obstruction Is Purely an Artifact of the Borel–Laplace Scaling: In the underlying Hurwitz ring \(K_{\text{exp}}[[x]]\), the combinatorial identity \(g_n = \sum_{k=1}^n \binom{n-1}{k-1} c_k g_{n-k}\) involves only integer binomial coefficients \(\binom{n-1}{k-1}\)! Furthermore, the \(k = n\) term on the right-hand side has coefficient \(\binom{n-1}{n-1} g_0 = 1 \cdot 1 = 1\), which is always invertible in every commutative ring \(R\).
The Division-Free Boxed Product Remedy: Isolating the \(k = n\) term (\(c_n g_0 = c_n\)) from \(g_n = \sum_{k=1}^n \binom{n-1}{k-1} c_k g_{n-k}\) yields an exact, 100% division-free recurrence valid over any commutative ring \(R\): \[c_n = g_n - \sum_{k=1}^{n-1} \binom{n-1}{k-1} c_k g_{n-k} \quad (n \ge 1)\] Using Pascal’s identity \(\binom{n}{k} = \binom{n-1}{k-1} + \binom{n-1}{k}\) to precompute binomial coefficients by addition only, this computes \(c_1, \dots, c_N\) in \(O(N^2)\) ring operations without a single division!
Hand-Checkable Trace over \(\mathbb{F}_2\) (\(p = 2 \le N = 4\)): For simple labeled graphs \(g_n = 2^{\binom{n}{2}}\), reducing modulo \(p = 2\) gives \(g_0 = 1, g_1 = 1, g_2 = 0, g_3 = 0, g_4 = 0\). Over \(\mathbb{F}_2\), \(\widehat{G}(x)\) and \(\ln \widehat{G}(x)\) do not exist past degree \(1\). Using the division-free Boxed Product recurrence modulo \(2\):

\(n = 1\): \(c_1 = g_1 = 1\).
\(n = 2\): \(c_2 = g_2 - \binom{1}{0} c_1 g_1 = 0 - 1(1)(1) \equiv 1 \pmod 2\) (matches \(c_2 = 1 \equiv 1 \pmod 2\)).
\(n = 3\): \(c_3 = g_3 - \binom{2}{0} c_1 g_2 - \binom{2}{1} c_2 g_1 = 0 - 1(1)(0) - 0(1)(1) \equiv 0 \pmod 2\) (matches \(c_3 = 4 \equiv 0 \pmod 2\)).
\(n = 4\): \(c_4 = g_4 - \binom{3}{0} c_1 g_3 - \binom{3}{1} c_2 g_2 - \binom{3}{2} c_3 g_1 = 0 - 0 - 0 - 0 \equiv 0 \pmod 2\) (matches \(c_4 = 38 \equiv 0 \pmod 2\)).










NoteAlgorithm Contract: Greene–Wilf Boxed Product & Division-Free \(\operatorname{SET}\) Inversion




Input: Sequence \((a_1, \dots, a_N)\) and \((b_0, \dots, b_N)\) for Boxed Product \(\mathcal{C} = \mathcal{A}^{\square} \star \mathcal{B}\), or sequence \((g_0, g_1, \dots, g_N)\) with \(g_0 = 1\) for inverting \(\mathcal{G} = \operatorname{SET}(\mathcal{C})\) (or sequence \((c_1, \dots, c_N)\) with \(c_0 = 0\) for forward \(\operatorname{SET}\) construction).
Preconditions:

Arbitrary Commutative Ring Regime (\(O(N^2)\) Division-Free): Valid over any commutative ring \(R\) (including small characteristic \(p \le N\), prime powers \(p^k\), or \(2^{64}\)); requires only \(\operatorname{val}(\mathcal{A}) \ge 1\) (\(c_0 = 0\)) and \(g_0 = 1\).
Invertible-Factorial Regime (\(O(N \log N)\) via EGF): Requires \(1, 2, \dots, N \in R^\times\) (e.g., \(\mathbb{F}_p\) with prime \(p > N\)).

Postcondition & Recurrence:

Boxed Product (\(\mathcal{C} = \mathcal{A}^{\square} \star \mathcal{B}\)): \[c_n = \sum_{k=1}^{n} \binom{n-1}{k-1} a_k b_{n-k} \quad (1 \le n \le N) \quad \Longleftrightarrow \quad \widehat{C}'(x) \equiv \widehat{A}'(x)\widehat{B}(x) \pmod{x^N}\]
Division-Free Connected Extraction (\(\mathcal{G} = \mathcal{E} + \mathcal{C}^{\square} \star \mathcal{G}\)): \[c_n = g_n - \sum_{k=1}^{n-1} \binom{n-1}{k-1} c_k g_{n-k}, \qquad g_n = \sum_{k=1}^{n} \binom{n-1}{k-1} c_k g_{n-k} \quad (1 \le n \le N)\]

Complexity: \(O(N^2)\) ring additions/multiplications and \(O(N)\) space over an arbitrary commutative ring \(R\) (using Pascal’s triangle \(\binom{n}{k} = \binom{n-1}{k-1} + \binom{n-1}{k}\)); \(O(N \log N)\) time and \(O(N)\) space via EGF derivative/integral when \(1, \dots, N \in R^\times\).
Correctness Invariant: Every non-empty labeled object on \(\{1, \dots, n\}\) has a unique component of size \(k \in \{1, \dots, n\}\) containing the minimum label \(1\), chosen in \(\binom{n-1}{k-1} c_k g_{n-k}\) ways without dividing by component multiplicity.

title: Chapter 04: The Labeled Symbolic Method: Exponential Generating Functions (EGFs), Boxed Products & Prüfer Sequences
section: 4.4 Prüfer Sequences, Cayley’s Formula & Degree-Constrained Labeled Trees
text:
4.4 Prüfer Sequences, Cayley’s Formula & Degree-Constrained Labeled Trees

Concrete Combinatorial Object: Labeled Trees with Prescribed Degrees
A labeled tree \(T\) of size \(n\) is a connected acyclic undirected graph on the vertex set \(V = \{1, 2, \dots, n\}\). In Chapter 11, we will study rooted trees via recursive functional equations \(\widehat{T}(x) = x e^{\widehat{T}(x)}\) and Lagrange Inversion. However, whenever a problem asks to count unrooted labeled trees subject to individual vertex degree constraints—for instance, fixing the degree \(\deg_T(i) = d_i\) of each vertex \(i\), bounding \(\deg_T(i) \le D\), or requiring \(\deg_T(i) \in S\) for all \(i\)—there is a direct, non-recursive bijection that converts the tree problem into a word-counting EGF problem: Prüfer’s Bijection (1918).


Constructive Bijection: Tree \(T \longleftrightarrow\) Prüfer Word \(P \in \{1, \dots, n\}^{n-2}\)
Assume \(n \ge 2\). We map any labeled tree \(T\) on \(\{1, 2, \dots, n\}\) to a sequence \(P = (p_1, p_2, \dots, p_{n-2}) \in \{1, 2, \dots, n\}^{n-2}\) of length \(n - 2\) by iteratively plucking leaves:

Encoding (\(T \mapsto P\)): For step \(t = 1, 2, \dots, n - 2\):

Among all leaves (vertices of current degree \(1\)) remaining in \(T\), select the leaf \(u_t\) with the smallest label.
Let \(p_t\) be the unique neighbor of \(u_t\) in the current tree.
Delete leaf \(u_t\) and the edge \((u_t, p_t)\) from \(T\) (which decrements the current degree of \(p_t\) by \(1\)). After \(n - 2\) steps, exactly \(2\) vertices remain (joined by a single edge, one of which is always the global maximum label \(n\)), and we stop.

The Fundamental Degree–Multiplicity Invariant: How many times does a vertex \(v \in \{1, 2, \dots, n\}\) appear in the Prüfer sequence \(P = (p_1, \dots, p_{n-2})\)?

Every time one of \(v\)’s incident edges is deleted because the other endpoint was a plucked leaf, \(v\) is recorded once in \(P\) and its remaining degree drops by \(1\).
When \(v\)’s remaining degree reaches \(1\), \(v\) is now a leaf itself; either \(v\) is eventually plucked as a leaf (deleting its last incident edge without recording \(v\) in \(P\)), or \(v\) is one of the final \(2\) surviving vertices at the end of step \(n - 2\) (whose last connecting edge is never deleted).
In both cases, out of the \(\deg_T(v)\) edges originally incident to \(v\), exactly \(\deg_T(v) - 1\) of them record \(v\) in \(P\)! Thus: \[\text{multiplicity of } v \text{ in } P = \deg_T(v) - 1 \quad \forall v \in \{1, 2, \dots, n\}\]

Decoding (\(P \mapsto T\)): Given any sequence \(P = (p_1, \dots, p_{n-2}) \in \{1, \dots, n\}^{n-2}\), we can reconstruct \(T\) uniquely:

Initialize the remaining vertex set \(R = \{1, 2, \dots, n\}\) and the remaining multiplicity \(c_v = \lvert \{t \mid p_t = v\} \rvert\) for each \(v \in R\).
At step \(t = 1\), a vertex \(u \in R\) was a leaf of \(T\) if and only if \(\deg_T(u) = 1 \iff c_u = 0\). Therefore, the plucked leaf \(u_1\) must be the smallest element of \(R\) with \(c_u = 0\)!
For \(t = 1, 2, \dots, n - 2\): find the smallest \(u_t \in R\) with \(c_{u_t} = 0\), add the edge \((u_t, p_t)\) to \(T\), remove \(u_t\) from \(R\), and decrement \(c_{p_t} \gets c_{p_t} - 1\).
Finally, connect the last two vertices remaining in \(R\) by an edge.



Hand-Checkable Trace (\(n = 4\))
For \(n = 4\), Prüfer sequences have length \(n - 2 = 2\) over alphabet \(\{1, 2, 3, 4\}\), giving \(4^{4-2} = 16\) labeled trees in total (Cayley’s Formula \(n^{n-2}\)):

Sequence \(P = (2, 2)\): Multiplicities are \((c_1, c_2, c_3, c_4) = (0, 2, 0, 0)\), so degrees are \(d_i = c_i + 1 = (1, 3, 1, 1)\). Decoding:

Step \(1\): leaves (\(c_v = 0\)) are \(\{1, 3, 4\}\); smallest is \(u_1 = 1\). Add edge \((1, 2)\), remove \(1\), decrement \(c_2 \gets 1\).
Step \(2\): leaves (\(c_v = 0\)) in \(R = \{2, 3, 4\}\) are \(\{3, 4\}\); smallest is \(u_2 = 3\). Add edge \((3, 2)\), remove \(3\), decrement \(c_2 \gets 0\).
Final step: connect remaining two vertices \(\{2, 4\}\) by edge \((2, 4)\). This is the star centered at vertex \(2\). Since there are \(4\) sequences of the form \((v, v)\), there are \(4\) star trees.

Sequences \((p_1, p_2)\) with \(p_1 \neq p_2\): There are \(4 \times 3 = 12\) such sequences. Each has two vertices appearing once (\(d_v = 2\)) and two vertices appearing zero times (\(d_v = 1\)), corresponding to the \(\frac{4!}{2} = 12\) labeled path trees on \(4\) vertices (\(12 + 4 = 16\)).





The Prüfer EGF Master Engine
Because Prüfer’s bijection identifies labeled trees \(T\) on \(\{1, \dots, n\}\) (for \(n \ge 2\)) with words of length \(n - 2\) over the alphabet \(\{1, \dots, n\}\) in which vertex \(i\) appears \(c_i = d_i - 1\) times, every degree-constrained tree counting problem translates immediately into a labeled word EGF product!

Exact Degree Sequence \((d_1, d_2, \dots, d_n)\): For \(n \ge 2\), the number of labeled trees on \(\{1, \dots, n\}\) with \(\deg_T(i) = d_i \ge 1\) (where \(\sum_{i=1}^n d_i = 2n - 2 \iff \sum_{i=1}^n (d_i - 1) = n - 2\)) is the multinomial coefficient: \[\text{Trees}(d_1, \dots, d_n) = \binom{n - 2}{d_1 - 1,\; d_2 - 1,\; \dots,\; d_n - 1} = \frac{(n - 2)!}{(d_1 - 1)!\,(d_2 - 1)!\,\cdots\,(d_n - 1)!}\]
General Degree-Weighted / Degree-Restricted Trees: Suppose vertex \(i\) is assigned a weight \(w_i(d)\) when its degree in \(T\) is \(d\) (for example, \(w_i(d) = [d \in S_i]\) if vertex \(i\)’s degree must belong to an allowed set \(S_i \subseteq \mathbb{Z}_{\ge 1}\), or \(w_i(d) = d^k\) if we are summing a degree statistic). Let \(c_i = d_i - 1 \ge 0\) be the Prüfer multiplicity of vertex \(i\). The EGF for vertex \(i\)’s occurrences in the Prüfer word is: \[\widehat{E}_i(x) = \sum_{d=1}^{\infty} w_i(d) \frac{x^{d-1}}{(d - 1)!} = \sum_{c=0}^{\infty} w_i(c + 1) \frac{x^c}{c!}\] Summing over all Prüfer words of length \(n - 2\) yields the Prüfer EGF Master Formula (for \(n \ge 2\)): \[\sum_{T} \prod_{i=1}^{n} w_i\bigl(\deg_T(i)\bigr) = (n - 2)! [x^{n-2}] \prod_{i=1}^{n} \widehat{E}_i(x) = (n - 2)! [x^{n-2}] \prod_{i=1}^{n} \left(\sum_{d=1}^{\infty} w_i(d) \frac{x^{d-1}}{(d - 1)!}\right)\]
Generalized Cayley Forest Formulas (\(k\) Rooted Components): What if instead of a single tree on \(n\) vertices, we count rooted forests on \(\{1, 2, \dots, n\}\) consisting of \(k\) rooted trees whose \(k\) roots are fixed at \(\{1, 2, \dots, k\}\) (or chosen arbitrarily)?

Fixed Roots \(\{1, \dots, k\}\): Add a virtual super-root \(0\) connected only to the \(k\) fixed roots \(\{1, \dots, k\}\). In the resulting tree on \(n + 1\) vertices \(\{0, 1, \dots, n\}\), the virtual root \(0\) has degree \(k\), so it appears \(k - 1\) times in the Prüfer sequence of length \((n + 1) - 2 = n - 1\), and its last plucked neighbor before \(\{0, n\}\) is fixed; equivalently, by EGF Lagrange Inversion on \(\widehat{T}(x)^k\) (Chapter 11), the number of forests on \(\{1, \dots, n\}\) rooted at \(k\) specified vertices is: \[F_{\text{fixed}}(n, k) = k \cdot n^{n - k - 1} \quad (1 \le k \le n, \text{ with } F_{\text{fixed}}(n, n) = 1)\]
Prescribed Component Sizes \(s_1, s_2, \dots, s_k\) (\(\sum s_i = n\)): If \(k\) existing trees have fixed vertex sets of sizes \(s_1, s_2, \dots, s_k\), contracting each component \(i\) into a super-vertex where an edge incident to component \(i\) can attach to any of its \(s_i\) vertices gives weight \(w_i(d) = s_i^d\) for degree \(d\). Factoring out \(s_i\) from \(\sum_{d \ge 1} s_i^d \frac{x^{d-1}}{(d-1)!} = s_i \sum_{c \ge 0} \frac{(s_i x)^c}{c!} = s_i e^{s_i x}\) and combining the exponentials via \(\sum_{i=1}^k s_i = n\) yields: \[\begin{aligned}
(k - 2)! [x^{k-2}] \prod_{i=1}^{k} \left(\sum_{d=1}^{\infty} s_i^d \frac{x^{d-1}}{(d-1)!}\right) &= (k - 2)! [x^{k-2}] \prod_{i=1}^{k} \bigl(s_i e^{s_i x}\bigr) \\
&= \left(\prod_{i=1}^{k} s_i\right) (k - 2)! [x^{k-2}] \exp\!\left(\sum_{i=1}^{k} s_i x\right) \\
&= \left(\prod_{i=1}^{k} s_i\right) (k - 2)! [x^{k-2}] e^{n x} \\
&= \left(\prod_{i=1}^{k} s_i\right) n^{k-2}
\end{aligned}\]









WarningCanonical Failure Mode #16: The Prüfer \(N = 1\) Boundary Trap




The Failure Mode: You derive the Prüfer EGF formula \(\text{Ans} = (N - 2)! [x^{N-2}] \prod_{i=1}^N \widehat{E}_i(x)\) for a degree-constrained tree problem (such as AtCoder ABC 303 Ex or Luogu P2290), implement it cleanly with \(O(N \log N)\) polynomial operations, and get Wrong Answer (WA) or Runtime Error (RE) on a single test case: \(N = 1\)!
Why \(N = 1\) Breaks Both Halves of Prüfer’s Theorem:

Length Underflow (\(N - 2 = -1 < 0\)): A Prüfer sequence has length \(N - 2\), which only exists for \(N \ge 2\). Indexing \([x^{N-2}]\) or computing \((N - 2)!\) at \(N = 1\) accesses index \(-1\)!
The Degree-\(0\) Exception (\(\deg_T(1) = 0\)): For every tree with \(N \ge 2\) vertices, every vertex has at least one incident edge (\(\deg_T(v) \ge 1\)). For \(N = 1\), the unique tree on \(\{1\}\) has \(0\) edges, so vertex \(1\) has degree \(0\) (\(\deg_T(1) = 0\))!

In a problem where vertex degrees are restricted to a subset \(S \subseteq \{1, 2, \dots, N-1\}\) of positive integers (e.g., ABC 303 Ex), \(0 \notin S\), so for \(N = 1\) there are \(0\) valid trees if \(0 \notin S\), or \(1\) valid tree if degree \(0\) is permitted (or if the problem specifies \(N \ge 2\)).
In a problem where exact degrees \((d_1, \dots, d_N)\) are given as input (Luogu P2290), at \(N = 1\) the answer is \(1\) if and only if \(d_1 = 0\), and \(0\) if \(d_1 \ge 1\)! (If you only check \(\sum d_i = 2N - 2 = 0\) and \(d_i \ge 1\), you will falsely output \(0\) for \(N = 1, d_1 = 0\), or crash on \(N = 1, d_1 = 1\).)


The Mandatory Guard Checklist: Always place an explicit boundary guard at the very top of any Prüfer-based solver before touching factorials or polynomials:

Case \(N = 1\): The unique tree has \(\deg_T(1) = 0\). Return \(w_1(0)\) (i.e., \(1\) if \(d_1 = 0\) is valid, else \(0\)).
Case \(N = 2\): The unique tree is a single edge \((1, 2)\) with \(\deg_T(1) = \deg_T(2) = 1\), corresponding to the empty Prüfer word of length \(N - 2 = 0\). The formula \(0! [x^0] \prod_{i=1}^2 \widehat{E}_i(x) = w_1(1) w_2(1)\) works correctly for \(N = 2\) as long as degree \(0\) of the polynomials is allocated.










NoteAlgorithm Contract 4.2: Prüfer Sequence Degree-Distribution Engine




Input: Number of labeled vertices \(N \ge 1\), degree weight functions \(w_i: \{0, 1, \dots, N-1\} \to \mathbb{F}_p\) for \(1 \le i \le N\), prime modulus \(p > N\).
Preconditions: \(p > N\) so factorials up to \((N-2)!\) are units in \(\mathbb{F}_p\).
Output: Total weight \(\sum_{T \text{ on } [N]} \prod_{i=1}^N w_i(\deg_T(i)) \pmod p\).
Algorithm Steps:

Guard \(N = 1\): Return \(w_1(0) \bmod p\).
For each vertex \(i = 1, \dots, N\), define the polynomial \(E_i(x) = \sum_{c=0}^{N-2} w_i(c + 1) \frac{x^c}{c!} \in \mathbb{F}_p[x]/(x^{N-1})\).
Compute \(P(x) \equiv \prod_{i=1}^N E_i(x) \pmod{x^{N-1}}\):

If all \(E_i(x) = E(x)\) are identical, compute \(P(x) \equiv E(x)^N \pmod{x^{N-1}}\) via poly_pow in \(O(N \log N)\) time (factoring out \(x^v\) where \(v = \operatorname{val}(E)\) first if \(E(0) = 0\)).
If \(E_i(x)\) vary across vertices with \(\sum \deg E_i = O(N)\), multiply via a Divide-and-Conquer product tree in \(O(N \log^2 N)\) time.

Return \((N - 2)! [x^{N-2}] P(x) \bmod p\).

Complexity: \(O(N \log N)\) time for identical degree constraints; \(O(N \log^2 N)\) time for heterogeneous degree bounds with \(\sum D_i = O(N)\).
Correctness Invariant: For \(N \ge 2\), Prüfer’s bijection maps the set of trees on \([N]\) bijectively onto \([N]^{N-2}\) such that \(\deg_T(i) = c_i + 1\), where \(c_i\) is the number of occurrences of \(i\) in the Prüfer word.

title: Chapter 04: The Labeled Symbolic Method: Exponential Generating Functions (EGFs), Boxed Products & Prüfer Sequences
text:
4.5 The 8-Problem 4-Tier Practice Ladder
Every problem below is drawn from the canonical textbook curriculum for Chapter 04 and is completely self-contained. Work through the Diagnostic Signal and Progressive Hints before opening the complete derivation.


Stepping Stone 1 (#002) — AtCoder fps_24_e: Sequence 2 (Bounded Multiset Permutations)

Source: AtCoder — fps_24_e (Sequence 2)
Prerequisite Tags: Labeled EGF Product (\(\mathcal{A} \star \mathcal{B}\)), Bounded Exponential Factors \(\sum_{j=0}^m \frac{x^j}{j!}\), Divide-and-Conquer / DP Convolution.


Problem Statement & Exact Constraints
Find the number, modulo \(998244353\), of integer sequences \(A = (A_1, A_2, \dots, A_N)\) of length \(N\) satisfying both of the following conditions:

\(1 \le A_i \le M\) for all \(1 \le i \le N\).
For every integer \(m \in \{1, 2, \dots, M\}\), the value \(m\) appears at most \(m\) times in the sequence \(A\).


Constraints: \(1 \le N, M \le 500\) (or up to \(N \le 2.5 \times 10^5\) in the large-scale D&C NTT regime), modulus \(998244353\), time limit \(2.0\text{ s}\).
Required Complexity: \(O(N \min(M, N)^2)\) or \(O(N \log^2 N)\) time, \(O(N)\) space.
Sample Trace (\(N = 3, M = 2\)): Valid sequences over \(\{1, 2\}\) of length \(3\) where \(1\) appears \(\le 1\) time and \(2\) appears \(\le 2\) times must use one \(1\) and two \(2\)’s: \((1,2,2), (2,1,2), (2,2,1)\), giving \(3! [x^3] (1 + x)\bigl(1 + x + \frac{x^2}{2}\bigr) = 3\).



Hint 1 — Diagnostic Signal & Combinatorial Model

In the sequence \(A = (A_1, \dots, A_N)\), the \(N\) positions \(\{1, 2, \dots, N\}\) are distinguishable. If value \(m\) is chosen to appear \(c_m\) times (\(0 \le c_m \le m\)) with \(c_1 + c_2 + \dots + c_M = N\), how many sequences \(A\) have this exact frequency profile \((c_1, \dots, c_M)\)? The multinomial coefficient \(\binom{N}{c_1, c_2, \dots, c_M} = \frac{N!}{c_1! c_2! \cdots c_M!}\)! What generating function family automatically produces \(\frac{N!}{c_1! \cdots c_M!}\) when multiplied?



Hint 2 — Algebraic Setup & Reverse-Engineering Scratchpad

Because the multinomial weight is \(\frac{N!}{c_1! \cdots c_M!}\), each value \(m \in \{1, 2, \dots, M\}\) contributes an independent truncated exponential generating function: \[\widehat{E}_m(x) = \sum_{j=0}^{m} \frac{x^j}{j!}\] The total number of valid sequences of length \(N\) is then \(N! [x^N] \prod_{m=1}^{M} \widehat{E}_m(x)\).



Hint 3 — Coefficient Extraction & Complexity Contract

Truncate all polynomial products modulo \(x^{N+1}\).

For \(N, M \le 500\): Maintain the coefficient array of \(\prod_{m=1}^k \widehat{E}_m(x) \bmod x^{N+1}\) and multiply by \(\widehat{E}_m(x)\) in \(O(N \cdot \min(m, N))\) time, taking \(O(M N^2)\) total operations (\(\le 1.25 \times 10^8\) ops, or \(O(M N \log N)\) with NTT).
If \(M\) and \(N\) are up to \(10^5\): Notice that \(\widehat{E}_m(x) \equiv e^x \pmod{x^{N+1}}\) for all \(m \ge N\), and for the remaining \(m < N\) you can either multiply the polynomials or group identical factors. Finally, multiply \([x^N]\) by \(N! \bmod 998244353\).








NoteComplete Derivation & Solution






1. Combinatorial-to-EGF Translation
A sequence \(A = (A_1, \dots, A_N) \in \{1, \dots, M\}^N\) is uniquely determined by partitioning the set of \(N\) position indices \(\{1, 2, \dots, N\}\) into \(M\) labeled subsets \((U_1, U_2, \dots, U_M)\), where \(U_m = \{i \in [N] \mid A_i = m\}\) is the set of positions holding value \(m\).
Condition 2 requires \(\lvert U_m \rvert = c_m \in \{0, 1, \dots, m\}\) for each \(m = 1, \dots, M\). For a fixed tuple of sizes \((c_1, \dots, c_M)\) summing to \(N\), the number of ways to partition \([N]\) into \((U_1, \dots, U_M)\) is \(\frac{N!}{c_1! c_2! \cdots c_M!}\). Summing over all valid tuples \((c_1, \dots, c_M)\): \[\begin{aligned}
\text{Ans} &= \sum_{\substack{c_1 + \dots + c_M = N \\ 0 \le c_m \le m}} \frac{N!}{c_1! c_2! \cdots c_M!} \\
&= N! [x^N] \prod_{m=1}^{M} \left( \sum_{c_m=0}^{m} \frac{x^{c_m}}{c_m!} \right)
\end{aligned}\]


2. Small Hand-Checkable Trace (\(N = 3, M = 2\))
For \(N = 3, M = 2\):

\(\widehat{E}_1(x) = 1 + x\)
\(\widehat{E}_2(x) = 1 + x + \frac{x^2}{2}\) Multiplying \(\widehat{E}_1(x) \widehat{E}_2(x) = (1 + x)\left(1 + x + \frac{x^2}{2}\right) = 1 + 2x + \frac{3}{2}x^2 + \frac{1}{2}x^3\). Extracting \(3! [x^3] = 6 \times \frac{1}{2} = 3\). Indeed, a sequence of length \(3\) over \(\{1, 2\}\) with at most one \(1\) and at most two \(2\)’s must have \(c_1 = 1\) and \(c_2 = 2\), giving the \(\binom{3}{1, 2} = 3\) permutations of \((1, 2, 2)\).



3. Algorithm Contract

Input & Preconditions: Integers \(N, M \ge 1\); prime modulus \(p = 998244353 > N\) so \(0!, 1!, \dots, N! \in \mathbb{F}_p^\times\).
Postconditions (Output): Returns \(N! [x^N] \prod_{m=1}^M \left(\sum_{j=0}^m \frac{x^j}{j!}\right) \bmod p\).
Time & Space Complexity: \(O(N \min(M, N)^2)\) time via bounded-degree polynomial multiplication (or \(O(\min(M, N) N \log N)\) via NTT) and \(O(N)\) auxiliary space.
Loop / Algebraic Invariant: After processing symbol \(m \in \{1, \dots, K\}\) (with all \(M - K\) unconstrained symbols \(m \ge N\) absorbed into \(e^{(M-K)x} \bmod x^{N+1}\)), \(k! [x^k] P(x)\) equals the number of valid sequences of length \(k \le N\) over \(\{1, \dots, m\} \cup \{K+1, \dots, M\}\).
Failure Modes & Edge Cases:

Total Capacity Shortage (\(\frac{M(M+1)}{2} < N\)): When \(M(M+1)/2 < N\), \(\deg \prod_{m=1}^M \widehat{E}_m(x) < N\), so \([x^N] P(x) = 0\).
Large \(M \ge N\): Any factor with \(m \ge N\) agrees with \(e^x\) modulo \(x^{N+1}\); grouping all \(M - K\) such factors into \(e^{(M-K)x}\) avoids \(O(M)\) redundant degree-\(N\) multiplications.

Algorithm Steps:

Precompute factorials \(j!\) and inverse factorials \((j!)^{-1} \bmod p\) for \(0 \le j \le N\) in \(O(N)\) time.
Set \(K = \min(M, N - 1)\). Since \(\widehat{E}_m(x) \equiv e^x \pmod{x^{N+1}}\) for all \(m \ge N\), combine all \(M - K\) unconstrained symbols into a single initial polynomial: \[P(x) \equiv e^{(M - K)x} \equiv \sum_{j=0}^{N} \frac{(M - K)^j}{j!} x^j \pmod{x^{N+1}}\]
For \(m = 1, 2, \dots, K\), update \(P(x) \gets P(x) \cdot \left(\sum_{j=0}^m \frac{x^j}{j!}\right) \pmod{x^{N+1}}\).
Return \(N! [x^N] P(x) \bmod p\).










Stepping Stone 2 (#007) — AtCoder fps_24_m: Value of Permutation (Cycle-Weight EGF Decomposition)

Source: AtCoder — fps_24_m (Value of Permutation / Cycle Decomposition)
Prerequisite Tags: Permutation Cycle Decomposition \(\mathcal{P} = \operatorname{SET}(\operatorname{CYC}(\mathcal{Z}))\), Weighted Cycle EGF \(\widehat{W}(x) = \sum_{k=1}^N \frac{w_k}{k} x^k\), Catalytic Variable Differentiation.


Problem Statement & Exact Constraints
Given an integer \(N\) and a cycle-length weight sequence \((w_1, w_2, \dots, w_N)\), every permutation \(\pi \in S_N\) of \(\{1, 2, \dots, N\}\) decomposes uniquely into a set of disjoint directed cycles \(\{C_1, C_2, \dots, C_r\}\). Find, modulo \(998244353\), the sum over all \(N!\) permutations \(\pi \in S_N\) of the multiplicative cycle weight: \[V(\pi) = \prod_{j=1}^{r} w_{\lvert C_j \rvert}\]

Constraints: \(1 \le N \le 2.5 \times 10^5\), \(0 \le w_k < 998244353\), modulus \(998244353\), time limit \(2.0\text{ s}\).
Required Complexity: \(O(N \log N)\) time and \(O(N)\) space (and \(O(N)\) time for the companion additive cycle-weight variant derived in the solution).
Sample Trace (\(N = 3\)): The \(6\) permutations in \(S_3\) consist of \(1\) identity (three \(1\)-cycles, weight \(w_1^3\)), \(3\) transpositions (one \(1\)-cycle and one \(2\)-cycle, weight \(3 w_1 w_2\)), and \(2\) three-cycles (weight \(2 w_3\)), totaling \(w_1^3 + 3 w_1 w_2 + 2 w_3 = 3! [x^3] \exp\bigl(w_1 x + \frac{w_2}{2}x^2 + \frac{w_3}{3}x^3\bigr)\).



Hint 1 — Diagnostic Signal & Combinatorial Model

Every permutation \(\pi \in S_N\) is uniquely an unordered \(\operatorname{SET}\) of directed cycles (\(\operatorname{CYC}\)). On a label subset of size \(k\), how many distinct directed cycles exist? There are \((k - 1)!\) directed cycles! When each cycle of length \(k\) carries weight \(w_k\), what is the EGF of a single weighted directed cycle?



Hint 2 — Algebraic Setup & Reverse-Engineering Scratchpad

Because there are \((k - 1)!\) directed cycles on \(k\) labeled elements, a single cycle of length \(k\) weighted by \(w_k\) has EGF term: \[w_k (k - 1)! \frac{x^k}{k!} = \frac{w_k}{k} x^k \quad \Longrightarrow \quad \widehat{W}(x) = \sum_{k=1}^{N} \frac{w_k}{k} x^k\]

For the multiplicative weight \(\prod_{j=1}^r w_{\lvert C_j \rvert}\), the \(\operatorname{SET}\) construction multiplies the weights of the constituent cycles, so the EGF is \(\exp\bigl(\widehat{W}(x)\bigr)\).
What if a companion problem asks for the additive weight \(\sum_{j=1}^r w_{\lvert C_j \rvert}\)? Then a permutation with one distinguished weighted cycle consists of one chosen cycle from \(\widehat{W}(x)\) paired with an arbitrary permutation on the remaining elements (counted by \(\exp(\ln\frac{1}{1-x}) = \frac{1}{1 - x}\))!




Hint 3 — Coefficient Extraction & Complexity Contract


Multiplicative: Call poly_exp on \(\widehat{W}(x) \bmod x^{N+1}\) in \(O(N \log N)\) time and return \(N! [x^N] \exp\bigl(\widehat{W}(x)\bigr) \bmod 998244353\).
Additive Companion: The EGF is \(\widehat{W}(x) \cdot \frac{1}{1 - x}\), so extracting \(N! [x^N] \frac{\widehat{W}(x)}{1 - x}\) gives \(N! \sum_{k=1}^N \frac{w_k}{k}\) in \(O(N)\) linear time!








NoteComplete Derivation & Solution






1. Weighted Cycle EGF & Bivariate Catalytic Generating Function
Let \(\mathcal{C}\) be the class of directed cycles. Since \(k\) labeled elements form \((k - 1)!\) directed cycles, the unweighted cycle EGF is \(\widehat{C}(x) = \sum_{k=1}^\infty (k - 1)! \frac{x^k}{k!} = \sum_{k=1}^\infty \frac{x^k}{k} = \ln\frac{1}{1 - x}\), and the weighted cycle EGF is: \[\widehat{W}(x) = \sum_{k=1}^{\infty} w_k (k - 1)! \frac{x^k}{k!} = \sum_{k=1}^{\infty} \frac{w_k}{k} x^k\]

Multiplicative Cycle Weight \(V_{\text{mul}}(\pi) = \prod_{j=1}^r w_{\lvert C_j \rvert}\): Under \(\mathcal{P} = \operatorname{SET}(\mathcal{C})\), the weight of a set of cycles \(\{C_1, \dots, C_r\}\) is the product of the individual cycle weights. By the Exponential Formula: \[\sum_{\pi \in S_N} \prod_{j=1}^{r} w_{\lvert C_j \rvert} = N! [x^N] \exp\bigl(\widehat{W}(x)\bigr) = N! [x^N] \exp\!\left(\sum_{k=1}^{N} \frac{w_k}{k} x^k\right)\]
Companion Variant — Additive Cycle Weight \(V_{\text{add}}(\pi) = \sum_{j=1}^r w_{\lvert C_j \rvert}\): Introduce a catalytic variable \(y\) where a cycle of length \(k\) carries weight \(e^{y w_k}\) (or \(1 + (y - 1)w_k\)). The bivariate EGF over all permutations is: \[\widehat{F}(x, y) = \exp\!\left(\sum_{k=1}^{\infty} \bigl(1 + (y - 1) w_k\bigr) \frac{x^k}{k}\right) = \exp\Bigl(\ln\frac{1}{1 - x} + (y - 1)\widehat{W}(x)\Bigr) = \frac{\exp\bigl((y - 1)\widehat{W}(x)\bigr)}{1 - x}\] Differentiating with respect to \(y\) and setting \(y = 1\) isolates the sum of cycle weights across all cycles of \(\pi\): \[\left.\frac{\partial \widehat{F}(x, y)}{\partial y}\right|_{y=1} = \frac{\widehat{W}(x)}{1 - x} = \left(\sum_{k=1}^{\infty} \frac{w_k}{k} x^k\right) \left(\sum_{m=0}^{\infty} x^m\right)\] Extracting \(N! [x^N]\) yields the exact \(O(N)\) closed form: \[\sum_{\pi \in S_N} \sum_{j=1}^{r} w_{\lvert C_j \rvert} = N! [x^N] \frac{\widehat{W}(x)}{1 - x} = N! \sum_{k=1}^{N} \frac{w_k}{k}\]



2. Small Hand-Checkable Trace (\(N = 3\))
The \(3! = 6\) permutations in \(S_3\) decompose into cycles as follows:

\(1\) identity permutation \((1)(2)(3)\): three \(1\)-cycles (multiplicative weight \(w_1^3\), additive weight \(3 w_1\)).
\(3\) transpositions \((12)(3), (13)(2), (23)(1)\): one \(1\)-cycle and one \(2\)-cycle each (multiplicative weight \(3 w_1 w_2\), additive weight \(3(w_1 + w_2)\)).
\(2\) three-cycles \((123), (132)\): one \(3\)-cycle each (multiplicative weight \(2 w_3\), additive weight \(2 w_3\)). Total multiplicative weight: \(w_1^3 + 3 w_1 w_2 + 2 w_3 = 3! [x^3] \exp\left(w_1 x + \frac{w_2}{2}x^2 + \frac{w_3}{3}x^3\right)\). Total additive weight: \(6 w_1 + 3 w_2 + 2 w_3 = 3! \left(\frac{w_1}{1} + \frac{w_2}{2} + \frac{w_3}{3}\right)\). Both match our formulas identically!



3. Algorithm Contract

Input & Preconditions: Integer \(N \ge 1\), cycle weights \(w_1, \dots, w_N \in \mathbb{F}_p\); prime modulus \(p = 998244353 > N\) so \(1, 2, \dots, N \in \mathbb{F}_p^\times\) and \([x^0]\widehat{W}(x) = 0\).
Postconditions (Output): Outputs \(\sum_{\pi \in S_N} V_{\text{mul}}(\pi) \bmod p\) (and \(\sum_{\pi \in S_N} V_{\text{add}}(\pi) \bmod p\) for the additive companion).
Time & Space Complexity: \(O(N \log N)\) time for multiplicative cycle weights (\(O(N)\) time for additive weights) and \(O(N)\) auxiliary space.
Loop / Algebraic Invariant: Because \(\mathcal{P} = \operatorname{SET}(\mathcal{C})\), for every \(0 \le n \le N\), \(n! [x^n] \exp(\widehat{W}(x))\) equals \(\sum_{\pi \in S_n} \prod_{C \in \pi} w_{\lvert C \rvert}\) and \(n! [x^n] \frac{\widehat{W}(x)}{1-x}\) equals \(\sum_{\pi \in S_n} \sum_{C \in \pi} w_{\lvert C \rvert}\).
Failure Modes & Edge Cases:

Missing \(1/k\) Cycle Symmetry Factor: A directed cycle on \(k\) labeled vertices has \((k-1)!\) orientations, so its EGF coefficient is \(\frac{w_k (k-1)!}{k!} = \frac{w_k}{k}\), not \(\frac{w_k}{k!}\).
Zero Constant Term Requirement for \(\exp\): \(\widehat{W}(0) = 0\) must hold before invoking poly_exp.

Algorithm Steps:

Precompute modular inverses \(k^{-1} \bmod p\) for \(1 \le k \le N\) and \(N! \bmod p\) in \(O(N)\) time.
Form \(\widehat{W}(x) = \sum_{k=1}^N (w_k \cdot k^{-1} \bmod p) x^k\).
Multiplicative Output: Compute \(E(x) \equiv \exp\bigl(\widehat{W}(x)\bigr) \pmod{x^{N+1}}\) via poly_exp in \(O(N \log N)\) time and output \(N! [x^N] E(x) \bmod p\).
Additive Companion Output: Compute \(N! \left(\sum_{k=1}^N w_k k^{-1}\right) \bmod p\) in \(O(N)\) time.










Intermediate 1 (#161) — Luogu P4841: [集训队作业2013] 城市规划 (Urban Planning)

Source: Luogu P4841 — [集训队作业2013] 城市规划
Prerequisite Tags: Connected Labeled Graphs \(\widehat{C}(x) = \ln \widehat{G}(x)\), Boxed Product ODE \(\widehat{G}'(x) = \widehat{C}'(x)\widehat{G}(x)\), Non-Standard NTT Prime \(p = 1004535809\).


Problem Statement & Exact Constraints
A country consists of \(n\) labeled cities \(\{1, 2, \dots, n\}\). Between any pair of distinct cities, an undirected road may or may not be built. Count the number of road networks (simple undirected graphs on \(n\) labeled vertices) such that all \(n\) cities form a single connected component, modulo \(1004535809\).

Constraints: \(1 \le n \le 1.3 \times 10^5\), prime modulus \(p = 1004535809 = 479 \times 2^{21} + 1\) (primitive root \(g = 3\)), time limit \(1.0\text{ s}\).
Required Complexity: \(O(n \log n)\) time and \(O(n)\) space.
Sample Trace (\(n = 3\)): Of the \(2^{\binom{3}{2}} = 8\) simple labeled graphs on \(\{1, 2, 3\}\), the \(4\) connected graphs are the \(3\) spanning paths (\(3\) labeled trees) plus \(1\) triangle \(K_3\), matching \(3! [x^3] \ln\bigl(1 + x + x^2 + \frac{4}{3}x^3\bigr) = 4\).



Hint 1 — Diagnostic Signal & Combinatorial Model

Notice that the modulus \(p = 1004535809 = 479 \times 2^{21} + 1\) is an NTT-friendly prime with \(2^{21} > 2.6 \times 10^5\) and primitive root \(g = 3\). We want to extract \(c_n = n! [x^n] \widehat{C}(x)\) where \(\widehat{G}(x) = \exp\bigl(\widehat{C}(x)\bigr)\) and \(g_k = 2^{\binom{k}{2}}\).



Hint 2 — Algebraic Setup & Reverse-Engineering Scratchpad

Compare the two equivalent algebraic formulations for \(\widehat{C}(x)\):

Direct Logarithm: \(\widehat{C}(x) = \ln \widehat{G}(x) = \int_0^x \widehat{G}'(t)\widehat{G}(t)^{-1}\,dt \pmod{x^{n+1}}\).
Boxed Product / Minimum-Label Pivot: Isolate the connected component of size \(k\) containing city \(1\): \[g_m = \sum_{k=1}^{m} \binom{m-1}{k-1} c_k g_{m-k} \iff \frac{g_m}{(m-1)!} = \sum_{k=1}^{m} \left(\frac{c_k}{(k-1)!}\right) \left(\frac{g_{m-k}}{(m-k)!}\right)\] Notice that \(\sum_{m \ge 1} \frac{g_m}{(m-1)!} x^{m-1} = \widehat{G}'(x)\) and \(\sum_{k \ge 1} \frac{c_k}{(k-1)!} x^{k-1} = \widehat{C}'(x)\), so solving \(\widehat{C}'(x) = \widehat{G}'(x)\widehat{G}(x)^{-1} \pmod{x^n}\) is the exact same polynomial inversion + multiplication!




Hint 3 — Coefficient Extraction & Complexity Contract

Watch out for integer overflow when computing \(\binom{k}{2} = \frac{k(k-1)}{2}\) for \(k = 1.3 \times 10^5\): \(\binom{k}{2} \approx 8.45 \times 10^9 > 2^{31}-1\). By Fermat’s Little Theorem, \(2^{\binom{k}{2}} \equiv 2^{\binom{k}{2} \bmod (p - 1)} \pmod p\)—reduce the exponent modulo \(p - 1 = 1004535808\) (not modulo \(p\)!).







NoteComplete Derivation & Solution






1. Derivation via the Boxed Product & EGF Logarithm
Let \(g_k = 2^{\binom{k}{2}}\) be the total number of simple undirected graphs on \(k\) labeled cities, and let \(c_k\) be the number of connected simple undirected graphs on \(k\) labeled cities.
In any graph on \(m \ge 1\) labeled cities, consider the connected component containing city \(1\). If this component has size \(k \in \{1, 2, \dots, m\}\):

There are \(\binom{m-1}{k-1}\) ways to choose the remaining \(k - 1\) cities in city \(1\)’s connected component from \(\{2, 3, \dots, m\}\).
There are \(c_k\) ways to form a connected graph on those \(k\) cities.
There are \(g_{m-k}\) ways to form an arbitrary simple graph on the remaining \(m - k\) cities (with no edges between the two parts).

Summing over \(k = 1, \dots, m\) yields the Boxed Product identity: \[g_m = \sum_{k=1}^{m} \binom{m-1}{k-1} c_k g_{m-k} \quad (m \ge 1)\] Dividing both sides by \((m - 1)!\): \[\frac{g_m}{(m - 1)!} = \sum_{k=1}^{m} \left(\frac{c_k}{(k - 1)!}\right) \left(\frac{g_{m-k}}{(m - k)!}\right)\] Define the formal power series: \[\widehat{G}(x) = \sum_{j=0}^{\infty} \frac{g_j}{j!} x^j, \qquad \widehat{G}'(x) = \sum_{m=1}^{\infty} \frac{g_m}{(m - 1)!} x^{m-1}, \qquad \widehat{C}'(x) = \sum_{k=1}^{\infty} \frac{c_k}{(k - 1)!} x^{k-1}\] Then the recurrence is equivalent to \(\widehat{G}'(x) = \widehat{C}'(x) \widehat{G}(x)\) in \(\mathbb{F}_p[[x]]\). Since \([x^0]\widehat{G}(x) = g_0 = 1 \in \mathbb{F}_p^\times\), \(\widehat{G}(x)\) is invertible in \(\mathbb{F}_p[[x]]\), and: \[\widehat{C}'(x) \equiv \widehat{G}'(x) \widehat{G}(x)^{-1} \pmod{x^n}\] Extracting \([x^{n-1}]\widehat{C}'(x) = \frac{c_n}{(n - 1)!}\) and multiplying by \((n - 1)!\) directly yields \(c_n\) without even needing the final integration step!


2. Algorithm Contract

Input & Preconditions: Integer \(1 \le n \le 1.3 \times 10^5\), prime modulus \(p = 1004535809 = 479 \times 2^{21} + 1 > n\) with primitive root \(g = 3\), and \([x^0]\widehat{G}(x) = 1\).
Postconditions (Output): Returns \(c_n = n! [x^n] \ln \widehat{G}(x) \bmod p\).
Time & Space Complexity: \(O(n \log n)\) time and \(O(n)\) auxiliary space.
Loop / Algebraic Invariant: At each Newton doubling step \(L = 2^s\) of poly_inv, \(A_L(x) \cdot \widehat{G}(x) \equiv 1 \pmod{x^L}\), so \(\widehat{C}'(x) \equiv \widehat{G}'(x) A_n(x) \pmod{x^n}\) satisfies \((m-1)! [x^{m-1}] \widehat{C}'(x) \equiv c_m \pmod p\) for all \(1 \le m \le n\).
Failure Modes & Edge Cases:

Exponent Overflow in \(\binom{k}{2}\): For \(k = 1.3 \times 10^5\), \(\binom{k}{2} > 2^{31}-1\) overflows 32-bit signed integers; compute 1LL * k * (k - 1) / 2 % (p - 1) before modular exponentiation (reducing modulo \(p - 1\), not \(p\)).
Non-Standard NTT Prime: Must configure NTT with \(p = 1004535809\) (not \(998244353\)), primitive root \(g = 3\).

Algorithm Steps:

Configure NTT with prime \(p = 1004535809\) and primitive root \(g = 3\).
Precompute factorials, inverse factorials, and \(g_k = 2^{\binom{k}{2} \bmod (p - 1)} \bmod p\) for \(0 \le k \le n\).
Construct polynomial \(A(x) = \sum_{j=0}^{n-1} \frac{g_j}{j!} x^j \bmod x^n\) and \(B(x) = \sum_{m=1}^{n} \frac{g_m}{(m-1)!} x^{m-1} \bmod x^n\).
Compute \(A^{-1}(x) \equiv A(x)^{-1} \pmod{x^n}\) via Newton polynomial inversion in \(O(n \log n)\) time.
Output \(c_n = (n - 1)! [x^{n-1}]\bigl(B(x) A^{-1}(x)\bigr) = (n - 1)! \sum_{k=1}^n \frac{g_k}{(k-1)!} [x^{n-k}]A^{-1}(x) \bmod p\).
