text:
12.3 Tutte’s Block-Cut Tree Equation (\(\ln \frac{R(x)}{x} = B'(R(x))\)) & Biconnected (2-Vertex-Connected) Graphs

Concrete Combinatorial Objects: Blocks, Cut-Vertices, and the Block-Cut Tree
Let \(G\) be a connected simple undirected graph on \(n \ge 2\) labeled vertices. A vertex \(v \in V(G)\) is an articulation point (or cut-vertex) if deleting \(v\) and its incident edges disconnects \(G\). A connected graph on \(n \ge 2\) vertices with no articulation points is called biconnected (or 2-vertex-connected; by standard convention in Tutte’s block theory, \(K_2\) is the unique biconnected block on \(2\) vertices, so \(b_2 = 1\), while for \(n \ge 3\) biconnected means every pair of vertices is joined by two internally vertex-disjoint paths).
A maximal biconnected subgraph of \(G\) is called a block. The fundamental structural theorem of 2-vertex-connectivity states that:

Every edge of \(G\) belongs to exactly one block (blocks partition the edge set \(E(G)\)).
Two blocks can share at most one vertex, which must be a cut-vertex of \(G\).
The bipartite incidence graph between the set of blocks \(\mathcal{B}(G)\) and the set of vertices \(V(G)\) is a tree—the block-cut tree of \(G\).

Let:

\(G(x) = \sum_{n=0}^{\infty} 2^{\binom{n}{2}} \frac{x^n}{n!}\) be the EGF of all simple labeled graphs;
\(C(x) = \ln G(x) = \sum_{n=1}^{\infty} c_n \frac{x^n}{n!}\) be the EGF of connected simple labeled graphs;
\(R(x) = \Theta C(x) = x C'(x) = \sum_{n=1}^{\infty} n c_n \frac{x^n}{n!}\) be the EGF of vertex-pointed connected graphs;
\(B(u) = \sum_{k=2}^{\infty} b_k \frac{u^k}{k!}\) be the EGF of biconnected labeled graphs (blocks).

Our goal is to express \(R(x)\) in terms of \(B(u)\) and then invert the relation to extract \(b_n = n! [u^n] B(u)\).


Diagnostic Signal & Reverse-Engineering Scratchpad

The Diagnostic Signal
We already know the connected graph EGF \(C(x) = \ln G(x)\) and its pointed version \(R(x) = x C'(x)\) in \(O(N \log N)\) time (Ch 04.3). Whenever we know the global connected EGF \(R(x)\) and want the local 2-vertex-connected block EGF \(B(u)\), we write the forward assembly \(R(x) = \dots\) via the block-cut tree and invert it using Ch 11 Lagrange Inversion!


The Reverse-Engineering Scratchpad
Let us trace what happens around the root vertex \(r\) in a vertex-pointed connected graph \((G, r)\) of EGF \(R(x)\):

Step 1 (Isolating the blocks incident to the root \(r\)): In the block-cut tree of \((G, r)\), the root vertex \(r\) is adjacent to an unordered set (\(\operatorname{SET} = \exp\)) of blocks \(H_1, H_2, \dots, H_m\) that contain \(r\). Because the block-cut graph is a tree, deleting \(r\) disconnects \(G\) into \(m\) completely separate pieces—one for each block \(H_i\) incident to \(r\).
Step 2 (Inside a single block \(H_i\) of size \(k \ge 2\) incident to \(r\)): Suppose block \(H_i\) has \(k\) vertices in total: the root \(r\) plus \(k - 1\) other vertices \(v_1, \dots, v_{k-1}\). How many ways can we form a biconnected block on \(\{r, v_1, \dots, v_{k-1}\}\) when \(r\) is already externally fixed? By definition, there are \(b_k\) biconnected graphs on \(k\) labeled vertices. Since \(r\) is fixed and the remaining \(k - 1\) vertices of the block carry labels, the EGF for choosing the block structure on the \(k - 1\) non-root vertices is: \[\sum_{k=2}^{\infty} b_k \frac{u^{k-1}}{(k-1)!} = \frac{d}{du} \left(\sum_{k=2}^{\infty} b_k \frac{u^k}{k!}\right) = B'(u).\]
Step 3 (Substituting pointed connected subgraphs at the \(k - 1\) non-root block vertices): In the full connected graph \((G, r)\), each of the \(k - 1\) non-root vertices \(v_j\) of block \(H_i\) is not just a bare vertex—it is the root of the entire connected sub-component of \(G\) hanging off \(H_i\) at \(v_j\) in the block-cut tree! That sub-component is an arbitrary vertex-pointed connected graph with EGF \(u = R(x)\). Therefore, a single block incident to \(r\) together with all the subgraphs hanging off its non-root vertices has EGF: \[B'\big(R(x)\big).\]
Step 4 (Taking the unordered set of blocks incident to \(r\) and multiplying by the root \(x\)): Since \(r\) itself contributes \(x\) and is incident to an unordered set (\(\exp\)) of such decorated blocks, we obtain Tutte’s Block-Cut Tree Equation: \[R(x) = x \exp\!\Big(B'\big(R(x)\big)\Big) \iff B'\big(R(x)\big) = \ln\!\left(\frac{R(x)}{x}\right) = \ln C'(x).\]






flowchart TD
    r["Root Vertex r (weight x)"] --> B1["Block H_1 incident to r: B'(u)"]
    r --> B2["Block H_2 incident to r: B'(u)"]
    B1 --> v11["Non-root vertex v_1 in H_1: roots R(x)"]
    B1 --> v12["Non-root vertex v_2 in H_1: roots R(x)"]
    B2 --> v21["Non-root vertex w_1 in H_2: roots R(x)"]









Single-\(n\) Extraction & The Log-Free Integration-by-Parts Formula (\(O(n \log n)\))
Suppose we want to compute \(b_n = n! [u^n] B(u) = (n - 1)! [u^{n-1}] B'(u)\) for a given \(n \ge 2\) (#183 Luogu P5827, #016 fps_24_w).
In Tutte’s Block-Cut Tree Equation \(B'\big(R(x)\big) = \ln C'(x)\), the inner series \(u = R(x) = x C'(x)\) has valuation \(1\) (\([x^0] R(x) = 0\) and \([x^1] R(x) = c_1 = 1\)), so \(R(x) = x \phi(x)^{-1}\) with \(\phi(x) = \frac{x}{R(x)} = \frac{1}{C'(x)}\). Let \(H(x) = \ln C'(x)\), so \(B'\big(R(x)\big) = H(x)\).
Applying Composite Lagrange Inversion (Ch 11, Form 2: Inverse Composition) to extract \([u^{n-1}] B'(u)\) from \(B'(R(x)) = H(x)\) for \(n \ge 2\) gives: \[\begin{aligned}
[u^{n-1}] B'(u)
&= \frac{1}{n - 1} [x^{n-2}] \left( H'(x) \left(\frac{x}{R(x)}\right)^{n-1} \right) && \text{(by Ch 11 LIF on } B'(R(x)) = H(x)\text{)} \\
&= \frac{1}{n - 1} [x^{n-2}] \left( \frac{C''(x)}{C'(x)} \cdot C'(x)^{-(n-1)} \right) && \text{(since } H(x) = \ln C'(x) \text{ and } \frac{x}{R(x)} = \frac{1}{C'(x)}\text{)} \\
&= \frac{1}{n - 1} [x^{n-2}] \Big( C''(x) \, C'(x)^{-n} \Big). && \text{(combining powers of } C'(x)\text{)}
\end{aligned}\] Now observe the exact derivative inside the bracket: by the power rule of formal differentiation (Ch 02.1), \[\frac{d}{dx}\Big( C'(x)^{-(n-1)} \Big) = -(n - 1) \, C''(x) \, C'(x)^{-n} \implies C''(x) \, C'(x)^{-n} = -\frac{1}{n - 1} \frac{d}{dx}\Big( C'(x)^{-(n-1)} \Big).\] Using the coefficient-derivative identity \([x^{n-2}] F'(x) = (n - 1) [x^{n-1}] F(x)\), the factors of \(n - 1\) cancel and the logarithm \(H(x) = \ln C'(x)\) disappears completely: \[[u^{n-1}] B'(u) = -\frac{1}{(n - 1)^2} [x^{n-2}] \frac{d}{dx}\Big( C'(x)^{-(n-1)} \Big) = -\frac{1}{n - 1} [x^{n-1}] \Big( C'(x)^{-(n-1)} \Big).\] Multiplying both sides by \((n - 1)!\) yields the Log-Free Biconnected Graph Formula: \[b_n = (n - 1)! [u^{n-1}] B'(u) = -(n - 2)! [x^{n-1}] \left(\frac{x}{R(x)}\right)^{n-1} = -(n - 2)! [x^{n-1}] \Big( C'(x)^{-(n-1)} \Big) \qquad (n \ge 2).\]






ImportantAlgorithm Contract: Single-\(n\) Biconnected Graph Extraction (\(O(n \log n)\))




Input: Integer \(n \ge 2\) and prime modulus \(p > n\) (e.g., \(p = 998244353\)).
Output: \(b_n \bmod p\), the number of labeled 2-vertex-connected (biconnected) simple graphs on \(n\) vertices.
Algebraic Preconditions: \([x^0] G(x) = 1\), \([x^0] C'(x) = c_1 = 1 \in \mathbb{F}_p^\times\), and \(p > n\) so that \(n!\) and \((n-1)\)-th powers via \(\ln/\exp\) are well-defined in \(\mathbb{F}_p[[x]]/(x^n)\).
Steps:

Construct \(G(x) = \sum_{k=0}^{n} 2^{\binom{k}{2}} \frac{x^k}{k!} \bmod x^{n+1}\).
Compute \(C(x) = \ln G(x) \bmod x^{n+1}\) (1 polynomial \(\ln\)) and differentiate to get \(C'(x) = \sum_{k=0}^{n-1} c_{k+1} \frac{x^k}{k!} \bmod x^n\).
Compute \(P(x) = C'(x)^{-(n-1)} = \exp\!\big(-(n - 1) \ln C'(x)\big) \bmod x^n\) (1 polynomial \(\ln\) + 1 polynomial \(\exp\)).
Return \(b_n = -(n - 2)! [x^{n-1}] P(x) \bmod p\).

Complexity: \(O(n \log n)\) time and \(O(n)\) space.
Invariant: Every cut-vertex tree topology of blocks is accounted for once in \(R(x) = x \exp(B'(R(x)))\); inverting via LIF strips away all multi-block trees and isolates single blocks at degree \(n\).





Concrete Hand-Checkable Trace (\(N = 4\))
Let us verify the Log-Free Formula \(b_n = -(n-2)! [x^{n-1}] \big(C'(x)^{-(n-1)}\big)\) for \(n = 2, 3, 4\):

Connected Graph EGF \(C(x)\) and \(C'(x)\): \[C(x) = x + \frac{x^2}{2!} + 4 \frac{x^3}{3!} + 38 \frac{x^4}{4!} + O(x^5) = x + \frac{1}{2} x^2 + \frac{2}{3} x^3 + \frac{19}{12} x^4 + O(x^5),\] \[C'(x) = 1 + x + 2 x^2 + \frac{19}{3} x^3 + O(x^4).\]
\(n = 2\): \[b_2 = -0! [x^1] C'(x)^{-1} = -[x^1] (1 - x + O(x^2)) = 1 \quad (\text{the single edge } K_2).\]
\(n = 3\): \[C'(x)^{-2} = \big(1 + (x + 2x^2) + O(x^3)\big)^{-2} = 1 - 2(x + 2x^2) + 3 x^2 + O(x^3) = 1 - 2x - x^2 + O(x^3),\] \[b_3 = -1! [x^2] C'(x)^{-2} = -(-1) = 1 \quad (\text{the triangle } K_3).\]
\(n = 4\): \[C'(x)^{-3} = \left(1 + \left(x + 2x^2 + \frac{19}{3}x^3\right) + O(x^4)\right)^{-3} = 1 - 3\left(x + 2x^2 + \frac{19}{3}x^3\right) + 6\big(x^2 + 4x^3\big) - 10 x^3 + O(x^4)\] \[= 1 - 3x + (6 - 6)x^2 + (-19 + 24 - 10)x^3 + O(x^4) = 1 - 3x - 5x^3 + O(x^4),\] \[b_4 = -2! [x^3] C'(x)^{-3} = -2 \cdot (-5) = 10.\] Combinatorial check at \(n = 4\): The \(10\) biconnected graphs on \(4\) labeled vertices are \(K_4\) (\(1\)), \(K_4 - e\) (\(6\)), and \(C_4\) (\(3\)): \(1 + 6 + 3 = 10\)!







NoteRevisited Dual-Perspective Cross-Reference (#9: #183 Luogu P5827 \(\leftrightarrow\) Ch 21.4 & Ch 24)



Notice how the algebraic engine for extracting biconnected subgraphs depends on the query regime and host-graph symmetry:

Single \(n \le 2 \times 10^5\) on \(K_n\) (#183 Luogu P5827, Current Chapter): Use the Log-Free LIF formula \(b_n = -(n-2)! [x^{n-1}] \big(C'(x)^{-(n-1)}\big)\) in \(O(n \log n)\) time.
All \(1 \le n \le N\) for small/medium \(N \le 5000\) (#016 fps_24_w small-\(N\) regime): Unroll the substitution \(H(x) = \ln C'(x) = \sum_{k=1}^{N-1} \frac{b_{k+1}}{k!} R(x)^k\) degree by degree in \(O(N^2)\) time: at each \(k = 1, \dots, N-1\), read off \(\frac{b_{k+1}}{k!} = [x^k] H(x)\), subtract \(\frac{b_{k+1}}{k!} R(x)^k\) from \(H(x)\), and update \(R(x)^{k+1} = R(x)^k \cdot R(x) \bmod x^N\).
All \(1 \le n \le N\) for large \(N \le 2 \times 10^5\) (Chapter 21.4: Kinoshita–Li Fast Composition & Power Projection): Requires computing the compositional inverse \(R^{\langle -1 \rangle}(u)\) of \(R(x)\) up to degree \(N\) so that \(B'(u) = (\ln(R(x)/x)) \circ R^{\langle -1 \rangle}(u)\). In Chapter 21.4, we will revisit #183 Luogu P5827 and #016 fps_24_w using the Kinoshita–Li \(O(N \log^2 N)\) Compositional Inverse (revert) and Power Projection algorithm to compute all \(b_1, \dots, b_N\) simultaneously in \(O(N \log^2 N)\) time.
Biconnected Subgraphs of an Arbitrary Input Graph \(G = (V, E)\) with \(|V| \le 20\) (Chapter 24: Bitwise FWT, Set Power Series & Dirichlet GFs): When the host graph is not \(K_n\), subsets of size \(k\) are no longer interchangeable, so univariate EGFs fail; in Chapter 24, we lift Tutte’s pointing operator to the Pointed Set Power Series Ring \(\mathcal{R}_n\) and remove articulation points vertex-by-vertex via SPS \(\ln/\exp\) in \(O(n^3 2^n)\) time!

12.4 Bridge-Block Trees & 2-Edge-Connected (Bridgeless) Labeled Graphs

Concrete Combinatorial Objects: Bridges and 2-Edge-Connected Components
An edge \(e \in E(G)\) of a connected graph \(G\) is called a bridge (or cut-edge) if deleting \(e\) disconnects \(G\). A connected simple undirected graph with no bridges is called 2-edge-connected (or bridgeless; note that \(K_1\) has no edges and therefore no bridges, so \(e_{2,1} = 1\), whereas \(K_2\) consists of a single bridge edge, so \(e_{2,2} = 0\)).
How does decomposing a connected graph across bridges (1-edge cuts) differ from decomposing across cut-vertices (1-vertex cuts)?

In vertex-biconnected decomposition (Section 12.3), blocks partition the edges \(E(G)\) and overlap at cut-vertices.
In 2-edge-connected decomposition, deleting all bridge edges of \(G\) partitions the vertices \(V(G)\) into disjoint maximal 2-edge-connected subgraphs \(H_1, \dots, H_k\) (the bridge-blocks or 2-ECCs). Contracting each \(H_i\) into a single super-vertex turns the bridge edges into a tree of 2-edge-connected components (the bridge-block tree)!

Let:

\(B_{\text{2-edge}}(z) = \sum_{n=1}^{\infty} e_{2,n} \frac{z^n}{n!}\) be the EGF of 2-edge-connected labeled graphs (\(e_{2,1} = 1, e_{2,2} = 0, e_{2,3} = 1, e_{2,4} = 10\));
\(E(z) = \Theta B_{\text{2-edge}}(z) = z B'_{\text{2-edge}}(z) = \sum_{n=1}^{\infty} n \, e_{2,n} \frac{z^n}{n!}\) be the EGF of vertex-pointed 2-edge-connected labeled graphs;
\(R(x) = x C'(x)\) be the EGF of vertex-pointed connected labeled graphs.



Diagnostic Signal & Reverse-Engineering Scratchpad

The Diagnostic Signal
Whenever a graph family is decomposed by contracting 2-edge-connected components into a tree of bridge edges, every vertex \(v\) inside the root 2-edge-connected component can sprout an arbitrary unordered set (\(\exp\)) of bridge edges leading to pointed connected components \(R(x)\). Consequently, each vertex \(z\) of the root 2-ECC is replaced by \(z = W(x) = x \exp\!\big(R(x)\big)\)!


The Reverse-Engineering Scratchpad
Let us trace a vertex-pointed connected graph \((G, r)\) of EGF \(R(x)\) from its root vertex \(r\):

Step 1 (The root 2-edge-connected component \(H_0\)): Since bridge-blocks partition \(V(G)\), the root vertex \(r\) belongs to a unique 2-edge-connected component \(H_0\) of size \(k \ge 1\). Because \(r \in V(H_0)\) is distinguished as the root of \(G\), the pair \((H_0, r)\) is a vertex-pointed 2-edge-connected graph, which is enumerated by \(E(z) = z B'_{\text{2-edge}}(z)\).
Step 2 (What hangs off each vertex \(v \in V(H_0)\) across bridge edges?): In the bridge-block tree of \(G\), deleting the edges of \(H_0\) leaves each of the \(k\) vertices \(v \in V(H_0)\) (including \(r\) itself!) incident to an unordered set (\(\operatorname{SET} = \exp\)) of bridge edges leaving \(H_0\) at \(v\). For each such bridge edge \(\{v, u\}\), deleting \(\{v, u\}\) separates a connected sub-component rooted at \(u\)—which is an arbitrary vertex-pointed connected graph with EGF \(R(x)\)! Therefore, a single vertex \(v \in V(H_0)\) together with the unordered set of bridge-attached pointed connected components hanging off \(v\) has EGF: \[z = W(x) = x \exp\!\big(R(x)\big) = x \exp\!\big(x C'(x)\big).\]
Step 3 (Substituting \(z = W(x)\) into every vertex of the pointed root 2-ECC \(E(z)\)): Replacing every vertex \(z\) of the pointed 2-ECC \(E(z)\) by \(W(x) = x \exp(R(x))\) accounts for every vertex and edge of \((G, r)\) uniquely, yielding the Bridge-Block Functional Equation: \[E\!\Big(x \exp\!\big(R(x)\big)\Big) = R(x) \iff E\big(W(x)\big) = R(x), \qquad \text{where } W(x) = x \exp\!\big(R(x)\big).\]






flowchart TD
    subgraph H0["Root 2-ECC H_0 (Pointed by r, EGF E(z))"]
        r["Root vertex r"] --- v1["Vertex v_1 in H_0"]
        v1 --- v2["Vertex v_2 in H_0"]
        v2 --- r
    end
    r ==>|"Bridge edges from r: exp(R(x))"| T1["Pointed Connected R(x)"]
    v1 ==>|"Bridge edges from v_1: exp(R(x))"| T2["Pointed Connected R(x)"]
    v1 ==>|"Bridge edges from v_1: exp(R(x))"| T3["Pointed Connected R(x)"]
    v2 ==>|"Bridge edges from v_2: exp(R(x))"| T4["Pointed Connected R(x)"]












NoteDual Viewpoint: Comparing \(z = x \exp\!\big(E(z)\big)\) with \(R(x) = x \exp\!\big(B'(R(x))\big)\)



Since \(z = W(x) = x \exp(R(x))\) and \(R(x) = E(W(x)) = E(z)\), substituting \(R(x) = E(z)\) into \(z = x \exp(R(x))\) yields the dual relation: \[z = x \exp\!\big(E(z)\big) \iff x = z \exp\!\big(-E(z)\big),\] where \(E(z) = z B'_{\text{2-edge}}(z)\) is the pointed 2-ECC generating function.
Why does the bridge-block equation have \(E(z) = z B'_{\text{2-edge}}(z)\) in the exponent of \(z = x \exp(E(z))\), whereas Tutte’s vertex-biconnected equation \(R(x) = x \exp(B'(R(x)))\) has \(B'(u)\) (without a factor of \(u\))?

In a vertex-biconnected block incident to \(r\), the root \(r\) is shared with the block, so only the \(k - 1\) non-root vertices of the block receive independent factors of \(R(x)\) (giving \(\frac{b_k}{(k-1)!} R(x)^{k-1}\), summed by \(B'(R(x))\)).
Across a bridge edge \(\{r, u\}\), the bridge connects \(r\) to a disjoint 2-edge-connected component rooted at \(u\), so all \(k\) vertices of that component (including \(u\)) lie outside \(r\)’s component (giving \(\frac{k \, e_{2,k}}{k!} z^k\), summed by \(E(z) = z B'_{\text{2-edge}}(z)\)).






Single-\(n\) Extraction via Ch 11 LIF (\(O(n \log n)\))
Suppose we want to compute \(e_{2,n} = n! [z^n] B_{\text{2-edge}}(z) = (n - 1)! [z^n] E(z)\) for a given \(n \ge 1\) (#184 Luogu P5828).
In the Bridge-Block Functional Equation \(E\big(W(x)\big) = R(x)\), the inner series \(z = W(x) = x \exp(R(x))\) has valuation \(1\) with \(\phi(x) = \frac{x}{W(x)} = \exp(-R(x))\). We can extract \([z^n] E(z)\) by either Form 3 or Form 2 of Chapter 11 LIF:

Derivation via Formal Residue Change of Variables (Ch 11, Form 3): Since \(z = W(x) = x e^{R(x)}\), we have \(W'(x) = \big(1 + x R'(x)\big) e^{R(x)}\), so: \[\begin{aligned}
[z^n] E(z)
&= \operatorname{Res}_z \, E(z) z^{-n-1} = \operatorname{Res}_x \, E(W(x)) W(x)^{-n-1} W'(x) && \text{(change of variables } z = W(x)\text{)} \\
&= [x^n] \, R(x) \big(1 + x R'(x)\big) \exp\!\big(-n R(x)\big). && \text{(substituting } E(W(x)) = R(x),\, W(x) = x e^{R(x)}\text{)}
\end{aligned}\]
Derivative-Free Simplification via Integration by Parts (for \(n \ge 2\)): Alternatively, applying Standard Inverse LIF (Ch 11, Form 2) to \(E(W(x)) = R(x)\) gives for \(n \ge 1\): \[[z^n] E(z) = \frac{1}{n} [x^{n-1}] \Big( R'(x) \exp\!\big(-n R(x)\big) \Big).\] For \(n \ge 2\), notice that \(\frac{d}{dx}\Big(\exp(-n R(x))\Big) = -n R'(x) \exp(-n R(x))\). Using \([x^{n-1}] F'(x) = n [x^n] F(x)\) cancels the factor of \(n\) and eliminates \(R'(x)\): \[[z^n] E(z) = -\frac{1}{n^2} [x^{n-1}] \frac{d}{dx}\Big(\exp\!\big(-n R(x)\big)\Big) = -\frac{1}{n} [x^n] \exp\!\big(-n R(x)\big) \qquad (n \ge 2).\] Multiplying by \((n - 1)!\) yields the Derivative-Free 2-Edge-Connected Graph Formula: \[e_{2,n} = (n - 1)! [z^n] E(z) = -\frac{(n - 1)!}{n} [x^n] \exp\!\big(-n R(x)\big) = -\frac{(n - 1)!}{n} [x^n] \exp\!\big(-n x C'(x)\big) \qquad (n \ge 2).\]



Connected Graphs with a Prescribed Number of Bridges (#190 Luogu P6596)
What if a problem asks for the number of connected simple labeled graphs on \(n\) vertices that have at most \(m\) bridge edges (or exactly \(b = k - 1\) bridge edges)?
Deleting the \(b = k - 1\) bridge edges splits the graph into an unordered set of \(k\) 2-edge-connected components \(H_1, \dots, H_k\) of sizes \(s_1 + s_2 + \dots + s_k = n\). By the Generalized Cayley Component-Tree Formula (Chapter 4.5), the number of ways to place \(k - 1\) bridge edges between \(k\) fixed components of sizes \(s_1, \dots, s_k\) to form a tree of components is: \[n^{k-2} \prod_{i=1}^{k} s_i \qquad (\text{which also holds at } k = 1 \text{ since } n^{-1} s_1 = 1).\] Notice that multiplying the 2-ECC count \(e_{2,s_i}\) by its vertex size \(s_i\) produces the \(s_i\)-th coefficient of the pointed 2-ECC generating function \(E(z) = z B'_{\text{2-edge}}(z) = \sum_{s \ge 1} s \, e_{2,s} \frac{z^s}{s!}\)! Therefore, the number of connected labeled graphs on \(n\) vertices with exact \(k - 1\) bridge edges (\(k\) 2-edge-connected components) is: \[\text{ans}_{k-1} = \frac{n!}{k!} \, n^{k-2} \, [z^n] E(z)^k \qquad (1 \le k \le n).\]


Concrete Hand-Checkable Trace (\(N = 4\))
Let us verify \(e_{2,n} = -\frac{(n-1)!}{n} [x^n] \exp(-n R(x))\) for \(n = 2, 3, 4\) using \(R(x) = x C'(x) = x + x^2 + 2x^3 + \frac{19}{3}x^4 + O(x^5)\):

\(n = 2\): \[\exp(-2 R(x)) = \exp(-2x - 2x^2 + O(x^3)) = 1 - 2x + (2 - 2)x^2 + O(x^3) = 1 - 2x + 0x^2 + O(x^3),\] \[e_{2,2} = -\frac{1!}{2} [x^2] \exp(-2 R(x)) = 0 \quad (\text{since } K_2 \text{ is a bridge}).\]
\(n = 3\): \[\exp(-3 R(x)) = \exp(-3x - 3x^2 - 6x^3 + O(x^4)) = 1 - 3x + \frac{3}{2}x^2 + \left(-\frac{9}{2} + 9 - 6\right)x^3 + O(x^4) = 1 - 3x + \frac{3}{2}x^2 - \frac{3}{2}x^3 + O(x^4),\] \[e_{2,3} = -\frac{2!}{3} [x^3] \exp(-3 R(x)) = -\frac{2}{3} \cdot \left(-\frac{3}{2}\right) = 1 \quad (\text{the triangle } K_3).\]
\(n = 4\): \[\begin{aligned}
[x^4]\exp\!\big(-4 R(x)\big)
&= [x^4]\exp\!\left(\underbrace{-4x - 4x^2 - 8x^3 - \frac{76}{3}x^4}_{A(x)} + O(x^5)\right) \\
&= [x^4]\left(A(x) + \frac{A(x)^2}{2!} + \frac{A(x)^3}{3!} + \frac{A(x)^4}{4!}\right) \\
&= -\frac{76}{3} + \frac{2(-4)(-8) + (-4)^2}{2} + \frac{3(-4)^2(-4)}{6} + \frac{(-4)^4}{24} \\
&= -\frac{76}{3} + 40 - 32 + \frac{32}{3} = -\frac{20}{3},
\end{aligned}\] \[e_{2,4} = -\frac{3!}{4} \cdot \left(-\frac{20}{3}\right) = 10 \quad (K_4,\, 6 \text{ copies of } K_4 - e, \text{ and } 3 \text{ copies of } C_4).\] (Note: At \(n = 4\), \(e_{2,4} = b_4 = 10\) because the smallest graph that is 2-edge-connected without being 2-vertex-connected is the “bowtie” graph formed by two triangles sharing a single cut-vertex, which requires \(n = 5\) vertices!)
Bridge-Count Decomposition of the \(38\) Connected Graphs on \(n = 4\) Vertices: Using \(E(z) = z + 0 \frac{z^2}{2!} + 3 \frac{z^3}{3!} + 40 \frac{z^4}{4!} = z + \frac{1}{2} z^3 + \frac{5}{3} z^4 + O(z^5)\) and \(\text{ans}_{k-1} = \frac{4!}{k!} 4^{k-2} [z^4] E(z)^k\):

\(b = 0\) bridges (\(k = 1\)): \(\frac{24}{1} \cdot 4^{-1} \cdot \frac{5}{3} = 10\) graphs.
\(b = 1\) bridge (\(k = 2\)): \(\frac{24}{2} \cdot 4^0 \cdot [z^4](z + \frac{1}{2}z^3)^2 = 12 \cdot 1 = 12\) graphs (a triangle \(K_3\) with one leaf attached: \(\binom{4}{3} \cdot 3 = 12\)).
\(b = 2\) bridges (\(k = 3\)): \(\frac{24}{6} \cdot 4^1 \cdot [z^4](z + \frac{1}{2}z^3)^3 = 0\) graphs (since \(e_{2,2} = 0\), no partition of \(4\) into \(3\) positive parts avoids size \(2\)).
\(b = 3\) bridges (\(k = 4\)): \(\frac{24}{24} \cdot 4^2 \cdot [z^4] z^4 = 16\) graphs (labeled trees on \(4\) vertices).
Total: \(10 + 12 + 0 + 16 = 38 = c_4\).








WarningFailure Mode & Remedy: Confusing \(B_{\text{2-edge}}(z)\) with \(B_{\text{vertex}}(u)\) at \(n = 1, 2, 5\)



Symptom: Using \(b_2 = 1\) in a 2-edge-connected problem or \(e_{2,1} = 1\) in a 2-vertex-connected problem.
Root Cause:

Vertex-biconnected blocks partition the edges \(E(G)\): a single edge \(K_2\) is a block (\(b_2 = 1\), \(b_1 = 0\)), and two triangles sharing a cut-vertex (“bowtie” on \(n = 5\) vertices) split into two \(K_3\) blocks (\(b_5\) excludes bowties).
2-edge-connected components partition the vertices \(V(G)\): an isolated vertex \(K_1\) is a 2-ECC (\(e_{2,1} = 1\)), a single bridge edge \(K_2\) is not 2-edge-connected (\(e_{2,2} = 0\)), and a bowtie on \(n = 5\) vertices has no bridges so it is 2-edge-connected (counted in \(e_{2,5}\)).

Remedy: Always check the \(n = 1, 2\) base cases against the table below before coding!








NoteAlgorithm Contract: Single-\(n\) 2-Edge-Connected Graphs & Bridge-Bounded Connected Graphs




Input: Vertex count \(n \ge 1\) (and optional bridge upper bound \(m \ge 0\)), prime modulus \(p > n\).
Preconditions: \([x^0] G(x) = 1\), \([x^0] R(x) = 0\), \([x^1] R(x) = 1\), and \(p > n\) so that \(n!\) and degree-\(n\) \(\ln/\exp\) are well-defined in \(\mathbb{F}_p[[x]]/(x^{n+1})\).
Postconditions:

Single-\(n\) 2-ECC count: Returns \(e_{2,1} = 1\) for \(n = 1\), and \(e_{2,n} = -\frac{(n-1)!}{n} [x^n] \exp\!\big(-n R(x)\big) \bmod p\) for \(n \ge 2\).
Connected graphs with \(\le m\) bridges: Given \(E(z) = \sum_{s=1}^{n} s \, e_{2,s} \frac{z^s}{s!}\), returns \(\sum_{k=1}^{\min(n, m+1)} \frac{n!}{k!} n^{k-2} [z^n] E(z)^k \bmod p\).

Complexity:

Single-\(n\) 2-ECC extraction: \(O(n \log n)\) time (1 polynomial \(\ln\) and 1 polynomial \(\exp\) of degree \(n\)) and \(O(n)\) space.
All \(e_{2,1 \dots n}\) + bridge-count assembly for small \(n\) under arbitrary prime \(p\): \(O(n^3)\) time and \(O(n^2)\) space.

Core Invariant: Every vertex \(z\) of the pointed root 2-ECC \(E(z)\) sprouts an unordered set of bridge-attached pointed connected components \(W(x) = x \exp(R(x))\), so \(E(W(x)) = R(x)\) holds identically up to degree \(n\).

text:
12.6 Practice Ladder (8-Problem 4-Tier Curriculum)

Tier 1: Stepping Stones (SS-1, SS-2)


Stepping Stone 1 (#176) — Luogu P5434: 有标号荒漠计数 (Labeled Desert Enumeration)

Source: Luogu P5434
Prerequisites: Pointed Cactus Functional Equation (§12.2), Logarithmic Newton Iteration (Ch 10.2), EGF Connected Component \(\exp\) (Ch 04.3).


Problem Statement & Exact Constraints
A cactus graph is a connected simple undirected graph in which every edge belongs to at most one simple cycle. A desert is a simple undirected graph in which every connected component is a cactus graph. Given a positive integer \(N\), compute for a given \(N\) (or for all \(1 \le n \le N\)) the number of labeled deserts on \(N\) vertices modulo \(998244353\).

Constraints: \(1 \le N \le 10^5\), modulus \(p = 998244353\).
Required Complexity: \(O(N \log N)\) time and \(O(N)\) space.



Small Hand-Checkable Trace (\(N \le 4\))

\(N = 1\): \(\mathbf{1}\) (\(K_1\)).
\(N = 2\): \(\mathbf{2}\) (\(K_2\) and \(2 K_1\)).
\(N = 3\): \(\mathbf{8}\) (all \(2^{\binom{3}{2}} = 8\) graphs on \(3\) vertices have at most \(1\) cycle, so all \(8\) are deserts).
\(N = 4\): \(\mathbf{57}\) (out of \(2^{\binom{4}{2}} = 64\) graphs on \(4\) vertices, only \(K_4\) (\(1\) graph) and \(K_4 - e\) (\(6\) graphs, two triangles sharing an edge) fail to be deserts, leaving \(64 - 7 = 57\) deserts, of which \(c_4 = 31\) are connected cacti).



Hint 1 — Diagnostic Signal & Combinatorial Model

A desert is an unordered set of connected cactus components. Because an unrooted cactus has no canonical starting vertex from which to peel off sub-cacti, distinguish one vertex as the root \(r\) and observe how the biconnected blocks incident to \(r\) (bridge edges and simple cycles) partition the remaining vertices into independent pointed sub-cacti.



Hint 2 — Algebraic Setup & Reverse-Engineering Scratchpad

Each block incident to the root \(r\) is either a bridge edge \(K_2\) (contributing \(T(x)\)) or a simple cycle \(C_m\) of length \(m \ge 3\) (contributing \(\frac{T(x)^{m-1}}{2}\) after dividing by \(2\) for undirected cycle reversal). Summing over all blocks gives: \[T(x) = x \exp\!\left(\frac{2T(x) - T(x)^2}{2(1 - T(x))}\right) \iff \Psi(T) = \ln\!\left(\frac{T(x)}{x}\right) - \frac{2T(x) - T(x)^2}{2(1 - T(x))} = 0.\] Then unpointing gives \(C(x) = \int_0^x \frac{T(t)}{t}\,dt\) and taking the SET of cactus components gives \(D(x) = \exp(C(x))\).



Hint 3 — Coefficient Extraction & Complexity Contract

Solve \(\Psi(T) = 0 \bmod x^{N+1}\) via Logarithmic Newton Iteration in \(O(N \log N)\) time, integrate \(C(x) = \int_0^x \frac{T(t)}{t}\,dt\) (dividing \([x^n]T(x)\) by \(n\) for \(1 \le n \le N\)), and compute \(D(x) = \exp(C(x)) \bmod x^{N+1}\) to extract \(d_N = N! [x^N] D(x)\).







NoteComplete Derivation & Solution






Step 1: Pointed Cactus Equation and Newton Iteration
Let \(T(x) = \sum_{n=1}^{N} t_n \frac{x^n}{n!}\) be the EGF of vertex-pointed labeled cacti. By Section 12.2, \(T(x)\) satisfies: \[T(x) = x \exp\!\left(\frac{2T(x) - T(x)^2}{2(1 - T(x))}\right).\] Writing \(\Psi(T) = \ln(T/x) - \frac{2T - T^2}{2(1 - T)} = 0\) and computing \(\Psi'(T) = \frac{2 - 6T + 6T^2 - T^3}{2T(1 - T)^2}\), the Newton step from precision \(d\) to \(2d\) (starting from \(T_2(x) = x \bmod x^2\)) is: \[T_{2d} \equiv T_d - \frac{2 T_d (1 - T_d)^2 \ln(T_d / x) - T_d (2 T_d - T_d^2)(1 - T_d)}{2 - 6 T_d + 6 T_d^2 - T_d^3} \pmod{x^{2d}}.\] Note that \(\ln(T_d / x)\) is computed by shifting \(T_d\) right by \(1\) degree so its constant term is \([x^1]T_d = 1\).


Step 2: Unpointing to \(C(x)\) and Exponentiating to \(D(x)\)
Since \(T(x) = x C'(x)\) and \(p = 998244353 > N\), the unrooted cactus EGF \(C(x)\) has coefficients: \[[x^0] C(x) = 0, \qquad [x^n] C(x) = \frac{[x^n] T(x)}{n} \quad (1 \le n \le N).\] (Equivalently, by Block-Cut Dissimilarity, \(C(x) = \frac{1}{2}\ln\frac{1}{1-T(x)} + \frac{2T(x)-5T(x)^2+T(x)^3}{4(1-T(x))}\).)
Finally, since a desert is a disjoint union of cactus components, its EGF is \(D(x) = \exp(C(x)) \bmod x^{N+1}\), and the number of labeled deserts on \(N\) vertices is: \[d_N = N! [x^N] \exp\!\big(C(x)\big) \pmod{998244353}.\]
// Core Newton step for pointed cactus T(x) mod x^d -> mod x^(2d)
Poly Q = Poly{2} - T * 6 + (T * T).trunc(2 * d) * 6 - (T * T * T).trunc(2 * d);
Poly one_minus_T = Poly{1} - T;
Poly ln_T_over_x = (T >> 1).Pre(2 * d - 1).Ln(2 * d - 1); // T(x)/x has constant term 1
Poly num = (T * 2 * one_minus_T).trunc(2 * d) * one_minus_T.trunc(2 * d) * ln_T_over_x
         - (T * (T * 2 - T * T)).trunc(2 * d) * one_minus_T;
T = (T - (num.trunc(2 * d) * Q.Inv(2 * d)).trunc(2 * d)).Pre(2 * d);






NoteAlgorithm Contract




Input & Preconditions: Integer \(N \in [1, 10^5]\) and prime modulus \(p = 998244353 > N\); \([x^0]T(x) = 0\) and \([x^1]T(x) = 1\), so \(T(x)/x\) has constant term \(1\).
Output & Postconditions: Computes \(T(x) \bmod x^{N+1}\), \(C(x) = \int_0^x \frac{T(t)}{t}\,dt \bmod x^{N+1}\), and outputs \(d_N = N! [x^N] \exp(C(x)) \bmod p\).
Invariants: After each Newton doubling step \(d \to 2d\), \(T_{2d}(x) \equiv x \exp\!\left(\frac{2T_{2d}(x) - T_{2d}(x)^2}{2(1 - T_{2d}(x))}\right) \pmod{x^{2d}}\).
Complexity: \(T(N) = T(N/2) + O(N \log N) = O(N \log N)\) time and \(O(N)\) space.
Failure Modes & Edge Cases: (1) Dividing the cycle weight by \(2\) omits undirected orientations of \(3\)-cycles or double-counts \(2\)-cycles unless \(\frac{2T - T^2}{2(1 - T)} = T + \sum_{k \ge 3} \frac{T^k}{2}\) is used; (2) Forgetting to integrate \(C(x) = \int_0^x \frac{T(t)}{t}\,dt\) before taking \(\exp(C(x))\) counts vertex-pointed deserts instead of unpointed deserts; (3) At \(N = 1\), \(d_1 = 1\).











Stepping Stone 2 (#245) — 51Nod 1728: 不动点 (Fixed Points / Bounded-Depth Endofunctions)

Source: 51Nod 1728
Prerequisites: Functional Digraphs & Rooted Trees (§12.1), SET/CYC Composition (Ch 04.2), Gessel’s Form 3 LIF (Ch 11.2).


Problem Statement & Exact Constraints
A function \(f : \{1, 2, \dots, n\} \to \{1, 2, \dots, n\}\) is called \(k\)-step stabilizing if for every element \(x \in \{1, 2, \dots, n\}\), iterating \(f\) reaches a fixed point in at most \(k\) steps: \[f^{(k)}(x) = f^{(k+1)}(x) \qquad \forall\, x \in \{1, 2, \dots, n\}.\] Given integers \(n\) and \(k\), compute the number of \(k\)-step stabilizing functions on \(\{1, 2, \dots, n\}\) modulo \(998244353\).

Constraints:

Subtask 1 (Small Depth): \(1 \le n \le 2 \times 10^5\), \(k \in \{1, 2\}\).
Subtask 2 (General Depth): \(1 \le n \le 5000\), \(1 \le k \le n\).
Subtask 3 (Unbounded Depth): \(1 \le n \le 2 \times 10^5\), \(k \ge n - 1\).

Required Complexity: \(O(n \log n)\) for Subtask 1, \(O(\min(k, n) \cdot n \log n)\) for Subtask 2, and \(O(\log n)\) for Subtask 3.



Small Hand-Checkable Trace (\(n \le 4\))

\(n = 2\):

\(k = 1\) (idempotent \(f(f(x)) = f(x)\)): \(\mathbf{3}\) functions (the identity \(f(1)=1, f(2)=2\), plus the two constant functions \(f \equiv 1\) and \(f \equiv 2\); only the swap \(1 \leftrightarrow 2\) fails).
\(k \ge 1\): \(\mathbf{3}\) functions (since \(n - 1 = 1\), no tree on \(2\) vertices has height \(\ge 2\)).

\(n = 3\):

\(k = 1\): \(\binom{3}{1} 1^2 + \binom{3}{2} 2^1 + \binom{3}{3} 3^0 = 3 + 6 + 1 = \mathbf{10}\).
\(k \ge 2\): \((3 + 1)^{3 - 1} = \mathbf{16}\) (adds the \(3! = 6\) chains \(u \to v \to r = r\) of height \(2\)).

\(n = 4\):

\(k = 1\): \(\sum_{m=1}^{4} \binom{4}{m} m^{4-m} = 4 + 24 + 12 + 1 = \mathbf{41}\).
\(k = 2\): \(\mathbf{101}\) (all rooted forests on \(4\) vertices except the \(4! = 24\) directed paths of height \(3\)).
\(k \ge 3\): \((4 + 1)^{4 - 1} = \mathbf{125}\).




Hint 1 — Diagnostic Signal & Combinatorial Model

What does the condition \(f^{(k)}(x) = f^{(k+1)}(x)\) mean in the functional digraph of \(f\)? First, every directed cycle must have length \(1\) (a fixed point \(r\) with \(f(r) = r\), since a cycle of length \(\ge 2\) never stabilizes under \(f^{(t)}(x) = f^{(t+1)}(x)\)). Second, every vertex \(x\) must have directed distance at most \(k\) to its component’s fixed point \(r\)!



Hint 2 — Algebraic Setup & Reverse-Engineering Scratchpad

Each connected component is a rooted labeled tree of height at most \(k\) (where the root \(r\) has height \(0\) and edges are directed toward \(r\)), and the entire function \(f\) is an unordered set (\(\exp\)) of such components! Let \(F_j(x)\) be the EGF of rooted labeled trees of height \(\le j\). Then: \[F_0(x) = x, \qquad F_j(x) = x \exp\!\big(F_{j-1}(x)\big) \quad (1 \le j \le k),\] and the EGF of valid functions \(f\) is \(\exp\!\big(F_k(x)\big) = \frac{F_{k+1}(x)}{x}\)!



Hint 3 — Coefficient Extraction & Complexity Contract

For general \(k\), compute \(F_0, F_1, \dots, F_k \bmod x^{n+1}\) by \(k\) successive polynomial exponentials and extract \(n! [x^n] \exp(F_k(x)) = n! [x^{n+1}] F_{k+1}(x)\). For the related variant where cycles of any length are allowed and tree height is \(\le 1\) (\(f(x) \in \text{Image}(f)\) or \(k \to \infty\)), use \(\frac{1}{1 - T(x)}\) or Bell numbers \(\exp(e^x - 1)\).







NoteComplete Derivation & Solution






Step 1: Combinatorial Characterization of \(f^{(k)}(x) = f^{(k+1)}(x)\)
In the functional digraph of \(f : \{1, \dots, n\} \to \{1, \dots, n\}\), let \(y = f^{(k)}(x)\). The condition \(f(y) = y\) says that \(y\) is a fixed point (a cycle of length \(1\)), and \(f^{(k)}(x) = y\) says that every vertex \(x\) reaches a fixed point in at most \(k\) directed steps. Deleting the self-loop \(r \to r\) at each fixed point \(r\) turns each connected component into a rooted labeled tree of height at most \(k\), where the root \(r\) is at depth \(0\) and every vertex is at depth \(\le k\).


Step 2: Iterated Exponential Recurrence
Let \(F_j(x)\) be the EGF of rooted labeled trees of height \(\le j\):

At height \(0\), a tree consists only of the root vertex: \(F_0(x) = x\).
At height \(j \ge 1\), a tree consists of a root vertex \(x\) together with an unordered set (\(\operatorname{SET} = \exp\)) of subtrees of height \(\le j - 1\): \[F_j(x) = x \exp\!\big(F_{j-1}(x)\big).\] Since an endofunction satisfying \(f^{(k)} = f^{(k+1)}\) is an unordered set (\(\operatorname{SET}\)) of connected components, each of which is a rooted tree of height \(\le k\), the EGF of valid functions is: \[G_k(x) = \exp\!\big(F_k(x)\big) = \frac{F_{k+1}(x)}{x}.\] Therefore, the number of valid functions on \(n\) elements is: \[\text{ans}(n, k) = n! [x^n] \exp\!\big(F_k(x)\big) = n! [x^{n+1}] F_{k+1}(x).\]



Step 3: Special Cases \(k = 1\), \(k = 2\), and \(k \ge n - 1\)

\(k = 1\) (Idempotent functions \(f(f(x)) = f(x)\)): \(F_1(x) = x e^x\), so \(G_1(x) = \exp(x e^x) = \sum_{m=0}^{\infty} \frac{x^m e^{mx}}{m!}\). Extracting \(n! [x^n] G_1(x)\) gives: \[\text{ans}(n, 1) = \sum_{m=1}^{n} \binom{n}{m} m^{n-m},\] which can also be computed for all \(n \le N\) in one \(O(N \log N)\) polynomial \(\exp\).
\(k = 2\) (\(f^{(2)}(x) = f^{(3)}(x)\)): \(F_2(x) = x \exp(x e^x)\) and \(G_2(x) = \exp(x \exp(x e^x))\), requiring two \(O(N \log N)\) polynomial exponentials.
\(k \ge n - 1\) (Forest of arbitrary-height rooted trees): As \(k \ge n - 1\), \(F_k(x) \equiv T(x) \pmod{x^{n+1}}\) where \(T(x) = x e^{T(x)}\). Then \(G_\infty(x) = \exp(T(x)) = \frac{T(x)}{x}\), and by Section 12.1: \[\text{ans}(n, \ge n-1) = n! [x^n] \frac{T(x)}{x} = n! [x^{n+1}] T(x) = \frac{n!}{(n+1)!} (n + 1)^n = (n + 1)^{n-1}.\]







NoteAlgorithm Contract




Input & Preconditions: Integers \(n \ge 1\) and \(k \ge 1\); prime modulus \(p = 998244353 > n\); \([x^0]F_j(x) = 0\) for all \(j \ge 0\) so \(\exp(F_j(x))\) is well-defined in \(\mathbb{F}_p[[x]]/(x^{n+1})\).
Postconditions: Outputs \(\text{ans}(n, k) = n! [x^n] \exp(F_k(x)) \bmod p\).
Index & Truncation Boundaries: Series are truncated modulo \(x^{n+1}\) on indices \([0, n]\); the height recursion runs for \(j = 0, 1, \dots, \min(k, n - 1)\) with \(F_0(x) = x\).
Time & Space Complexity: \(O(\min(k, n) \cdot n \log n)\) time via iterated polynomial \(\exp\) (\(O(n \log n)\) for \(k \in \{1, 2\}\), \(O(\log n)\) for \(k \ge n - 1\)) and \(O(n)\) space.
Core Invariant: After iteration \(j \in [0, \min(k, n-1)]\), \(m! [x^m] F_j(x)\) equals the exact number of rooted labeled trees on \(m\) vertices of height at most \(j\) for all \(1 \le m \le n\).
Failure Modes & Edge Cases: When \(k \ge n - 1\), running \(k\) polynomial exponentials when \(k\) is large (e.g. \(k = 10^9\)) will TLE—clamp \(k \leftarrow \min(k, n - 1)\) or use the closed form \((n + 1)^{n - 1} \bmod p\); also ensure \(F_{j}(x) = x \exp(F_{j-1}(x))\) shifts coefficients by \(1\) before zeroing degree \(> n\).












Tier 2: Intermediate (Int-1, Int-2)


Intermediate 1 (#146) — Luogu P3684 / BZOJ 3684: 大朋友和多叉树 (Big Friend and Multi-Way Trees)

Source: Luogu P3684 / BZOJ 3684
Prerequisites: Implicit Tree Equation \(F(x) = x \phi(F(x))\) & LIF (Ch 11.2), Pointed Tree Species (§12.1).


Problem Statement & Exact Constraints
We want to count rooted ordered (plane) trees with \(s\) leaves (each leaf has \(0\) children) such that every internal node has an allowed number of children \(d \in D\), where \(D \subseteq \{2, 3, \dots, s\}\) is a given set of allowed branching degrees (Notice \(1 \notin D\), so there are no unary internal nodes, making the total number of trees with \(s\) leaves finite!).
Given the leaf count \(s\) and the set \(D\) presented via \(m\) forbidden degree intervals, compute the number of valid rooted plane trees with \(s\) leaves modulo \(998244353\).

Constraints: \(1 \le s \le 10^5\), \(D \subseteq \{2, 3, \dots, s\}\), modulus \(p = 998244353\).
Required Complexity: \(O(s \log s)\) time and \(O(s)\) space.



Small Hand-Checkable Trace (\(s \le 4\), with \(D = \{2, 3\}\))

\(s = 1\): \(\mathbf{1}\) (a single leaf node).
\(s = 2\): \(\mathbf{1}\) (root with \(2\) leaf children).
\(s = 3\): \(\mathbf{3}\) (\(1\) tree where the root has \(3\) leaf children, plus \(2\) binary trees where the root has \(2\) children of leaf counts \((1, 2)\) or \((2, 1)\)).
\(s = 4\): \(\mathbf{10}\) when \(D = \{2, 3\}\) (\(5\) binary trees \(+ 3\) trees with a ternary root and one binary child \(+ 2\) trees with a binary root and one ternary child), or \(\mathbf{11}\) when \(D = \{2, 3, 4\}\) (adding the \(1\) tree whose root has \(4\) leaf children, recovering the super-Catalan / little Schröder sequence \(1, 1, 3, 11\)).



Hint 1 — Diagnostic Signal & Combinatorial Model

Let \(F(x)\) be the OGF of valid rooted plane trees where \(x\) marks leaves (\([x^1] F(x) = 1\) for a single leaf). Every valid tree is either a single leaf (\(x\)) or an internal root node with \(d \in D\) ordered child subtrees (\(F(x)^d\)).



Hint 2 — Algebraic Setup & Reverse-Engineering Scratchpad

The specification translates directly to the functional equation: \[F(x) = x + \sum_{d \in D} F(x)^d \iff x = F(x) - \sum_{d \in D} F(x)^d = F(x)\left(1 - \sum_{d \in D} F(x)^{d-1}\right).\] Dividing by \(1 - \sum_{d \in D} F(x)^{d-1}\) puts this into the standard Lagrange Inversion form \(F(x) = x \phi(F(x))\)!



Hint 3 — Coefficient Extraction & Complexity Contract

Here \(\phi(u) = \left(1 - \sum_{d \in D} u^{d-1}\right)^{-1}\). By Ch 11 LIF, for a single leaf count \(s\): \[[x^s] F(x) = \frac{1}{s} [u^{s-1}] \phi(u)^s = \frac{1}{s} [u^{s-1}] \left(1 - \sum_{d \in D} u^{d-1}\right)^{-s},\] which is computed via one polynomial logarithm and one polynomial exponential in \(O(s \log s)\) time!







NoteComplete Derivation & Solution






Step 1: Translating the Leaf-Enumerated Tree Specification
Let \(F(x) = \sum_{n=1}^{\infty} f_n x^n\) be the OGF of valid rooted plane trees where \(x\) marks the number of leaves. Because \(1 \notin D\), every internal node has at least \(2\) children, so a tree with \(s\) leaves has at most \(s - 1\) internal nodes and \(f_s\) is finite.
A valid tree is either:

A single leaf node (contributes \(x\)), or
An internal root node with \(d \in D\) ordered child subtrees, each of which is a valid tree (contributes \(F(x)^d\)).

Summing over both cases gives: \[F(x) = x + \sum_{d \in D} F(x)^d.\]


Step 2: Rewriting in Standard LIF Form \(F(x) = x \phi(F(x))\)
Rearranging the equation to isolate \(x\) gives: \[x = F(x) - \sum_{d \in D} F(x)^d = F(x)\left(1 - \sum_{d \in D} F(x)^{d-1}\right) \implies F(x) = \frac{x}{1 - \sum_{d \in D} F(x)^{d-1}}.\] Define \(Q(u) = 1 - \sum_{d \in D} u^{d-1}\) (since \(d \ge 2\) for all \(d \in D\), we have \(d - 1 \ge 1\) and \([u^0] Q(u) = 1\)) and \(\phi(u) = Q(u)^{-1}\).


Step 3: Extracting \([x^s] F(x)\) via Lagrange Inversion
By Chapter 11.2 Lagrange Inversion (Form 1), for \(s \ge 1\): \[[x^s] F(x) = \frac{1}{s} [u^{s-1}] \phi(u)^s = \frac{1}{s} [u^{s-1}] Q(u)^{-s} = \frac{1}{s} [u^{s-1}] \exp\!\big(-s \ln Q(u)\big).\] Since \([u^0] Q(u) = 1\), \(\ln Q(u) \bmod u^s\) and \(\exp(-s \ln Q(u)) \bmod u^s\) are well-defined in \(\mathbb{F}_{998244353}[[u]]/(u^s)\).






NoteAlgorithm Contract




Input & Preconditions: Leaf count \(s \in [1, 10^5]\) and allowed out-degree set \(D \subseteq \{2, 3, \dots, s\}\); \(1 \notin D\), so \(Q(u) = 1 - \sum_{d \in D} u^{d-1}\) satisfies \([u^0]Q(u) = 1\); prime modulus \(p = 998244353 > s\).
Postconditions: Outputs \([x^s] F(x) = \frac{1}{s} [u^{s-1}] \exp(-s \ln Q(u)) \bmod p\) (with boundary check \(s = 1 \implies 1\)).
Index & Truncation Boundaries: Polynomial \(Q(u)\) is constructed modulo \(u^s\) on indices \([0, s - 1]\), where each \(d \in D\) with \(d \le s\) sets \([u^{d-1}] Q(u) \equiv -1 \pmod p\).
Time & Space Complexity: \(O(s \log s)\) time (1 polynomial \(\ln\) and 1 polynomial \(\exp\) of degree \(s\)) and \(O(s)\) space.
Core Invariant: Under \(x = u Q(u)\), \([x^s] F(x) = \frac{1}{s} [u^{s-1}] Q(u)^{-s}\) holds for every \(1 \le s < p\).
Failure Modes & Edge Cases: At \(s = 1\), a single leaf node is always valid (output \(1\)) regardless of whether \(D\) is empty; if \(1 \in D\) were allowed, unary chains of arbitrary length would make the number of trees with \(s\) leaves infinite and violate \([u^0] Q(u) = 1\).











Intermediate 2 (#227) — LOJ 6569: 仙人掌计数 (Labeled Cactus Enumeration for Single \(n\))

Source: LibreOJ 6569
Prerequisites: Husimi Cactus Functional Equation & Single-\(n\) LIF / D-Finite Recurrence (§12.2).


Problem Statement & Exact Constraints
Given a positive integer \(n\) and a prime modulus \(p\) (or \(p = 998244353\)), compute the number of labeled cactus graphs (connected simple undirected graphs in which every edge belongs to at most one simple cycle) on \(n\) vertices modulo \(p\).

Constraints: \(1 \le n \le 5 \times 10^5\) (up to \(10^7\) in the linear-time subtask), prime \(p > n\).
Required Complexity: \(O(n \log n)\) via LIF + polynomial \(\exp\), or \(O(n)\) time and \(O(1)\) auxiliary space via the 3-term D-finite recurrence / partial-fraction split!



Small Hand-Checkable Trace (\(n \le 4\))

\(n = 1\): \(\mathbf{1}\) (\(K_1\)).
\(n = 2\): \(\mathbf{1}\) (\(K_2\)).
\(n = 3\): \(\mathbf{4}\) (\(3\) labeled paths \(P_3\) + \(1\) triangle \(K_3\)).
\(n = 4\): \(\mathbf{31}\) (\(16\) trees + \(12\) unicyclic graphs with a triangle and a leaf + \(3\) four-cycles \(C_4\)).



Hint 1 — Diagnostic Signal & Combinatorial Model

Unlike #176 (which needed all \(n \le N\) to assemble disconnected deserts from connected cacti), here we only need the cactus count \(c_n\) for a single integer \(n\). Instead of running Newton Iteration for all degrees up to \(n\), can you extract the single \(n\)-th coefficient of the pointed cactus equation directly and then compute that single coefficient via a linear recurrence?



Hint 2 — Algebraic Setup & Reverse-Engineering Scratchpad

Applying Ch 11 LIF to the pointed cactus equation \(T(x) = x \phi(T(x))\) with \(\phi(u) = \exp\!\left(\frac{2u - u^2}{2(1 - u)}\right)\) gives: \[c_n = \frac{(n - 1)!}{n} [u^{n-1}] \exp\!\left(n \frac{2u - u^2}{2(1 - u)}\right).\] Can we compute \([u^{n-1}] \exp\!\left(n \frac{2u - u^2}{2(1 - u)}\right)\) in \(O(n)\) time without any NTT?



Hint 3 — Coefficient Extraction & Complexity Contract

Either split \(n \frac{2u - u^2}{2(1 - u)} = n u + \frac{n u^2}{2(1 - u)}\) and convolve \(e^{nu}\) with \(\exp\!\big(\frac{n u^2}{2(1 - u)}\big)\) at degree \(n - 1\) in \(O(n)\) time, or differentiate \(H(u) = \exp\!\left(n \frac{2u - u^2}{2(1 - u)}\right)\) to obtain the 3-term recurrence: \[a_m = \frac{1}{m}\left((2m - 2 + n) a_{m-1} - (m - 2 + n) a_{m-2} + \frac{n}{2} a_{m-3}\right).\]







NoteComplete Derivation & Solution






Step 1: Reducing to a Single Coefficient via Lagrange Inversion
Let \(c_n\) be the number of labeled cacti on \(n\) vertices, and \(T(x) = \sum_{n=1}^{\infty} n c_n \frac{x^n}{n!}\) be the pointed cactus EGF satisfying \(T(x) = x \phi(T(x))\) with \(\phi(u) = \exp\!\left(\frac{2u - u^2}{2(1 - u)}\right)\). By Ch 11 LIF: \[n c_n = n! [x^n] T(x) = (n - 1)! [u^{n-1}] \phi(u)^n \implies c_n = \frac{(n - 1)!}{n} [u^{n-1}] \exp\!\left(n \frac{2u - u^2}{2(1 - u)}\right).\]


Step 2: Deriving the \(O(n)\) 3-Term Recurrence (Zero NTTs)
Let \(H(u) = \exp\!\left(n \frac{2u - u^2}{2(1 - u)}\right) = \sum_{m=0}^{\infty} a_m u^m\) with \(a_0 = 1\). Differentiating \(H(u)\) with respect to \(u\): \[\begin{aligned}
H'(u)
&= H(u) \cdot \frac{d}{du}\left(n u + \frac{n u^2}{2(1 - u)}\right) \\
&= H(u) \cdot n \left(1 + \frac{2u(1 - u) + u^2}{2(1 - u)^2}\right) = H(u) \cdot n \frac{2 - 2u + u^2}{2(1 - u)^2}.
\end{aligned}\] Multiplying both sides by \(2(1 - u)^2 = 2 - 4u + 2u^2\) yields the polynomial ODE: \[(2 - 4u + 2u^2) H'(u) = n(2 - 2u + u^2) H(u).\] Extracting \([u^{m-1}]\) on both sides for \(m \ge 1\) (with \(a_{-1} = a_{-2} = 0\)): \[2 m a_m - 4(m - 1) a_{m-1} + 2(m - 2) a_{m-2} = 2 n a_{m-1} - 2 n a_{m-2} + n a_{m-3},\] which rearranges to: \[a_m = \frac{1}{m}\left((2m - 2 + n) a_{m-1} - (m - 2 + n) a_{m-2} + \frac{n}{2} a_{m-3}\right) \qquad (1 \le m \le n - 1).\]


Step 3: Alternative Closed-Form Sum via Partial-Fraction Split
Writing \(H(u) = e^{n u} \cdot \exp\!\left(\frac{n u^2}{2(1 - u)}\right)\) and expanding \(\exp\!\left(\frac{n u^2}{2(1 - u)}\right) = 1 + \sum_{k=1}^{\infty} \frac{(n/2)^k}{k!} u^{2k} (1 - u)^{-k}\) also gives a direct \(O(n)\) sum that does not even divide by \(n\) when we cancel \(n\) against the \(k \ge 1\) or \(e^{nu}\) terms: \[c_n = (n - 1)! \left( \frac{n^{n-2}}{(n - 1)!} + \sum_{m=2}^{n-1} \frac{n^{n - 1 - m}}{(n - 1 - m)!} \sum_{j=1}^{\lfloor m/2 \rfloor} \frac{n^{j-1}}{2^j \, j!} \binom{m - j - 1}{j - 1} \right).\]
// O(n) 3-term recurrence for cactus_n mod p
long long a0 = 1, a1 = 0, a2 = 0, inv2 = (p + 1) / 2;
for (int m = 1; m <= n - 1; ++m) {
    long long cur = ((2LL * m - 2 + n) % p * a0 - (m - 2LL + n) % p * a1 + p
                   + (n * inv2) % p * a2) % p * inv[m] % p;
    a2 = a1; a1 = a0; a0 = cur;
}
long long ans = a0 * fac[n - 1] % p * power(n, p - 2) % p;






NoteAlgorithm Contract




Input: Integer \(n \ge 1\) and prime modulus \(p > \max(n, 2)\).
Preconditions: \(1, 2, \dots, n\) are invertible modulo \(p\); \(a_0 = 1, a_{-1} = a_{-2} = 0\).
Postconditions: Outputs \(c_n = \frac{(n-1)!}{n} a_{n-1} \bmod p\), the exact number of labeled cacti on \(n\) vertices.
Time & Space Complexity: \(O(n)\) time and \(O(n)\) space using linear-sieve modular inverses inv[1..n-1] (or \(O(1)\) auxiliary space via the partial-fraction sum).
Core Invariant: At the end of iteration \(m \in [1, n-1]\), (a0, a1, a2) holds \((a_m, a_{m-1}, a_{m-2})\) where \(a_j = [u^j] \exp\!\big(n \frac{2u - u^2}{2(1 - u)}\big) \bmod p\).
Failure Mode & Characteristic-\(p\) Condition: Fails if \(p \le n\) (since both the D-finite division by \(m \in [1, n-1]\) and the Lagrange inversion factor \(1/n\) divide by zero modulo \(p\)), or if \(n = 1\) is not handled with the \(0\)-iteration base case \(a_0 = 1 \implies c_1 = 1\).

Advanced 1 (#190) — Luogu P6596: How Many of Them (Connected Graphs with \(\le m\) Bridges)

Source: Luogu P6596 / QOJ 5017
Prerequisites: Bridge-Block Trees & 2-Edge-Connected Graphs (§12.4), Generalized Cayley Component-Tree Formula (Ch 04.5).


Problem Statement & Exact Constraints
Given integers \(n\) and \(m\), compute the number of connected simple undirected labeled graphs on \(n\) vertices that contain at most \(m\) bridge edges (cut-edges), modulo \(10^9 + 7\) (for \(n \le 50\)) or modulo \(998244353\) (for \(n \le 2000\) / \(10^5\)).

Constraints: \(1 \le n \le 50\), \(0 \le m \le \binom{n}{2}\), modulus \(10^9 + 7\) (with arbitrary-size polynomial extension up to \(n \le 2000\)).
Required Complexity: \(O(n^3)\) (or \(O(n^2 \log n)\) via LIF + polynomial power) time and \(O(n^2)\) space.



Small Hand-Checkable Trace (\(n = 3, 4\))

\(n = 3\):

\(m = 0 \implies \mathbf{1}\) (only \(K_3\) is bridgeless).
\(m \ge 1 \implies \mathbf{4}\) (\(K_3\) plus the \(3\) labeled paths \(P_3\), each having \(2\) bridges; so \(m = 1 \implies \mathbf{1}\) and \(m \ge 2 \implies \mathbf{4}\)).

\(n = 4\):

\(m = 0 \implies \mathbf{10}\) (\(10\) 2-edge-connected graphs).
\(m = 1 \implies 10 + 12 = \mathbf{22}\) (adding \(12\) unicyclic graphs consisting of a triangle \(K_3\) with \(1\) pendant bridge leaf).
\(m = 2 \implies \mathbf{22}\) (no connected graph on \(4\) vertices has exactly \(2\) bridges).
\(m \ge 3 \implies 22 + 16 = \mathbf{38}\) (adding all \(16\) labeled trees on \(4\) vertices, each having \(3\) bridges).




Hint 1 — Diagnostic Signal & Combinatorial Model

Deleting all \(b = k - 1\) bridge edges of a connected graph on \(n\) vertices decomposes it into \(k\) disjoint 2-edge-connected components of sizes \(s_1 + \dots + s_k = n\) connected by \(k - 1\) bridge edges into a tree of components.



Hint 2 — Algebraic Setup & Reverse-Engineering Scratchpad

First, find the number of 2-edge-connected graphs \(e_{2,s}\) for every \(1 \le s \le n\) using the Bridge-Block LIF formula from Section 12.4: \[e_{2,1} = 1, \qquad e_{2,s} = -\frac{(s - 1)!}{s} [x^s] \exp\!\big(-s x C'(x)\big) \quad (2 \le s \le n).\] Next, form the vertex-pointed 2-ECC generating function \(E(z) = \sum_{s=1}^{n} s \, e_{2,s} \frac{z^s}{s!}\).



Hint 3 — Coefficient Extraction & Complexity Contract

By the Generalized Cayley Formula (Ch 04.5), \(k\) components of sizes \(s_1, \dots, s_k\) (\(\sum s_i = n\)) can be linked by \(k - 1\) bridge edges into a tree of components in \(n^{k-2} \prod_{i=1}^k s_i\) ways. Thus the number of connected graphs on \(n\) vertices with exact \(k - 1\) bridges is \(\frac{n!}{k!} n^{k-2} [z^n] E(z)^k\). Sum this over \(k = 1, 2, \dots, \min(n, m + 1)\)!







NoteComplete Derivation & Solution






Step 1: Computing Connected Graphs \(c_s\) and Pointed Connected Graphs \(R(x) = x C'(x)\)
Let \(G(x) = \sum_{s=0}^{n} 2^{\binom{s}{2}} \frac{x^s}{s!}\) be the EGF of all simple labeled graphs, and \(C(x) = \ln G(x) = \sum_{s=1}^{n} c_s \frac{x^s}{s!}\) be the EGF of connected simple labeled graphs. (Under \(10^9 + 7\) with \(n \le 50\), \(\ln\) and \(\exp\) of truncated power series up to degree \(n\) are computed directly via the \(O(n^2)\) recurrence \([x^s] \ln G(x) = [x^s] G(x) - \frac{1}{s} \sum_{j=1}^{s-1} j [x^j]\ln G(x) \cdot [x^{s-j}]G(x)\) from Ch 02.4 without needing an NTT prime!)
Let \(R(x) = x C'(x) = \sum_{s=1}^{n} s \, c_s \frac{x^s}{s!}\).


Step 2: Extracting 2-Edge-Connected Counts \(e_{2,s}\) for \(1 \le s \le n\)
By the Bridge-Block Functional Equation \(E\big(x e^{R(x)}\big) = R(x)\) and its LIF inversion (Section 12.4): \[e_{2,1} = 1, \qquad e_{2,s} = -\frac{(s - 1)!}{s} [x^s] \exp\!\big(-s R(x)\big) \qquad (2 \le s \le n).\] Computing \(\exp(-s R(x)) \bmod x^{s+1}\) in \(O(s^2)\) time for each \(s = 2, \dots, n\) yields all \(e_{2,1}, \dots, e_{2,n}\) in \(O(n^3)\) total time.


Step 3: Gluing \(k\) 2-Edge-Connected Components via the Generalized Cayley Formula
A connected graph on \(n\) vertices with \(b = k - 1\) bridge edges consists of an unordered set of \(k\) 2-edge-connected components of sizes \(s_1, \dots, s_k \ge 1\) (\(s_1 + \dots + s_k = n\)), together with \(k - 1\) bridge edges forming a tree on those \(k\) components. By the Generalized Cayley Formula (Ch 04.5), for fixed component vertex sets of sizes \(s_1, \dots, s_k\), there are \(n^{k-2} \prod_{i=1}^k s_i\) ways to choose the \(k - 1\) bridge edges (where for \(k = 1\), \(n^{-1} s_1 = n^{-1} n = 1\)).
Defining the pointed 2-ECC generating function \[E(z) = \sum_{s=1}^{n} s \, e_{2,s} \frac{z^s}{s!},\] the coefficient \(n! [z^n] \frac{E(z)^k}{k!}\) sums \(\prod_{i=1}^k \big(s_i \, e_{2,s_i}\big)\) over all unordered partitions of \(\{1, \dots, n\}\) into \(k\) parts. Multiplying by \(n^{k-2}\) and summing over \(1 \le k \le \min(n, m + 1)\) gives the final answer: \[\text{Total}(\le m \text{ bridges}) = \sum_{k=1}^{\min(n, m+1)} \frac{n!}{k!} \, n^{k-2} \, [z^n] E(z)^k \pmod{10^9 + 7}.\]






NoteAlgorithm Contract




Input: Integers \(n \ge 1\), \(m \ge 0\), and prime modulus \(p = 10^9 + 7\).
Preconditions: \(p > n\); \([x^0] G(x) = 1\) and \([x^0] \exp(-s R(x)) = 1\) for all \(1 \le s \le n\).
Postconditions: Outputs \(\sum_{k=1}^{\min(n, m+1)} \frac{n!}{k!} n^{k-2} [z^n] E(z)^k \bmod p\) (with boundary check \(m \ge n - 1 \implies c_n\)).
Time & Space Complexity: \(O(n^3)\) time under arbitrary prime modulus (or \(O(n^2 \log n)\) with NTT) and \(O(n^2)\) space.
Core Invariant: For each \(k \in [1, n]\), \(\frac{n!}{k!} n^{k-2} [z^n] E(z)^k\) equals the exact number of connected labeled graphs on \(n\) vertices with \(k - 1\) bridge edges.
Failure Mode & Characteristic-\(p\) Condition: Fails if \(p \le n\) (since \(k!\), \(n\), and \(n - k\) in \(\frac{k}{n - k}\) hit division by zero modulo \(p\)), or if \(k = 1\) is not weighted by \(n^{1-2} \equiv n^{-1} \pmod p\) in the Cayley bridge-tree factor \(n^{k-2}\).











Advanced 2 (#016) — AtCoder fps_24_w: Biconnected Graphs

Source: AtCoder FPS 24-Problem Set — Task W
Prerequisites: Tutte’s Block-Cut Tree Equation \(\ln\frac{R(x)}{x} = B'(R(x))\) & Single-\(n\) Log-Free LIF (§12.3).


Problem Statement & Exact Constraints
A connected simple undirected graph on \(N\) labeled vertices is called biconnected (or 2-vertex-connected) if it contains no articulation points (no vertex whose removal disconnects the graph; in particular, the single-vertex graph \(K_1\) and single-edge graph \(K_2\) have no articulation points, while for \(N \ge 3\) biconnectivity requires at least two internally vertex-disjoint paths between every pair of vertices). Given \(N\), compute the number of labeled biconnected simple undirected graphs on \(N\) vertices modulo \(998244353\).

Constraints: \(1 \le N \le 2 \times 10^5\) (or \(1 \le n \le N \le 5000\) in the all-\(n\) small-\(N\) variant), modulus \(p = 998244353\).
Required Complexity: \(O(N \log N)\) time for a single \(N\) via Log-Free LIF (or \(O(N^2)\) for all \(n \le N \le 5000\); simultaneous all-\(n\) for \(N \le 2 \times 10^5\) in \(O(N \log^2 N)\) is covered in Ch 21.4).



Small Hand-Checkable Trace (\(N \le 4\))

\(N = 1\): \(\mathbf{1}\) (\(K_1\)).
\(N = 2\): \(\mathbf{1}\) (\(K_2\)).
\(N = 3\): \(\mathbf{1}\) (\(K_3\)).
\(N = 4\): \(\mathbf{10}\) (\(1\) copy of \(K_4\), \(6\) copies of \(K_4 - e\), and \(3\) four-cycles \(C_4\)).



Hint 1 — Diagnostic Signal & Combinatorial Model

Every connected graph decomposes across its articulation points (cut-vertices) into a tree of maximal biconnected subgraphs (blocks). If we distinguish a root vertex \(r\) in a connected graph, how do the biconnected blocks containing \(r\) and the remaining connected pieces attached to their non-root vertices fit together?



Hint 2 — Algebraic Setup & Reverse-Engineering Scratchpad

Let \(G(x) = \sum_{k=0}^{N} 2^{\binom{k}{2}} \frac{x^k}{k!}\), \(C(x) = \ln G(x)\), and \(R(x) = x C'(x)\). In the block-cut tree, the root \(r\) belongs to an unordered set (\(\exp\)) of biconnected blocks incident to \(r\), where each non-root vertex in a block roots an independent pointed connected graph \(R(x)\): \[R(x) = x \exp\!\Big(B'\big(R(x)\big)\Big) \iff B'\big(R(x)\big) = \ln\frac{R(x)}{x} = \ln C'(x).\]



Hint 3 — Coefficient Extraction & Complexity Contract

Apply Ch 11 Lagrange Inversion to \(B'(R(x)) = \ln C'(x)\) and integrate by parts (Section 12.3) to obtain the log-free single-\(N\) formula: \[b_N = -(N - 2)! [x^{N-1}] \Big( C'(x)^{-(N-1)} \Big) \qquad (N \ge 2).\] If all \(b_2, \dots, b_N\) are required for \(N \le 5000\), unroll \(H(x) = \ln C'(x) = \sum_{k=1}^{N-1} \frac{b_{k+1}}{k!} R(x)^k\) in \(O(N^2)\) time!







NoteComplete Derivation & Solution






Step 1: Connected Graph EGF and Pointed Derivative \(C'(x)\)
Construct \(G(x) = \sum_{k=0}^{N} 2^{\binom{k}{2}} \frac{x^k}{k!} \bmod x^{N+1}\) and compute \(C(x) = \ln G(x) \bmod x^{N+1}\) in \(O(N \log N)\) time. Differentiating gives: \[C'(x) = \frac{R(x)}{x} = \sum_{k=0}^{N-1} c_{k+1} \frac{x^k}{k!} \bmod x^N, \qquad [x^0] C'(x) = c_1 = 1.\]


Step 2: Method A — Single-\(N\) Extraction in \(O(N \log N)\) Time
For \(N = 1\), output \(1\) (\(K_1\)) and for \(N = 2\), output \(b_2 = 1\) (\(K_2\)). For \(N \ge 2\), by Section 12.3: \[\begin{aligned}
b_N
&= (N - 1)! [u^{N-1}] B'(u) \\
&= (N - 2)! [x^{N-2}] \left( \frac{C''(x)}{C'(x)} \cdot C'(x)^{-(N-1)} \right) \\
&= -(N - 2)! [x^{N-1}] \Big( C'(x)^{-(N-1)} \Big) \\
&= -(N - 2)! [x^{N-1}] \exp\!\Big(-(N - 1) \ln C'(x)\Big).
\end{aligned}\] This requires only one polynomial \(\ln\) of \(G(x)\) (degree \(N\)), one polynomial \(\ln\) of \(C'(x)\) (degree \(N - 1\)), and one polynomial \(\exp\) (degree \(N - 1\)).


Step 3: Method B — All-\(n\) Extraction for \(N \le 5000\) via \(O(N^2)\) Substitution Elimination
To extract \(b_2, b_3, \dots, b_N\) for all \(n \le N \le 5000\) using only Ch 01–Ch 12 tools, let \(H(x) = \ln C'(x) \bmod x^N\) and \(R(x) = x C'(x) \bmod x^N\). Since \(H(x) = B'(R(x)) = \sum_{k=1}^{N-1} \big([u^k] B'(u)\big) R(x)^k\) and \(\operatorname{val}(R(x)) = 1\), at step \(k = 1, 2, \dots, N - 1\):

Read off \([u^k] B'(u) = [x^k] H(x)\), so \(b_{k+1} = k! [x^k] H(x)\).
Subtract \(([u^k] B'(u)) \cdot R(x)^k\) from \(H(x)\) in \(O(N - k)\) operations, and advance \(R(x)^k \to R(x)^{k+1} \bmod x^N\).







NoteAlgorithm Contract




Input: Integer \(N \ge 1\) and prime modulus \(p = 998244353\).
Preconditions: \(p > N\); \([x^0] G(x) = 1\) and \([x^0] C'(x) = 1\).
Postconditions: Outputs \(b_N \bmod p\), the exact number of labeled biconnected simple undirected graphs on \(N\) vertices (with \(b_1 = 1, b_2 = 1\)).
Time & Space Complexity: \(O(N \log N)\) time for single \(N\) (or \(O(N^2)\) time for all \(n \le N \le 5000\)) and \(O(N)\) space.
Core Invariant: Under \(u = R(x) = x C'(x)\), \([u^{N-1}] B'(u) = -\frac{1}{N-1} [x^{N-1}] \big(C'(x)^{-(N-1)}\big)\) holds for all \(2 \le N < p\).
Failure Mode & Characteristic-\(p\) Condition: Fails if \(p \le N\) (since \(N!\) in \(G(x)\) and \(1/(N-1)\) in the Lagrange inversion formula divide by zero modulo \(p\)), or if \(N = 1\) is passed into the \(1/(N-1)\) inversion formula without an explicit base-case guard.












Tier 4: Mastery (Mas-1, Mas-2)


Mastery 1 (#183) — Luogu P5827: 点双连通图计数 (Vertex-Biconnected Labeled Graphs)

Source: Luogu P5827
Prerequisites: Tutte’s Block-Cut Tree Equation & Log-Free Single-\(n\) Formula (§12.3), Formal Residue Integration by Parts (Ch 11.1).


Problem Statement & Exact Constraints
Given a positive integer \(n\), compute the number of simple undirected 2-vertex-connected (biconnected) labeled graphs on \(n\) vertices (connected graphs with no articulation points / cut-vertices) modulo \(998244353\).

Constraints: \(1 \le n \le 2 \times 10^5\), modulus \(p = 998244353\). (Note: for \(n = 1\), \(K_1\) has no cut-vertices so output \(1\); for \(n = 2\), \(K_2\) has no cut-vertices so output \(1\).)
Required Complexity: \(O(n \log n)\) time and \(O(n)\) space.



Small Hand-Checkable Trace (\(n \le 5\))

\(n = 1\): \(\mathbf{1}\) (\(K_1\)).
\(n = 2\): \(\mathbf{1}\) (\(K_2\)).
\(n = 3\): \(\mathbf{1}\) (\(K_3\)).
\(n = 4\): \(\mathbf{10}\) (\(1\) copy of \(K_4\), \(6\) copies of \(K_4 - e\), and \(3\) four-cycles \(C_4\)).
\(n = 5\): \(\mathbf{238}\).



Hint 1 — Diagnostic Signal & Combinatorial Model

We need the single count \(b_n\) at \(n \le 2 \times 10^5\) in \(O(n \log n)\) time without full polynomial composition inversion. If you root a connected graph at a vertex \(r\), how does \(r\) sit inside the biconnected blocks incident to \(r\), and what is attached to each non-root vertex of those blocks?



Hint 2 — Algebraic Setup & Reverse-Engineering Scratchpad

By Tutte’s Block-Cut Tree decomposition, the vertex-pointed connected EGF \(R(x) = x C'(x)\) satisfies \(R(x) = x \exp\!\big(B'(R(x))\big)\), where \(C(x) = \ln\!\left(\sum_{k=0}^{n} 2^{\binom{k}{2}} \frac{x^k}{k!}\right)\). Taking logarithms gives \(B'\big(x C'(x)\big) = \ln C'(x)\). Applying Ch 11 Lagrange Inversion to extract \([u^{n-1}] B'(u)\) with \(u = x C'(x)\) gives: \[[u^{n-1}] B'(u) = \frac{1}{n - 1} [x^{n-2}] \left( \big(\ln C'(x)\big)' \cdot C'(x)^{-(n-1)} \right).\]



Hint 3 — Coefficient Extraction & Complexity Contract

Notice that \(\big(\ln C'(x)\big)' \cdot C'(x)^{-(n-1)} = C''(x) C'(x)^{-n} = -\frac{1}{n-1} \frac{d}{dx}\big(C'(x)^{-(n-1)}\big)\). Using \([x^{n-2}] F'(x) = (n-1)[x^{n-1}] F(x)\) eliminates the outer logarithm and derivative completely, yielding \(b_n = -(n-2)! [x^{n-1}] \big(C'(x)^{-(n-1)}\big)\) for \(n \ge 2\)!







NoteComplete Derivation & Solution






Step 1: From All Graphs to Pointed Connected Graphs
Let \(G(x) = \sum_{k=0}^{n} 2^{\binom{k}{2}} \frac{x^k}{k!} \bmod x^{n+1}\) be the EGF of all simple labeled graphs on at most \(n\) vertices. By the Exp–Log Connected Component Bridge (Ch 04.3), the EGF of connected labeled graphs is: \[C(x) = \ln G(x) = \sum_{k=1}^{n} c_k \frac{x^k}{k!} \pmod{x^{n+1}}.\] Pointing a connected graph at a root vertex \(r\) multiplies the \(k\)-th coefficient by \(k\), giving \(R(x) = x C'(x)\), where: \[C'(x) = \frac{R(x)}{x} = \sum_{k=0}^{n-1} c_{k+1} \frac{x^k}{k!} \pmod{x^n}.\]


Step 2: Block-Cut Tree Equation and Formal Residue Extraction
For \(n = 1\), a single vertex \(K_1\) has no cut-vertices (\(b_1 = 1\)). For \(n \ge 2\), let \(B(u) = \sum_{k=2}^{\infty} b_k \frac{u^k}{k!}\) be the EGF of biconnected blocks. In any vertex-pointed connected graph \((G, r)\), the root \(r\) belongs to an unordered set of blocks incident to \(r\), and each of the \(k - 1\) non-root vertices in a block of size \(k\) roots an independent pointed connected graph \(u = R(x) = x C'(x)\): \[R(x) = x \exp\!\Big(B'\big(R(x)\big)\Big) \iff B'\big(x C'(x)\big) = \ln C'(x).\] Let \(u = R(x) = x C'(x)\). For \(n \ge 2\), by the Formal Residue Change-of-Variables Theorem (Ch 11.1): \[\begin{aligned}
[u^{n-1}] B'(u)
&= \frac{1}{n - 1} \operatorname{Res}_u \, B''(u) u^{-(n-1)} = \frac{1}{n - 1} \operatorname{Res}_x \, \frac{d}{dx}\Big(B'\big(R(x)\big)\Big) R(x)^{-(n-1)} \\
&= \frac{1}{n - 1} [x^{n-2}] \left( \frac{d}{dx}\big(\ln C'(x)\big) \cdot C'(x)^{-(n-1)} \right) \\
&= \frac{1}{n - 1} [x^{n-2}] \Big( C''(x) \, C'(x)^{-n} \Big) \\
&= -\frac{1}{(n - 1)^2} [x^{n-2}] \frac{d}{dx}\Big( C'(x)^{-(n-1)} \Big) \\
&= -\frac{1}{n - 1} [x^{n-1}] \Big( C'(x)^{-(n-1)} \Big).
\end{aligned}\] Multiplying by \((n - 1)!\) gives the exact count of biconnected labeled graphs on \(n \ge 2\) vertices: \[b_n = (n - 1)! [u^{n-1}] B'(u) = -(n - 2)! [x^{n-1}] \exp\!\Big(-(n - 1) \ln C'(x)\Big) \pmod{998244353}.\]
// O(n log n) Single-n Biconnected Graph Extraction (Luogu P5827)
if (n == 1) return 1;
Poly G(n + 1);
for (int k = 0; k <= n; ++k)
    G[k] = power(2, 1LL * k * (k - 1) / 2 % (MOD - 1)) * ifac[k] % MOD;
Poly C_prime = G.Ln(n + 1).Deriv(); // C'(x) of degree n - 1, [x^0]C'(x) = 1
Poly P = (C_prime.Ln(n) * (MOD - (n - 1))).Exp(n); // C'(x)^{-(n-1)} mod x^n
long long ans = (MOD - fac[n - 2]) * P[n - 1] % MOD;






NoteAlgorithm Contract




Input: Integer \(n \in [1, 2 \times 10^5]\) and prime modulus \(p = 998244353\).
Preconditions: \(p > n\); \([x^0] G(x) = 1\) and \([x^0] C'(x) = 1\).
Postconditions: Outputs \(b_n \bmod p\), the exact number of labeled 2-vertex-connected graphs on \(n\) vertices (with boundary check \(n = 1 \implies 1\)).
Time & Space Complexity: \(O(n \log n)\) time (2 polynomial \(\ln\) calls and 1 polynomial \(\exp\) call of degree \(n\)) and \(O(n)\) space.
Core Invariant: Formal residue integration by parts reduces \(\operatorname{Res}_x (\ln C'(x))' R(x)^{-(n-1)}\) to \(-(n-1) [x^{n-1}] \big(C'(x)^{-(n-1)}\big)\) for all \(2 \le n < p\).
Failure Mode & Characteristic-\(p\) Condition: Fails if \(p \le n\) (since \(n!\), \(1/(n-1)\), and the formal integration steps inside \(\ln\) and \(\exp\) up to degree \(n\) divide by zero modulo \(p\)), or if \(C'(x)\) is not truncated to degree \(n - 1\) before taking \(\ln C'(x)\).











Mastery 2 (#184) — Luogu P5828: 边双连通图计数 (2-Edge-Connected Labeled Graphs)

Source: Luogu P5828
Prerequisites: Bridge-Block Functional Equation \(E(x e^{R(x)}) = R(x)\) & Derivative-Free Single-\(n\) LIF (§12.4).


Problem Statement & Exact Constraints
Given a positive integer \(n\), compute the number of simple undirected 2-edge-connected (bridgeless) labeled graphs on \(n\) vertices (connected graphs with no bridge edges / cut-edges) modulo \(998244353\).

Constraints: \(1 \le n \le 2 \times 10^5\), modulus \(p = 998244353\). (Note: for \(n = 1\), \(K_1\) has \(0\) edges and thus \(0\) bridges, so \(e_{2,1} = 1\); for \(n = 2\), \(K_2\) is a single bridge, so \(e_{2,2} = 0\).)
Required Complexity: \(O(n \log n)\) time and \(O(n)\) space.



Small Hand-Checkable Trace (\(n \le 5\))

\(n = 1\): \(\mathbf{1}\) (\(K_1\) has \(0\) bridges).
\(n = 2\): \(\mathbf{0}\) (\(K_2\) is a bridge).
\(n = 3\): \(\mathbf{1}\) (\(K_3\)).
\(n = 4\): \(\mathbf{10}\) (same as biconnected graphs for \(n = 4\)).
\(n = 5\): \(\mathbf{253}\) (\(238\) biconnected graphs plus \(\binom{5}{1} \cdot \frac{1}{2}\binom{4}{2} = 15\) “bowtie” graphs consisting of two triangles sharing a single cut-vertex, which has no bridge edges!).



Hint 1 — Diagnostic Signal & Combinatorial Model

Contracting every 2-edge-connected component of a connected graph into a super-vertex turns the bridge edges into a tree of 2-ECCs. If we distinguish a root vertex \(r\), it belongs to a unique root 2-ECC \(H_0\); what hangs off each vertex \(v \in V(H_0)\) across the bridge edges incident to \(v\)?



Hint 2 — Algebraic Setup & Reverse-Engineering Scratchpad

Every vertex \(v \in V(H_0)\) (including \(r\)) sprouts an unordered set (\(\exp\)) of bridge edges leading to pointed connected components \(R(x) = x C'(x)\). Let \(E(z) = z B'_{\text{2-edge}}(z) = \sum_{k=1}^{\infty} k \, e_{2,k} \frac{z^k}{k!}\) be the EGF of vertex-pointed 2-edge-connected graphs. Replacing every vertex \(z\) of the root 2-ECC by \(W(x) = x \exp(R(x))\) yields: \[E\big(W(x)\big) = R(x), \qquad W(x) = x \exp\!\big(R(x)\big) = x \exp\!\big(x C'(x)\big).\]



Hint 3 — Coefficient Extraction & Complexity Contract

Applying Ch 11 LIF to \(E(W(x)) = R(x)\) and integrating by parts for \(n \ge 2\) gives: \[[z^n] E(z) = \frac{1}{n} [x^{n-1}] \Big( R'(x) \exp\!\big(-n R(x)\big) \Big) = -\frac{1}{n} [x^n] \exp\!\big(-n R(x)\big).\] Multiply by \((n - 1)!\) to obtain \(e_{2,n} = -\frac{(n - 1)!}{n} [x^n] \exp\!\big(-n x C'(x)\big)\) in \(O(n \log n)\) time!







NoteComplete Derivation & Solution






Step 1: Pointed Connected Graph EGF \(R(x) = x C'(x)\)
As in #183, form \(G(x) = \sum_{k=0}^{n} 2^{\binom{k}{2}} \frac{x^k}{k!} \bmod x^{n+1}\), compute \(C(x) = \ln G(x) \bmod x^{n+1}\) in \(O(n \log n)\) time, and apply the pointing operator \(\Theta = x D_x\) to obtain: \[R(x) = x C'(x) = \sum_{k=1}^{n} k \, c_k \frac{x^k}{k!} \pmod{x^{n+1}}.\]


Step 2: Bridge-Block Substitution and LIF Extraction
For \(n = 1\), output \(e_{2,1} = 1\). For \(n \ge 2\), let \(E(z) = \sum_{k=1}^{\infty} k \, e_{2,k} \frac{z^k}{k!}\) be the EGF of vertex-pointed 2-edge-connected graphs. By Section 12.4, \(E(W(x)) = R(x)\) where \(W(x) = x \exp(R(x))\).
Applying Ch 11 Inverse Lagrange Inversion (Form 2) with \(\phi(x) = \frac{x}{W(x)} = \exp(-R(x))\): \[\begin{aligned}
[z^n] E(z)
&= \frac{1}{n} [x^{n-1}] \left( R'(x) \left(\frac{x}{W(x)}\right)^n \right) \\
&= \frac{1}{n} [x^{n-1}] \Big( R'(x) \exp\!\big(-n R(x)\big) \Big) \\
&= -\frac{1}{n^2} [x^{n-1}] \frac{d}{dx}\Big( \exp\!\big(-n R(x)\big) \Big) \\
&= -\frac{1}{n} [x^n] \exp\!\big(-n R(x)\big).
\end{aligned}\] Since \([z^n] E(z) = \frac{n \, e_{2,n}}{n!} = \frac{e_{2,n}}{(n - 1)!}\), multiplying both sides by \((n - 1)!\) yields the exact count of 2-edge-connected labeled graphs on \(n \ge 2\) vertices: \[e_{2,n} = -\frac{(n - 1)!}{n} [x^n] \exp\!\big(-n R(x)\big) = -\frac{(n - 1)!}{n} [x^n] \exp\!\big(-n x C'(x)\big) \pmod{998244353}.\]
// O(n log n) Single-n 2-Edge-Connected Graph Extraction (Luogu P5828)
if (n == 1) return 1;
Poly G(n + 1);
for (int k = 0; k <= n; ++k)
    G[k] = power(2, 1LL * k * (k - 1) / 2 % (MOD - 1)) * ifac[k] % MOD;
Poly R = G.Ln(n + 1);
for (int k = 0; k <= n; ++k) R[k] = R[k] * k % MOD; // R(x) = x C'(x)
Poly P = (R * (MOD - n)).Exp(n + 1);                // exp(-n R(x)) mod x^{n+1}
long long ans = (MOD - fac[n - 1]) * inv[n] % MOD * P[n] % MOD;






NoteAlgorithm Contract




Input: Integer \(n \in [1, 2 \times 10^5]\) and prime modulus \(p = 998244353\).
Preconditions: \(p > n\); \([x^0] G(x) = 1\) and \([x^0] R(x) = 0\).
Postconditions: Outputs \(e_{2,n} \bmod p\), the exact number of labeled 2-edge-connected graphs on \(n\) vertices (with boundary check \(n = 1 \implies 1, n = 2 \implies 0\)).
Time & Space Complexity: \(O(n \log n)\) time (1 polynomial \(\ln\) call and 1 polynomial \(\exp\) call of degree \(n\)) and \(O(n)\) space.
Core Invariant: Under \(z = W(x) = x \exp(R(x))\), \([z^n] E(z) = -\frac{1}{n} [x^n] \exp(-n R(x))\) holds for all \(2 \le n < p\).
Failure Mode & Characteristic-\(p\) Condition: Fails if \(p \le n\) (since \(n!\), \(1/n\), and the formal integration steps inside \(\ln\) and \(\exp\) up to degree \(n\) divide by zero modulo \(p\)), or if \(n = 1\) is evaluated via \(-\frac{1}{1}[x^1]\exp(-R(x)) = 1\) without accounting for the bridge-tree sign convention (which holds only for \(n \ge 2\)).

title: 14 — Probability Generating Functions, Renewal Stopping Times, Poissonization & Martingales
text:
In Chapters 01 through 13, our generating functions encoded deterministic enumeration sequences: \([x^n]A(x)\) counted unlabeled structures of size \(n\), and \(n!\,[x^n]\widehat{A}(x)\) counted labeled structures on \(n\) vertices. In this chapter we open Part IV (Probabilistic Generating Functions, Lattice Walks & Multivariate Series) by turning the formal power series ring \(K[[z]]\) into an algebraic engine for stochastic processes and random stopping times.
When a random process evolves step by step—tossing biased coins until one of \(m\) competing patterns appears, drawing coupons with multiplicity thresholds \(B_i\), flipping random switches on a hypercube until a target state is reached, or redistributing tokens among \(n\) piles until one player holds everything—computing the expected stopping time \(\mathbb{E}[T]\), its variance \(\operatorname{Var}(T)\), or the winning probabilities \(P_i\) via state-space Gaussian elimination often requires \(O(V^3)\) time over an exponentially large state space. Probabilistic Generating Functions (PGFs) collapse these infinite-horizon Markov chains into compact polynomial and exponential equations where \(\mathbb{E}[T]\) and \(\operatorname{Var}(T)\) are extracted by algebraic behavior at \(z = 1\).

Learning Objectives
By the end of this chapter, you will be able to:

Formulate Stopping-Time & Survival PGFs (§14.1): Construct the stopping-time PGF \(F(z) = \mathbb{E}[z^T] = \sum_{n \ge 0} \mathbb{P}(T = n)z^n\) and the survival (tail) generating function \(G(z) = \sum_{n \ge 0} \mathbb{P}(T > n)z^n\), derive the Stopping-Time Conservation Identity \(F(z) + (1 - z)G(z) = 1\), and extract falling factorial moments \(\mathbb{E}[T^{\underline{k}}] = F^{(k)}(1) = k G^{(k-1)}(1)\), ordinary moments \(\mathbb{E}[T^k] = [(\vartheta_z)^k F(z)]_{z=1}\), and variance \(\operatorname{Var}(T) = 2G'(1) + G(1) - G(1)^2\).
Eliminate \(0/0\) Indeterminate Forms via Formal Taylor Shift in \(K[t]/(t^3)\) (§14.2): Replace error-prone quotient-rule and L’Hôpital differentiations of rational PGFs \(F(z) = P(z)/Q(z)\) at \(z = 1\) with the Formal Jet Substitution \(z = 1 + t \bmod t^3\), factoring out the common valuation \(t^v\) (\(v = \operatorname{val}_t Q(1+t)\)) and inverting in \(K[t]/(t^3)\) in \(O(1)\) operations.
Execute First-Passage Renewal Deconvolution & Continuous-Time Poissonization (§14.3): Convert unconstrained visit generating functions \(H_{u \to v}(z)\) into first-passage PGFs \(F_{u \to v}(z) = H_{u \to v}(z) / H_{v \to v}(z)\), cancel the stationary simple pole at \(z = 1\) by multiplying numerator and denominator by \((1 - z)\), bridge coordinate-wise EGFs to OGFs via the Borel–Laplace Transform \(\mathcal{B}[e^{\lambda z}] = \frac{1}{1 - \lambda x}\), and pair Min–Max Inclusion–Exclusion (Ch 08) with Poissonized truncated exponential EGFs \(\sum_{c < B_i} \frac{(p_i t)^c}{c!}\).
Master the Singing Kingdom KMP Border Theorem & Penney’s Game Correlation Systems (§14.4): Derive the exact polynomial relation between \(G(z)\) and \(F(z)\) by forcibly appending a target pattern \(S\) to surviving runs, extract \(\mathbb{E}[T]\) and \(\operatorname{Var}(T)\) over the KMP border chain \(\operatorname{Borders}(S)\) in \(O(L)\) time, and solve multi-pattern competing stopping games in \(O(m^2 L + m^3)\) via the Guibas–Odlyzko correlation matrix.
Deploy Martingale Optional Stopping & Separable Potential Drift Duality (§14.4): Re-derive string stopping times via Li’s fair-casino martingale and Doob’s Optional Stopping Theorem, construct additively separable potentials \(\Phi(a_1, \dots, a_n) = \sum_{i=1}^n f(a_i)\) with unit drift \(\mathbb{E}[\Delta \Phi \mid X_t] = -1\) for symmetric multi-pile processes, reduce the resulting tridiagonal balance equations to first-difference recurrences \(g(x) = f(x+1) - f(x)\), and connect \(\phi_u = -\widetilde{H}'_{u \to t}(1)\) to the Poisson drift equation \((I - P)\phi = e_t - \pi_t \mathbf{1}\).







ImportantPrerequisite Map (Ch 04, Ch 05, Ch 06, Ch 08)



This chapter builds directly on four foundational modules from Parts I and II:

Chapter 04: Labeled Symbolic Method & EGFs: Exponential generating functions \(\widehat{A}(z) = \sum_{n \ge 0} a_n \frac{z^n}{n!}\), independent labeled tuple products, and the hyperbolic parity filters \(\cosh(z) = \frac{e^z + e^{-z}}{2}\) and \(\sinh(z) = \frac{e^z - e^{-z}}{2}\).
Chapter 05: Rational GFs, Euclidean Division & Bostan–Mori: Rational power series \(P(z)/Q(z) \in K(z)\), transfer-matrix resolvents \((I - zT)^{-1}\), and partial-fraction decompositions.
Chapter 06: Binomial Sums, Stirling Numbers & Taylor Shift: Converting between falling factorials \(n^{\underline{k}}\) and ordinary powers \(n^k\) via Stirling numbers of the second kind \(\left\{\begin{matrix} k \\ j \end{matrix}\right\}\), and the \(O(N \log N)\) polynomial Taylor Shift \(P(z) \mapsto P(1 + t)\).
Chapter 08: Sieve & Inclusion–Exclusion Engine: Subset Inclusion–Exclusion, Min–Max Inversion \(\max_{i \in S} T_i = \sum_{\emptyset \neq T \subseteq S} (-1)^{|T|-1} \min_{i \in T} T_i\), and the Goulden–Jackson cluster overlap polynomial.
