title: Chapter 24: Non-Cauchy Algebras: Bitwise FWT, Set Power Series (\(\mathcal{R}_n = K[\mathbf{x}]/(\mathbf{x}^2)\)) & The Dirichlet Ring (\(\mathcal{D}_f\))
section: 24.4 The Ring of Dirichlet Series \(\mathcal{D}_f\), Bell Series & The \(\Omega(n)\)-Derivation
text:
24.4 The Ring of Dirichlet Series \(\mathcal{D}_f\), Bell Series & The \(\Omega(n)\)-Derivation
Our third non-Cauchy algebra replaces \(x^i \cdot x^j = x^{i+j}\) with integer multiplication of indices \(n^{-s} \cdot m^{-s} = (nm)^{-s}\). A formal Dirichlet Generating Function (DGF) is a formal series
\[
F(s) = \sum_{n=1}^{\infty} \frac{f(n)}{n^s} \in \mathcal{D}_f,
\]
equipped with Dirichlet convolution:
\[
(f *_D g)(n) = \sum_{d \mid n} f(d) \, g\!\left(\frac{n}{d}\right).
\]
The multiplicative identity is \(\varepsilon(n) = [n = 1]\), and a series \(f \in \mathcal{D}_f\) is invertible (\(f \in \mathcal{D}_f^\times\)) if and only if \(f(1) \in K^\times\). By enumerating pairs \((d, k)\) with \(dk \le N\), a single Dirichlet convolution or inversion up to \(N\) takes \(\sum_{d=1}^N \lfloor N/d \rfloor = O(N \log N)\) time.

Algebraic Isomorphism with \(\mathcal{R}_n\) & Bell Series for Multiplicative Functions
By the Fundamental Theorem of Arithmetic, every integer \(n = p_1^{e_1} p_2^{e_2} \cdots p_k^{e_k}\) corresponds to a monomial \(\prod_i x_{p_i}^{e_i}\) in infinitely many prime variables \(x_2, x_3, x_5, \dots\):

Square-Free Restriction: If we restrict \(f(n)\) to square-free integers (\(\mu(n) \neq 0\)) on the first \(n\) primes, then \(x_{p_i}^2 = 0\) and Dirichlet convolution becomes isomorphic to the Set Power Series ring \(\mathcal{R}_n\)!
Multiplicative Functions & Bell Series: When \(f\) is multiplicative (\(f(mn) = f(m)f(n)\) for \(\gcd(m, n) = 1\)), the Dirichlet series factors as an Euler product over primes, where the behavior at prime \(p\) is captured by the 1D Bell series in \(K[[x]]\): \[
B_p(f; x) = \sum_{k=0}^{\infty} f(p^k) x^k, \qquad B_p(f *_D g; x) = B_p(f; x) \cdot B_p(g; x).
\]



Diagnostic Signal & The Prime-Multiplicity \(\Omega(n)\)-Derivation
What if \(f(n)\) is not multiplicative, and we need \(\ln_D(f)\), \(\exp_D(f)\), or \(f^\alpha\) in \(\mathcal{D}_f\) up to \(N \le 10^6\)? In \(K[[x]]\), we reduced \(\exp\) and \(\ln\) to ODEs using the standard derivative \(\frac{d}{dx} x^n = n x^{n-1}\). What is the counterpart of \(\frac{d}{dx}\) inside the Dirichlet ring \(\mathcal{D}_f\)?






TipDiagnostic Signal & Reverse-Engineering Scratchpad: Why \(\Omega(n)\) Replaces \(\ln n\)




The Diagnostic Signal: You need to compute \(\exp_D(f)\), \(\ln_D(f)\), or \(f^\alpha\) for an arbitrary (non-multiplicative) arithmetic function \(f(1 \dots N)\) modulo \(p\).
The Reverse-Engineering Scratchpad: Analytically, differentiating \(F(s) = \sum_{n=1}^\infty f(n) n^{-s}\) with respect to \(s\) multiplies \(f(n)\) by \(-\ln n\). Why does that satisfy the product rule (Leibniz rule) on Dirichlet convolution? Because \(\ln(ab) = \ln a + \ln b\) is a completely additive function! In modular arithmetic \(\mathbb{F}_p\), the real logarithm \(\ln n\) does not exist. However, ANY completely additive integer-valued function \(w : \mathbb{Z}_{\ge 1} \to \mathbb{Z}\) satisfying \(w(ab) = w(a) + w(b)\) defines a formal derivation \((\vartheta f)(n) = w(n) f(n)\) on \(\mathcal{D}_f\): \[
\vartheta(f *_D g)(n) = w(n) \sum_{ab = n} f(a) g(b) = \sum_{ab = n} \big(w(a) + w(b)\big) f(a) g(b) = (\vartheta f *_D g + f *_D \vartheta g)(n).
\] To solve for \(g(n)\) from \((\vartheta g)(n) = w(n) g(n)\), we must divide by \(w(n) \bmod p\) for every \(n \ge 2\). Therefore, we need a completely additive integer function \(w(n)\) such that \(w(n) > 0\) for all \(n \ge 2\) and \(w(n)\) is as small as possible so \(w(n) < p\)! The canonical choice is the total prime multiplicity function: \[
\Omega(n) = \sum_{p^k \parallel n} k \qquad \big(\Omega(1) = 0, \text{ and } 1 \le \Omega(n) \le \lfloor \log_2 N \rfloor \text{ for all } 2 \le n \le N\big).
\] Because \(\Omega(n) \le 20\) for \(N \le 10^6\), \(\Omega(n)\) is invertible modulo every prime \(p > \log_2 N\)!



Applying the derivation \((\vartheta f)(n) = \Omega(n) f(n)\) to \(g = \ln_D(f)\) (with \(f(1) = 1\)), \(g = \exp_D(f)\) (with \(f(1) = 0\)), and \(g = f^\alpha\) (with \(f(1) = 1\)) yields three \(O(N \log N)\) divisor recurrences:

Dirichlet Logarithm (\(g = \ln_D f\), \(f(1) = 1 \implies \vartheta g *_D f = \vartheta f\)): \[
\begin{aligned}
\sum_{d \mid n} \Omega(d) \, g(d) \, f\!\left(\frac{n}{d}\right) = \Omega(n) f(n) &\iff \Omega(n) g(n) f(1) + \sum_{\substack{d \mid n \\ 1 < d < n}} \Omega(d) \, g(d) \, f\!\left(\frac{n}{d}\right) = \Omega(n) f(n) \\
&\iff g(n) = f(n) - \frac{1}{\Omega(n)} \sum_{\substack{d \mid n \\ 1 < d < n}} \Omega(d) \, g(d) \, f\!\left(\frac{n}{d}\right) \qquad (n \ge 2, \ g(1) = 0).
\end{aligned}
\]
Dirichlet Exponential (\(g = \exp_D f\), \(f(1) = 0 \implies \vartheta g = \vartheta f *_D g\)): \[
\begin{aligned}
\Omega(n) g(n) = \sum_{d \mid n} \Omega\!\left(\frac{n}{d}\right) f\!\left(\frac{n}{d}\right) g(d) &\iff \Omega(n) g(n) = \sum_{\substack{d \mid n \\ d < n}} \Omega\!\left(\frac{n}{d}\right) f\!\left(\frac{n}{d}\right) g(d) \quad (\text{since } \Omega(1) = 0) \\
&\iff g(n) = \frac{1}{\Omega(n)} \sum_{\substack{d \mid n \\ d < n}} \Omega\!\left(\frac{n}{d}\right) f\!\left(\frac{n}{d}\right) g(d) \qquad (n \ge 2, \ g(1) = 1).
\end{aligned}
\]
Dirichlet Power (\(g = f^\alpha\), \(f(1) = 1 \implies f *_D \vartheta g = \alpha \, \vartheta f *_D g\)): \[
\begin{aligned}
\sum_{d \mid n} \Omega(d) g(d) f\!\left(\frac{n}{d}\right) = \alpha \sum_{d \mid n} \Omega\!\left(\frac{n}{d}\right) f\!\left(\frac{n}{d}\right) g(d) &\iff \Omega(n) g(n) f(1) = \sum_{\substack{d \mid n \\ d < n}} \left(\alpha \, \Omega\!\left(\frac{n}{d}\right) - \Omega(d)\right) f\!\left(\frac{n}{d}\right) g(d) \\
&\iff g(n) = \frac{1}{\Omega(n)} \sum_{\substack{d \mid n \\ d < n}} \left(\alpha \, \Omega\!\left(\frac{n}{d}\right) - \Omega(d)\right) f\!\left(\frac{n}{d}\right) g(d) \qquad (n \ge 2, \ g(1) = 1).
\end{aligned}
\]

// O(N log N) Dirichlet Exp and Ln using the Omega(n)-derivation
vector<mint> dgf_exp(const vector<mint>& f, const vector<int>& Om, int N) {
    vector<mint> g(N + 1); g[1] = 1;
    for (int d = 1; d <= N; ++d) {
        if (d >= 2) g[d] *= inv_small[Om[d]]; // finalize g[d] before pushing to multiples
        for (int k = 2; d * k <= N; ++k)
            g[d * k] += g[d] * f[k] * Om[k];
    }
    return g;
}


Hand-Checkable Trace (\(N = 6\) Dirichlet Exponential)
Let us trace \(g = \exp_D(f)\) up to \(N = 6\) where \(f(1) = 0\), \(f(2) = 1\), \(f(3) = 2\), and \(f(4) = f(5) = f(6) = 0\). Here \(\Omega = [0, 0, 1, 1, 2, 1, 2]\) for indices \(0 \dots 6\):

\(n = 1\): \(g(1) = 1\). Push to \(k = 2\): \(g(2) \mathrel{+}= g(1) f(2) \Omega(2) = 1 \cdot 1 \cdot 1 = 1\). Push to \(k = 3\): \(g(3) \mathrel{+}= g(1) f(3) \Omega(3) = 1 \cdot 2 \cdot 1 = 2\).
\(n = 2\): Finalize \(g(2) = 1 / \Omega(2) = 1\). Push to \(k = 2\) (\(n'=4\)): \(g(4) \mathrel{+}= g(2) f(2) \Omega(2) = 1 \cdot 1 \cdot 1 = 1\). Push to \(k = 3\) (\(n'=6\)): \(g(6) \mathrel{+}= g(2) f(3) \Omega(3) = 1 \cdot 2 \cdot 1 = 2\).
\(n = 3\): Finalize \(g(3) = 2 / \Omega(3) = 2\). Push to \(k = 2\) (\(n'=6\)): \(g(6) \mathrel{+}= g(3) f(2) \Omega(2) = 2 \cdot 1 \cdot 1 = 2\).
\(n = 4\): Finalize \(g(4) = 1 / \Omega(4) = 1/2\).
\(n = 6\): Finalize \(g(6) = (2 + 2) / \Omega(6) = 4 / 2 = 2\).
Direct check: \(\exp_D(f) = \varepsilon + f + \frac{1}{2!}(f *_D f)\) has \([4^{-s}]\exp_D(f) = \frac{1}{2} f(2)^2 = \frac{1}{2}\) and \([6^{-s}]\exp_D(f) = \frac{1}{2}(f(2)f(3) + f(3)f(2)) = 2\). Exact match!







NoteAlgorithm Contract: Dirichlet Generating Function Engine (\(*_{\text{Dir}}, A^{-1}, \ln_D, \exp_D\))




Input: Arithmetic functions \(f, g : \{1, \dots, N\} \to K\) representing truncated Dirichlet series \(\sum_{n=1}^N f(n) n^{-s} \in \mathcal{D}_f\).
Output: Dirichlet convolution \(f *_D g\), inverse \(f^{-1}\), logarithm \(\ln_D f\), exponential \(\exp_D f\), or power \(f^\alpha\) on \(\{1, \dots, N\}\).
Algebraic Hypothesis:

Convolution \(f *_D g\): Any commutative ring \(K\).
Inversion \(f^{-1}\): Requires \(f(1) \in K^\times\) (no characteristic restriction!).
Transcendental Operations (\(\ln_D f, \exp_D f, f^\alpha\)) via \(\Omega(n)\)-Derivation: Requires \(f(1) = 1\) (\(\ln_D, f^\alpha\)) or \(f(1) = 0\) (\(\exp_D\)), and \(1, 2, \dots, \lfloor \log_2 N \rfloor \in K^\times\) (i.e., \(\operatorname{char}(K) = 0\) or \(p > \lfloor \log_2 N \rfloor\)).

Complexity: \(O(N \log N)\) time (\(\sum_{d=1}^N \lfloor N / d \rfloor \approx N \ln N\) harmonic loop iterations; \(O(N \log \log N)\) when restricted to prime multipliers via Dirichlet FZT/IFZT), \(O(N)\) space.
Failure Modes & Edge Cases:

\(\Omega(1) = 0\) Division-by-Zero Guard: Since \(\Omega(1) = 0\), the divisor recurrence \(\Omega(n) g(n) = \sum_{d \mid n} \dots\) only determines \(g(n)\) for \(n \ge 2\). Always initialize \(g(1) = 0\) (for \(\ln_D\)) or \(g(1) = 1\) (for \(\exp_D, f^\alpha\)) explicitly and guard the division by \(\Omega(n)^{-1}\) with \(n \ge 2\).
Small Characteristic \(p \le \lfloor \log_2 N \rfloor\): If \(p \le \lfloor \log_2 N \rfloor\), \(\Omega(n) \equiv 0 \pmod p\) for integers with \(p\) prime factors (counted with multiplicity), breaking the \(\Omega(n)\)-derivation recurrence.

24.6 4-Tier Practice Ladder


Stepping Stone 1 (#216) — Jzzhu and Numbers

Source: Codeforces 449D — Jzzhu and Numbers
Prerequisites: Superset Fast Zeta & Möbius Transform (§24.1), Binomial Expansion in Bitwise AND Algebra


Problem Statement
You are given an array of \(m\) non-negative integers \(a_1, a_2, \dots, a_m\) where \(0 \le a_i < 2^{20}\). Count the number of non-empty subsequences of indices \(1 \le i_1 < i_2 < \dots < i_k \le m\) such that the bitwise AND of the chosen elements equals zero:
\[
a_{i_1} \mathbin{\&} a_{i_2} \mathbin{\&} \cdots \mathbin{\&} a_{i_k} = 0.
\]
Output the answer modulo \(10^9 + 7\).


Constraints

\(1 \le m \le 10^6\)
\(0 \le a_i \le 10^6 < 2^{20}\) (so \(n = 20\) bits)
Time limit: \(2.0\text{ s}\), Memory limit: \(256\text{ MB}\)

Sample Trace (\(m = 3, n = 2\), \(a = [1, 2, 3]\)):

The frequency array on masks \(00_2, 01_2, 10_2, 11_2\) is \(C = [0, 1, 1, 1]\).
Superset Zeta Transform \(\widehat{C}_S = \sum_{T \supseteq S} C_T\) gives \(\widehat{C} = [3, 2, 2, 1]\).
Pointwise non-empty subsequence counts \(\widehat{F}_S = 2^{\widehat{C}_S} - 1\) give \(\widehat{F} = [2^3-1, 2^2-1, 2^2-1, 2^1-1] = [7, 3, 3, 1]\).
Superset Möbius Transform at \(S = 00_2\): \(F_0 = \widehat{F}_{00} - \widehat{F}_{01} - \widehat{F}_{10} + \widehat{F}_{11} = 7 - 3 - 3 + 1 = 2\) (corresponding to \(\{1, 2\}\) and \(\{1, 2, 3\}\)).



Hint 1 — Diagnostic Signal & Combinatorial Model

Each element \(a_i\) can either be excluded (which acts as the identity mask \(\mathbf{1} = 2^n - 1\) for bitwise AND) or included with mask \(a_i\). What polynomial product in the bitwise AND monoid algebra \(K[(\{0, 1\}^n, \mathbin{\&})]\) generates the bitwise AND of all subsets?



Hint 2 — Algebraic Setup & Reverse-Engineering Scratchpad

In the bitwise AND algebra where the identity element is \(\mathbf{1} = 2^n - 1\), the generating function over all \(2^m\) subsequences is \(F(\mathbf{e}) = \prod_{i=1}^m (\mathbf{e}_{\mathbf{1}} + \mathbf{e}_{a_i})\). Apply the Superset Fast Zeta Transform \(\widehat{F}_S = \sum_{T \supseteq S} F_T\): a factor \((\mathbf{e}_{\mathbf{1}} + \mathbf{e}_{a_i})\) evaluates at \(S\) to \(1 + [a_i \supseteq S] = 2^{[S \subseteq a_i]}\).



Hint 3 — Coefficient Extraction & Complexity Contract

Let \(C_u\) be the frequency of \(u\) in \(a\). Compute \(\widehat{C}_S = \sum_{T \supseteq S} C_T\) in \(O(n 2^n)\) via the Superset FZT. Then \(\widehat{F}_S = 2^{\widehat{C}_S} - 1\) counts non-empty subsequences whose bitwise AND is a superset of \(S\). Recover \(F_0\) by applying the Superset IFMT (or direct inclusion-exclusion \(F_0 = \sum_{S} (-1)^{\operatorname{popcount}(S)} \widehat{F}_S\)) in \(O(2^n)\).







NoteComplete Derivation & Solution






Mathematical Derivation
Let \(M = \{0, 1\}^n\) with \(n = 20\) be the commutative monoid under bitwise AND (\(\mathbin{\&}\)), whose multiplicative identity is the all-ones mask \(\mathbf{1} = 2^n - 1\). For each \(i \in \{1, \dots, m\}\), choosing whether to omit or pick \(a_i\) corresponds to the binomial factor \((\mathbf{e}_{\mathbf{1}} + \mathbf{e}_{a_i}) \in \mathbb{F}_p[M]\). Subtracting the empty subsequence \(\mathbf{e}_{\mathbf{1}}\), the generating element for all non-empty subsequences is:
\[
F = \prod_{i=1}^m \left(\mathbf{e}_{\mathbf{1}} + \mathbf{e}_{a_i}\right) - \mathbf{e}_{\mathbf{1}} \quad \text{in } \mathbb{F}_p[(M, \mathbin{\&})],
\]
and we seek the coefficient \(F_0 = [\mathbf{e}_0] F\).
Applying the Superset Fast Zeta Transform \(\mathcal{Z}_{\supseteq}(A)_S = \sum_{T \supseteq S} A_T\) diagonalizes bitwise AND convolution into pointwise multiplication. For a single factor \(\mathbf{e}_{\mathbf{1}} + \mathbf{e}_{a_i}\):

Since \(\mathbf{1} \supseteq S\) for every mask \(S\), \(\mathbf{e}_{\mathbf{1}}\) always contributes \(1\) to \(\mathcal{Z}_{\supseteq}(\mathbf{e}_{\mathbf{1}} + \mathbf{e}_{a_i})_S\).
The term \(\mathbf{e}_{a_i}\) contributes \(1\) if and only if \(a_i \supseteq S\) (i.e., \(a_i \mathbin{\&} S = S\)), and \(0\) otherwise.

Let \(C_u = \#\{i : a_i = u\}\) be the frequency array of the input, and let \(\widehat{C}_S = \sum_{T \supseteq S} C_T\) be its Superset Fast Zeta Transform. Then exactly \(\widehat{C}_S\) elements satisfy \(a_i \supseteq S\), so multiplying across all \(i = 1, \dots, m\) yields:
\[
\widehat{F}_S = \prod_{i=1}^m 2^{[a_i \supseteq S]} - 1 = 2^{\widehat{C}_S} - 1.
\]
Finally, inverting \(\mathcal{Z}_{\supseteq}\) at mask \(S = 0\) via the Superset Möbius Transform \(\mu_{\supseteq}(0, S) = (-1)^{|S \setminus 0|} = (-1)^{\operatorname{popcount}(S)}\) extracts \(F_0\):
\[
F_0 = \sum_{S=0}^{2^n - 1} (-1)^{\operatorname{popcount}(S)} \left(2^{\widehat{C}_S} - 1\right) \pmod{10^9 + 7}.
\]
for (int i = 0; i < n; ++i)
    for (int mask = 0; mask < (1 << n); ++mask)
        if (!(mask & (1 << i))) C[mask] += C[mask | (1 << i)];
mint ans = 0;
for (int mask = 0; mask < (1 << n); ++mask) {
    mint ways = pw2[C[mask]] - 1;
    ans += (__builtin_popcount(mask) & 1) ? -ways : ways;
}


Algorithm Contract

Input & Exact Index Boundaries: Integer \(m \ge 1\), array \(a[1 \dots m]\) with \(0 \le a_i < 2^{20}\) (\(n = 20\)), modulus \(p = 10^9 + 7\).
Preconditions: None (Superset FZT and IFMT require no divisions in \(K\)).
Postconditions (Output): Returns \(F_0 = \#\{\varnothing \neq I \subseteq \{1, \dots, m\} : \bigwedge_{i \in I} a_i = 0\} \bmod p\).
Time & Space Complexity: \(O(m + n 2^n)\) time (\(20 \times 2^{19} \approx 10^7\) additions) and \(O(2^n)\) auxiliary space.
Loop / Algebraic Invariant: After outer iteration \(i \in [0, n-1]\), C[mask] stores the exact sum of initial frequencies over all masks \(T\) that agree with mask on bits \(i+1 \dots n-1\) and are supersets of mask on bits \(0 \dots i\).
Failure Modes & Edge Cases: In bitwise AND convolution, the multiplicative identity is the all-ones mask \(\mathbf{1} = 2^n - 1\), not \(0\); subtracting \(-1\) in \(2^{\widehat{C}_S} - 1\) excludes the empty subsequence (whose bitwise AND is \(\mathbf{1}\)) before applying the Superset Möbius Transform.









Stepping Stone 2 (#020) — Connectivity 2

Source: AtCoder Beginner Contest 213 G — Connectivity 2
Prerequisites: Set Power Series \(\ln\) / Pointed Connected-Component Decomposition (§24.2, §24.3)


Problem Statement
You are given a simple undirected graph \(G = (V, E)\) with \(n\) vertices \(V = \{1, 2, \dots, n\}\) and \(m\) edges. There are \(2^m\) spanning subgraphs \(G' = (V, E')\) obtained by choosing a subset of edges \(E' \subseteq E\). For each vertex \(k \in \{2, 3, \dots, n\}\) independently, find the number of spanning subgraphs \(G'\) in which vertex \(1\) and vertex \(k\) belong to the same connected component, modulo \(998244353\).


Constraints

\(2 \le n \le 17\)
\(0 \le m \le \frac{n(n-1)}{2}\)
Modulus: \(p = 998244353\)
Time limit: \(2.0\text{ s}\), Memory limit: \(1024\text{ MB}\)

Sample Trace (\(n = 3, m = 2\), edges \((1, 2)\) and \((2, 3)\)):

Total subgraphs on subsets \(S \subseteq \{1, 2, 3\}\): \(F_S = 2^{e(S)}\) has \(F_{\{1\}} = 1\), \(F_{\{1,2\}} = 2^1 = 2\), \(F_{\{1,3\}} = 2^0 = 1\), \(F_{\{1,2,3\}} = 2^2 = 4\).
Connected subgraphs \(C = \ln F\):

\(C_{\{1\}} = 1\).
\(C_{\{1,2\}} = F_{\{1,2\}} - C_{\{1\}} F_{\{2\}} = 2 - 1(1) = 1\).
\(C_{\{1,3\}} = F_{\{1,3\}} - C_{\{1\}} F_{\{3\}} = 1 - 1(1) = 0\).
\(C_{\{1,2,3\}} = F_{\{1,2,3\}} - C_{\{1\}} F_{\{2,3\}} - C_{\{1,2\}} F_{\{3\}} - C_{\{1,3\}} F_{\{2\}} = 4 - 1(2) - 1(1) - 0(1) = 1\).

Answer for \(k = 2\): \(\sum_{S \ni 1, 2} C_S F_{V \setminus S} = C_{\{1,2\}} F_{\{3\}} + C_{\{1,2,3\}} F_{\varnothing} = 1(1) + 1(1) = 2\).
Answer for \(k = 3\): \(\sum_{S \ni 1, 3} C_S F_{V \setminus S} = C_{\{1,3\}} F_{\{2\}} + C_{\{1,2,3\}} F_{\varnothing} = 0(1) + 1(1) = 1\).



Hint 1 — Diagnostic Signal & Combinatorial Model

Every spanning subgraph \(G' = (V, E')\) decomposes uniquely into the connected component \(S \subseteq V\) containing vertex \(1\), and an arbitrary Induced subgraph on the remaining vertices \(V \setminus S\) with zero edges crossing between \(S\) and \(V \setminus S\).



Hint 2 — Algebraic Setup & Reverse-Engineering Scratchpad

For each subset \(S \subseteq V\), let \(F_S = 2^{e(S)}\) be the total number of subgraphs on \(S\), where \(e(S)\) is the number of input edges with both endpoints in \(S\). Let \(C_S\) be the number of connected subgraphs on \(S\). In the Set Power Series ring \(\mathcal{R}_n\), \(F(\mathbf{x}) = \exp(C(\mathbf{x}))\), or equivalently using the pointed MSB derivative at vertex \(1\): \(F^{(1)}(\mathbf{x}) = C^{(1)}(\mathbf{x}) *_{\text{sub}} F(\mathbf{x})\) in \(\mathcal{R}_{V \setminus \{1\}}\).



Hint 3 — Coefficient Extraction & Complexity Contract

Either compute \(C(\mathbf{x}) = \ln F(\mathbf{x})\) in \(O(n^2 2^n)\) (or even simpler for \(n = 17\), the \(O(3^n)\) pointed recurrence \(C_S = F_S - \sum_{1 \in T \subsetneq S} C_T F_{S \setminus T}\)). Once \(C_S\) is known for all \(S \ni 1\), for each \(k \in \{2, \dots, n\}\), sum \(C_S \cdot F_{V \setminus S}\) over all subsets \(S \subseteq V\) containing both \(1\) and \(k\).







NoteComplete Derivation & Solution






Mathematical Derivation
For every subset \(S \subseteq V\), let \(e(S) = |\{(u, v) \in E : u \in S \text{ and } v \in S\}|\) denote the number of edges induced by \(S\), and let \(F_S = 2^{e(S)}\) be the total number of spanning subgraphs on vertex set \(S\). Let \(C_S\) denote the number of connected spanning subgraphs on \(S\).
By the exponential formula in the Set Power Series ring \(\mathcal{R}_n = \mathbb{F}_p[x_1, \dots, x_n]/(x_1^2, \dots, x_n^2)\), every spanning subgraph on \(S\) is a disjoint union of connected components:
\[
F(\mathbf{x}) = \sum_{S \subseteq V} F_S \mathbf{x}^S = \exp\!\left(\sum_{\varnothing \neq S \subseteq V} C_S \mathbf{x}^S\right) \implies C(\mathbf{x}) = \ln F(\mathbf{x}).
\]
Even more directly, apply the partial derivative \(\partial_{x_1}\) (pointing at vertex \(1\)) to \(F(\mathbf{x}) = \exp(C(\mathbf{x}))\):
\[
\partial_{x_1} F(\mathbf{x}) = \partial_{x_1} C(\mathbf{x}) *_{\text{sub}} F(\mathbf{x}) \quad \text{in } \mathcal{R}_{V \setminus \{1\}}.
\]
Reading the coefficient of \(\mathbf{x}^{S \setminus \{1\}}\) for any subset \(S \ni 1\) states that every subgraph on \(S\) is uniquely formed by choosing the connected component \(T \subseteq S\) containing vertex \(1\) (in \(C_T\) ways) and an arbitrary subgraph on \(S \setminus T\) (in \(F_{S \setminus T}\) ways):
\[
F_S = \sum_{\substack{T \subseteq S \\ 1 \in T}} C_T F_{S \setminus T} \implies C_S = F_S - \sum_{\substack{T \subsetneq S \\ 1 \in T}} C_T F_{S \setminus T}.
\]
We can compute \(C(\mathbf{x}) = \ln F(\mathbf{x})\) in \(O(n^2 2^n)\) via Ranked FZT (or the submask loop in \(\frac{1}{2} 3^n\) since \(n \le 17\)). Finally, a spanning subgraph \(G'\) on \(V\) connects vertex \(1\) and vertex \(k\) if and only if the connected component \(S\) of vertex \(1\) also contains \(k\), while \(V \setminus S\) carries any of the \(F_{V \setminus S}\) subgraphs on the remaining vertices:
\[
\text{Ans}(k) = \sum_{\substack{S \subseteq V \\ \{1, k\} \subseteq S}} C_S F_{V \setminus S} \pmod{998244353}.
\]
// Compute C = ln(F) via Ranked FZT in O(n^2 2^n), or pointed inversion at vertex 0
vector<mint> C = sps_ln(F, n); // F[0] = 1, C[S] = connected subgraphs on S
for (int k = 1; k < n; ++k) {
    mint ans = 0;
    for (int S = 0; S < (1 << n); ++S)
        if ((S & 1) && (S & (1 << k))) ans += C[S] * F[((1 << n) - 1) ^ S];
    cout << ans.val() << "\n";
}


Algorithm Contract

Input & Exact Index Boundaries: \(2 \le n \le 17\) (0-indexed \(0 \dots n-1\)), edge list \(E\) of size \(m\).
Preconditions: \(F_\varnothing = 2^{e(\varnothing)} = 1 \in \mathbb{F}_p^\times\).
Postconditions (Output): Outputs \(n - 1\) integers: \(\text{Ans}(k) \bmod 998244353\) for \(k = 1, \dots, n-1\).
Time & Space Complexity: \(O(n^2 2^n)\) time and \(O(n 2^n)\) space using SPS \(\ln\) (or \(O(3^n)\) time and \(O(2^n)\) space via pointed submask DP).
Loop / Algebraic Invariant: For every mask \(S\) with bit \(0\) set, \(C_S\) equals the number of connected spanning subgraphs on \(S\), and \(\sum_{0 \in T \subseteq S} C_T F_{S \setminus T} = F_S\).
Failure Modes & Edge Cases: When summing \(C_S F_{V \setminus S}\), only masks \(S\) containing both vertex \(0\) (1-indexed vertex \(1\)) and vertex \(k\) may be included, and the complement mask \(V \setminus S = ((1 \ll n) - 1) \oplus S\) must be taken inside the \(n\)-bit universe [0, 2^n - 1] so no bits \(\ge n\) leak into the index.









Intermediate 1 (#027) — We Love Forest

Source: AtCoder Beginner Contest 253 Ex — We Love Forest
Prerequisites: Matrix-Tree Theorem (Ch 13), Set Power Series Divided Power \(\frac{T(\mathbf{x})^c}{c!}\) (§24.3)


Problem Statement
You are given an undirected multigraph \(G = (V, E)\) with \(n\) vertices and \(m\) labeled edges \(e_1, e_2, \dots, e_m\) (self-loops are not present, but multiple edges between the same pair of vertices are distinct). For each integer \(k = 1, 2, \dots, n - 1\), you perform the following random process starting from an empty graph \(H\) on \(V\):

Repeat \(k\) times: choose one of the \(m\) edges of \(G\) uniformly at random (with replacement, so the same edge can be chosen multiple times) and add it to \(H\).

Find the probability that the resulting \(k\)-edge graph \(H\) is a forest (contains no cycles, including no 2-edge cycles formed by picking the same edge or parallel edges twice), modulo \(998244353\).


Constraints

\(2 \le n \le 14\)
\(1 \le m \le 500\)
Modulus: \(p = 998244353\)
Time limit: \(3.0\text{ s}\), Memory limit: \(1024\text{ MB}\)

Sample Trace (\(n = 3, m = 2\), edges \(e_1 = (1, 2), e_2 = (2, 3)\)):

Spanning trees per subset \(S\): \(T_{\{1\}} = T_{\{2\}} = T_{\{3\}} = 1\), \(T_{\{1,2\}} = T_{\{2,3\}} = 1, T_{\{1,3\}} = 0\), \(T_{\{1,2,3\}} = 1\).
For \(k = 1\) edge (\(c = n - k = 2\) components): \([x^V] \frac{T(\mathbf{x})^2}{2!} = T_{\{1,2\}} T_{\{3\}} + T_{\{2,3\}} T_{\{1\}} + T_{\{1,3\}} T_{\{2\}} = 1 + 1 + 0 = 2\) forests. Ordered edge sequences: \(2 \cdot 1! = 2\), probability \(2 / 2^1 = 1\).
For \(k = 2\) edges (\(c = n - k = 1\) component): \([x^V] \frac{T(\mathbf{x})^1}{1!} = T_{\{1,2,3\}} = 1\) forest. Ordered sequences: \(1 \cdot 2! = 2\), probability \(2 / 2^2 = 1/2 \equiv 499122177 \pmod{998244353}\).



Hint 1 — Diagnostic Signal & Combinatorial Model

A sequence of \(k\) chosen edges forms a forest on \(V\) if and only if the \(k\) edges are all distinct and form an unordered \(k\)-edge spanning forest on \(V\) (which has exactly \(c = n - k\) connected tree components), ordered in \(k!\) ways.



Hint 2 — Algebraic Setup & Reverse-Engineering Scratchpad

For each non-empty subset \(S \subseteq V\), compute the number of spanning trees \(T_S\) induced on \(S\) using Kirchhoff’s Matrix-Tree determinant in \(O(|S|^3)\). In the Set Power Series ring \(\mathcal{R}_n\), what is the coefficient of \(\mathbf{x}^V\) in the divided power \(\frac{T(\mathbf{x})^c}{c!}\)? It counts unordered partitions of \(V\) into \(c = n - k\) disjoint spanning trees!



Hint 3 — Coefficient Extraction & Complexity Contract

Lift \(T(\mathbf{x})\) to Ranked Zeta space \(\widehat{T}_M(t) = \sum_{S \subseteq M} T_S t^{|S|} \in \mathbb{F}_p[t]/(t^{n+1})\). Note that \(\widehat{T}_M(0) = 0\) because \(T_\varnothing = 0\). At each mask \(M\), compute powers \(\widehat{T}_M(t)^c \bmod t^{n+1}\) for \(c = 1, \dots, n-1\), apply Ranked IFZT at the full mask \(V = 2^n - 1\), and multiply \([t^n]\big(T(\mathbf{x})^c / c!\big)_V\) by \(k! / m^k \bmod p\).







NoteComplete Derivation & Solution






Mathematical Derivation
Any forest on \(n\) vertices with \(k\) edges contains no cycles (and thus no duplicate edges) and consists of exactly \(c = n - k\) connected components, each of which is a spanning tree on its vertex subset. Furthermore, any unordered \(k\)-edge forest can be produced by \(k!\) distinct ordered sequences of \(k\) edge draws out of \(m^k\) total sequences. Thus, if \(F_k\) denotes the number of unordered \(k\)-edge spanning forests on \(V\), the desired probability is:
\[
\mathbb{P}(\text{forest at step } k) = F_k \cdot \frac{k!}{m^k} \pmod{998244353}.
\]
To compute \(F_k\) for all \(k = 1, \dots, n - 1\):

Spanning Trees per Subset \(T_S\): For each non-empty subset \(S \subseteq V\), build the \(|S| \times |S|\) Laplacian matrix \(L_S\) of the induced subgraph \(G[S]\) and take the \((|S|-1) \times (|S|-1)\) principal minor determinant via Gaussian elimination in \(O(|S|^3)\) (or compute \(T_S\) via SPS Matrix-Tree / edge-by-edge tree DP). This gives the tree SPS \(T(\mathbf{x}) = \sum_{\varnothing \neq S \subseteq V} T_S \mathbf{x}^S \in \mathcal{R}_n\).
Forests via Divided Powers in \(\mathcal{R}_n\): An unordered \(k\)-edge spanning forest on \(V\) is an unordered set of \(c = n - k\) vertex-disjoint spanning trees whose union is \(V\). In \(\mathcal{R}_n\), multiplying \(T(\mathbf{x})\) with itself \(c\) times counts ordered \(c\)-tuples of disjoint trees, so dividing by \(c!\) counts unordered \(c\)-component forests: \[
F_k = [\mathbf{x}^V] \frac{T(\mathbf{x})^{n-k}}{(n-k)!}.
\]

In Ranked Zeta space, we compute \(\widehat{T}_M(t) \in \mathbb{F}_p[t]/(t^{n+1})\) once in \(O(n^2 2^n)\). Since we only need the coefficient at the single full mask \(V = 2^n - 1\) after Ranked IFZT, recall that IFZT at the top mask \(V\) is simply the alternating sum over all masks \(M \subseteq V\):
\[
[\mathbf{x}^V] \frac{T(\mathbf{x})^c}{c!} = \frac{1}{c!} [t^n] \sum_{M=0}^{2^n - 1} (-1)^{n - \operatorname{popcount}(M)} \widehat{T}_M(t)^c.
\]
Thus we don’t even need \(n\) separate Ranked IFZTs! At each mask \(M\), we maintain the running polynomial power \(P_M^{(c)}(t) = \widehat{T}_M(t)^c \bmod t^{n+1}\) for \(c = 1, \dots, n - 1\) in \(O(n^3)\) per mask, accumulating \((-1)^{n - |M|} [t^n] P_M^{(c)}(t)\) into forest_ord[c].
ranked_fzt(T_ranked, n, false);
vector<mint> forest_ord(n + 1, 0);
for (int M = 0; M < (1 << n); ++M) {
    mint sgn = ((n - __builtin_popcount(M)) & 1) ? -1 : 1;
    vector<mint> pw(n + 1, 0); pw[0] = 1;
    for (int c = 1; c < n; ++c) {
        vector<mint> nxt(n + 1, 0);
        for (int i = 0; i <= n; ++i)
            for (int j = 1; i + j <= n; ++j)
                nxt[i + j] += pw[i] * T_ranked[M * (n + 1) + j];
        pw.swap(nxt);
        forest_ord[c] += sgn * pw[n];
    }

Algorithm Contract

Input & Exact Index Boundaries: \(2 \le n \le 14\), \(1 \le m \le 500\), edge list of size \(m\).
Preconditions: \(1, 2, \dots, n \in \mathbb{F}_p^\times\) and \(m \not\equiv 0 \pmod p\) (\(p = 998244353\)).
Postconditions (Output): Outputs \(F_k \cdot k! \cdot m^{-k} \bmod p\) for \(k = 1, \dots, n - 1\).
Time & Space Complexity: \(O(n^3 2^n)\) time and \(O(n 2^n)\) space (\(\approx 14^3 \cdot 2^{14} \approx 4.5 \times 10^7\) operations).
Loop / Algebraic Invariant: At iteration \(c\), pw[d] at mask \(M\) equals \([t^d] \widehat{T}_M(t)^c\), and summing \((-1)^{n-|M|} \text{pw}[n]\) over all \(M\) yields \(c! \cdot F_{n-c}\) by inclusion-exclusion over missing vertices.
Failure Modes & Edge Cases: Because \(G\) is a multigraph, parallel edges between \(u\) and \(v\) must be accumulated with multiplicity in the Laplacian entries \(L_{u,u}, L_{v,v} \mathrel{+}= 1\) and \(L_{u,v}, L_{v,u} \mathrel{-}= 1\); single-vertex subsets (\(|S| = 1\)) have \(0 \times 0\) reduced Laplacian determinant \(T_S = 1\), whereas \(T_\varnothing = 0\).









Intermediate 2 (#042) — Balance Scale

Source: AtCoder Beginner Contest 306 Ex — Balance Scale
Prerequisites: DAG Source-Layer Recurrence (Ch 13.3), Connected Component SPS \(\ln\) & SPS Inversion (§24.2, §24.3)


Problem Statement
You have \(n\) balls numbered \(1, \dots, n\) with unknown positive weights, and \(m\) pairs of balls \((u_i, v_i)\) that you compare on a balance scale. Each of the \(m\) comparisons independently produces one of three symbols: < (\(w_{u_i} < w_{v_i}\)), > (\(w_{u_i} > w_{v_i}\)), or = (\(w_{u_i} = w_{v_i}\)).
Count how many of the \(3^m\) outcome strings of length \(m\) are consistent with at least one assignment of real weights \(w_1, \dots, w_n \in \mathbb{R}\), modulo \(998244353\).


Constraints

\(2 \le n \le 17\)
\(1 \le m \le \frac{n(n-1)}{2}\)
Modulus: \(p = 998244353\)
Time limit: \(4.0\text{ s}\), Memory limit: \(1024\text{ MB}\)

Sample Trace (\(n = 3, m = 3\), triangle \(K_3\) with edges \((1,2), (2,3), (1,3)\)):

Every non-empty subset \(T \subseteq \{1, 2, 3\}\) induces a connected subgraph \(G[T]\), so the number of connected components is \(c(T) = 1\), giving weight \(W_T = (-1)^{c(T) - 1} = +1\) for all \(T \neq \varnothing\).
Solving \(A(\mathbf{x}) = (1 - W(\mathbf{x}))^{-1}\) in \(\mathcal{R}_3\) (where \(A_k\) denotes \(A_S\) for \(|S| = k\) by symmetry):

\(|S| = 1\): \(A_1 = W_1 A_0 = 1(1) = 1\).
\(|S| = 2\): \(A_2 = 2 W_1 A_1 + W_2 A_0 = 2(1)(1) + 1(1) = 3\).
\(|S| = 3\): \(A_3 = 3 W_1 A_2 + 3 W_2 A_1 + W_3 A_0 = 3(3) + 3(1) + 1(1) = 13\) (\(6\) strict orders, \(6\) orders with one equal pair, and \(1\) all-equal ===).




Hint 1 — Diagnostic Signal & Combinatorial Model

An outcome string of <, >, and = is consistent with some real weights \(w_1, \dots, w_n\) if and only if contracting all = edges and directing </> edges produces a DAG with no </> edge having both endpoints inside the same = connected component.



Hint 2 — Algebraic Setup & Reverse-Engineering Scratchpad

Suppose we partition \(V\) into contracted = components. Within any layer of \(k\) minimal (source) components \(T_1, \dots, T_k\) of the contracted DAG, there can be NO edges of \(G\) between \(T_i\) and \(T_j\) (otherwise that edge would have a symbol: = would merge \(T_i\) and \(T_j\), while < or > would make one non-minimal!). Therefore, the union \(T = T_1 \sqcup \dots \sqcup T_k\) of any \(k\) independent contracted components is a subset \(T \subseteq V\) such that \(T_1, \dots, T_k\) are the exact connected components of the induced subgraph \(G[T]\)!



Hint 3 — Coefficient Extraction & Complexity Contract

By the DAG source-layer inclusion-exclusion recurrence (Chapter 13.3), selecting a non-empty independent set of \(c\) contracted components covering vertex set \(T\) carries weight \((-1)^{c - 1}\). Since the connected components of \(G[T]\) are uniquely determined by \(T\) itself (say \(c(T)\) components), the weight of choosing \(T\) as the source layer is simply \(W_T = (-1)^{c(T) - 1}\) for \(T \neq \varnothing\)! Then \(A_S = \sum_{\varnothing \neq T \subseteq S} (-1)^{c(T)-1} A_{S \setminus T}\), which is a single Set Power Series inversion \(A(\mathbf{x}) = (1 - W(\mathbf{x}))^{-1}\) in \(\mathcal{R}_n\) in \(O(n^2 2^n)\)!







NoteComplete Derivation & Solution






Mathematical Derivation
Consider any valid outcome string on the \(m\) edges of \(G = (V, E)\). Define an equivalence relation on \(V\) where \(u \sim v\) if and only if they are connected by a path of = edges. Let \(B_1, B_2, \dots, B_r\) be the resulting equivalence classes (blocks of equal weight). For the outcome string to be consistent with real weights \(w_1, \dots, w_n\):

Each block \(B_i\) must induce a connected subgraph \(G[B_i]\), and every edge of \(G\) with both endpoints in \(B_i\) must be assigned = (since all vertices in \(B_i\) have equal weight).
Every edge of \(G\) between two distinct blocks \(B_i \neq B_j\) must be assigned < or >, and the resulting directed multigraph on the contracted blocks \(\{B_1, \dots, B_r\}\) must be acyclic (a DAG).

Crucially, once we know the orientation of every edge between distinct blocks \(B_i \neq B_j\), the outcome string on all \(m\) edges is uniquely determined! Now apply the standard DAG source-layer inclusion-exclusion recurrence (Chapter 13.3) to the contracted blocks: if we peel off a non-empty set of \(k\) blocks \(B_1, \dots, B_k\) that have no edges between them in \(G\) (so they are pairwise disconnected in \(G\) and can simultaneously serve as sources), inclusion-exclusion assigns weight \((-1)^{k-1}\).
Notice the miracle: if \(B_1, \dots, B_k\) are non-empty connected subgraphs of \(G\) with no edges of \(G\) between distinct \(B_i\) and \(B_j\), then \(B_1, \dots, B_k\) are simply the connected components of the induced subgraph \(G[T]\) on their union \(T = B_1 \sqcup \dots \sqcup B_k\)! Thus, for each non-empty subset \(T \subseteq V\), there is at most one way to decompose \(T\) into pairwise non-adjacent connected blocks, namely into the \(c(T)\) connected components of \(G[T]\)!
Therefore, defining the Set Power Series \(W(\mathbf{x}) \in \mathcal{R}_n\) by:
\[
W_T = \begin{cases} 0 & \text{if } T = \varnothing, \\ (-1)^{c(T) - 1} & \text{if } T \neq \varnothing, \end{cases}
\]
where \(c(T)\) is the number of connected components of \(G[T]\), the number of valid outcome strings \(A_S\) on \(G[S]\) satisfies:
\[
A_S = \sum_{\varnothing \neq T \subseteq S} W_T A_{S \setminus T} \quad (S \neq \varnothing, \ A_\varnothing = 1) \iff A(\mathbf{x}) = \frac{1}{1 - W(\mathbf{x})} \quad \text{in } \mathcal{R}_n.
\]
We precompute \(c(T)\) for all \(T \subseteq V\) in \(O(n 2^n)\) (using BFS/DFS or DSU on masks) and run one \(O(n^2 2^n)\) SPS inversion (1 - W)^{-1}! (Alternatively, applying sps_compose from §24.3 with \(G(y) = (1 - y)^{-1} = \sum_{d=0}^n d! \frac{y^d}{d!}\)—passing the EGF derivative array \(g_d = d!\)—computes \((1 - W(\mathbf{x}))^{-1}\) with zero divisions in any characteristic.)
vector<mint> P((n + 1) << n, 0); P[0] = 1;
for (int T = 1; T < (1 << n); ++T)
    P[T * (n + 1) + __builtin_popcount(T)] = (comp_cnt[T] & 1) ? -1 : 1; // 1 - W(x)
ranked_fzt(P, n, false);
for (int M = 0; M < (1 << n); ++M)
    poly_inv_inplace(&P[M * (n + 1)], n); // O(n^2) truncated inverse at each mask
ranked_fzt(P, n, true);
mint ans = P[((1 << n) - 1) * (n + 1) + n];


Algorithm Contract

Input & Exact Index Boundaries: \(2 \le n \le 17\), \(1 \le m \le \binom{n}{2}\), undirected edge list \(E\).
Preconditions: \([t^0](1 - W)_\varnothing = 1 \in \mathbb{F}_p^\times\) (no divisions needed in poly_inv_inplace since constant term is \(1\)).
Postconditions (Output): Returns \(A_V \bmod 998244353\), the number of consistent </>/= strings of length \(m\).
Time & Space Complexity: \(O(n^2 2^n)\) time and \(O(n 2^n)\) space (\(\approx 17^2 \cdot 2^{17} \approx 3.8 \times 10^7\) operations).
Loop / Algebraic Invariant: In Ranked Zeta space at mask \(M\), P[M*(n+1) + d] after poly_inv_inplace equals \([t^d]\big(1 - \widehat{W}_M(t)\big)^{-1}\), and Ranked IFZT extracts \([\mathbf{x}^V](1 - W(\mathbf{x}))^{-1}\) at degree \(d = n\).
Failure Modes & Edge Cases: When forming \(P(\mathbf{x}) = 1 - W(\mathbf{x})\) for inversion, the sign of \(W_T = (-1)^{c(T) - 1}\) is negated to \(-W_T = (-1)^{c(T)}\) for all \(T \neq \varnothing\) while \(P_\varnothing = 1\); getting this sign parity backwards computes \((1 + W(\mathbf{x}))^{-1}\) instead of \((1 - W(\mathbf{x}))^{-1}\).









Advanced 1 (#110) — Wise Men (Hard Version)

Source: Codeforces 1326F2 — Wise Men (Hard Version)
Prerequisites: Partition-Indexed Subset Convolution, Ranked Zeta Space & Superset Möbius Inversion (§24.1, §24.2)


Problem Statement
There are \(n\) wise men numbered \(1, \dots, n\), and a symmetric binary adjacency matrix \(G \in \{0, 1\}^{n \times n}\) indicating which pairs of wise men know each other. For each of the \(n!\) permutations \(p = (p_1, p_2, \dots, p_n)\) of \(\{1, \dots, n\}\), we form a binary string \(s(p) = s_1 s_2 \dots s_{n-1} \in \{0, 1\}^{n-1}\) of length \(n - 1\), where \(s_i = 1\) if \(p_i\) and \(p_{i+1}\) know each other (\(G_{p_i, p_{i+1}} = 1\)), and \(s_i = 0\) otherwise.
For every binary string \(w \in \{0, 1\}^{n-1}\), compute the number of permutations \(p\) such that \(s(p) = w\). (Output all \(2^{n-1}\) exact integer counts in \(64\)-bit integers int64_t.)


Constraints

\(2 \le n \le 18\)
\(G_{i,j} \in \{0, 1\}\), \(G_{i,i} = 0\), \(G_{i,j} = G_{j,i}\)
Exact 64-bit integer output (no modulus!)
Time limit: \(4.0\text{ s}\), Memory limit: \(512\text{ MB}\)

Sample Trace (\(n = 3\), edges \((1, 2)\) and \((2, 3)\)):

Path counts \(P_k(S)\) for \(S = \{1, 2, 3\}\):

Partition \(\lambda = (3)\) (one path of length 3): \(1 \to 2 \to 3\) and \(3 \to 2 \to 1\), so \(Z_{(3)} = 2\).
Partition \(\lambda = (2, 1)\) (path of length 2 on \(T\) and length 1 on \(V \setminus T\)): for \(T = \{1,2\}\), \(2 \times 1 = 2\); for \(T = \{2,3\}\), \(2 \times 1 = 2\); for \(T = \{1,3\}\), \(0\). Sum \(Z_{(2,1)} = 4\).
Partition \(\lambda = (1, 1, 1)\): \(1! \times 3! = 6\).

Mapping partitions to masks \(w \in \{00_2, 01_2, 10_2, 11_2\}\) of 1-runs (Superset Zeta \(\widehat{A}_w\)):

\(\widehat{A}_{11} = Z_{(3)} = 2\); \(\widehat{A}_{10} = \widehat{A}_{01} = Z_{(2,1)} = 4\); \(\widehat{A}_{00} = Z_{(1,1,1)} = 6\).

Superset IFMT gives \(A_{11} = 2\), \(A_{10} = 4 - 2 = 2\), \(A_{01} = 4 - 2 = 2\), \(A_{00} = 6 - 4 - 4 + 2 = 0\).



Hint 1 — Diagnostic Signal & Combinatorial Model

Directly requiring \(s_i = 0\) (two adjacent vertices do not know each other) is awkward, whereas requiring \(s_i = 1\) (an edge is present) simply chains consecutive vertices into directed paths in \(G\)! Apply Superset Zeta Transform on the \((n-1)\)-bit pattern \(w\): requiring \(s(p) \supseteq w\) means every maximal contiguous block of \(1\)s in \(w\) of length \(L - 1\) forces a directed path of \(L\) vertices in \(G\).



Hint 2 — Algebraic Setup & Reverse-Engineering Scratchpad

Notice that the number of ways to cover \(V\) with disjoint directed paths of vertex sizes \(L_1, L_2, \dots, L_r\) (where \(\sum L_i = n\)) depends only on the unordered integer partition \(\lambda = (L_1 \ge L_2 \ge \dots \ge L_r) \vdash n\), NOT on the order of the blocks! For \(n = 18\), there are \(2^{17} = 131072\) masks \(w\), but only \(p(18) = 385\) integer partitions of \(18\)!



Hint 3 — Coefficient Extraction & Complexity Contract


Use standard \(O(n^2 2^n)\) Hamiltonian path DP to compute \(P_{|S|}(S)\), the number of directed paths spanning subset \(S\).
Apply the \(O(n 2^n)\) Fast Zeta Transform to each rank \(k = 1, \dots, n\): \(\widehat{P}_k(M) = \sum_{S \subseteq M, |S|=k} P_k(S)\).
Backtrack over all \(p(n) \le 385\) partitions \(\lambda = (L_1, \dots, L_r) \vdash n\), maintaining the pointwise product \(\prod_{i=1}^r \widehat{P}_{L_i}(M)\) and evaluating the top-mask IFZT sum \(\sum_{M} (-1)^{n - |M|} \prod_i \widehat{P}_{L_i}(M)\) in \(O(2^n)\) per partition.
Assign each mask \(w \in [0, 2^{n-1}-1]\) the value of its run-length partition \(\lambda(w)\), and run an \(O((n-1) 2^{n-1})\) Superset IFMT!








NoteComplete Derivation & Solution






Mathematical Derivation
For each pattern mask \(w \in \{0, 1\}^{n-1}\), let \(A_w\) be the number of permutations \(p\) with \(s(p) = w\), and let \(\widehat{A}_w = \sum_{w' \supseteq w} A_{w'}\) be its Superset Zeta Transform: the number of permutations \(p\) such that \(p_i\) and \(p_{i+1}\) know each other whenever bit \(i\) of \(w\) is \(1\) (with no restriction when bit \(i\) of \(w\) is \(0\)).
Decompose the \((n-1)\)-bit mask \(w\) by splitting at every \(0\)-bit. This partitions the \(n\) positions \(\{1, \dots, n\}\) into maximal contiguous segments of sizes \(L_1, L_2, \dots, L_r\) (\(\sum_{i=1}^r L_i = n\)), where a segment of \(L_i\) vertices corresponds to \(L_i - 1\) consecutive \(1\)-bits in \(w\). A permutation \(p\) satisfies \(s(p) \supseteq w\) if and only if it partitions the vertex set \(V\) into an ordered tuple of disjoint subsets \((S_1, S_2, \dots, S_r)\) with \(|S_i| = L_i\), and forms a valid directed path in \(G[S_i]\) on each subset \(S_i\)!
For each \(k \in \{1, \dots, n\}\) and \(S \subseteq V\) with \(|S| = k\), let \(P_k(S)\) be the number of directed Hamiltonian paths spanning \(S\). Then in the Set Power Series ring \(\mathcal{R}_n\):
\[
\widehat{A}_w = [\mathbf{x}^V] \prod_{i=1}^r \left(\sum_{|S| = L_i} P_{L_i}(S) \mathbf{x}^S\right).
\]
Because \(\mathcal{R}_n\) is commutative, this product depends only on the sorted integer partition \(\lambda(w) = \operatorname{sort}(L_1, \dots, L_r) \vdash n\)! For \(n = 18\), the number of partitions is \(p(18) = 385 \ll 2^{17} = 131072\).
Let \(\widehat{P}_k(M) = \sum_{S \subseteq M, |S| = k} P_k(S)\) be the Fast Zeta Transform of the rank-\(k\) slice. Because \(\sum L_i = n\), any overlapping union \(\bigcup_{i=1}^r S_i\) with \(|S_i| = L_i\) has cardinality strictly less than \(n\), so its contribution to the full mask \(V\) vanishes under IFZT! Thus, for every partition \(\lambda = (L_1, \dots, L_r) \vdash n\), we evaluate the top-mask IFZT directly by inclusion-exclusion:
\[
Z_\lambda = [\mathbf{x}^V] \prod_{i=1}^r P_{L_i}(\mathbf{x}) = \sum_{M=0}^{2^n - 1} (-1)^{n - \operatorname{popcount}(M)} \prod_{i=1}^r \widehat{P}_{L_i}(M).
\]
We compute \(P_k(S)\) in \(O(n^2 2^n)\) via standard bitmask path DP, transform each rank \(k\) in \(O(n 2^n)\), DFS over the \(p(n) = 385\) partitions maintaining the running pointwise product array prod[M] in \(385 \times 2^{18} \approx 10^8\) multiplications, fill \(\widehat{A}_w = Z_{\lambda(w)}\), and finish with a Superset IFMT on \(\widehat{A}\) in \(O(n 2^{n-1})\)!
// DFS over integer partitions lambda of n, maintaining pointwise product in Zeta space
void dfs_part(int rem, int max_L, vector<int>& cur, const vector<ll>& prod) {
    if (rem == 0) {
        ll sum = 0;
        for (int M = 0; M < (1 << n); ++M)
            sum += ((n - __builtin_popcount(M)) & 1) ? -prod[M] : prod[M];
        part_val[cur] = sum; return;
    }
    for (int L = min(rem, max_L); L >= 1; --L) {
        vector<ll> nxt(1 << n);
        for (int M = 0; M < (1 << n); ++M) nxt[M] = prod[M] * P_hat[L][M];
        cur.push_back(L); dfs_part(rem - L, L, cur, nxt); cur.pop_back();
    }
}


Algorithm Contract

Input & Exact Index Boundaries: \(2 \le n \le 18\), \(n \times n\) symmetric adjacency matrix \(G\).
Preconditions: Exact 64-bit signed arithmetic int64_t (since \(18! \approx 6.4 \times 10^{15} < 2^{63} - 1\) and no divisions are needed).
Postconditions (Output): Outputs \(2^{n-1}\) exact integers \(A_w\) for \(w \in [0, 2^{n-1}-1]\).
Time & Space Complexity: \(O\big((n^2 + p(n)) 2^n\big)\) time and \(O(n 2^n)\) space, where \(p(18) = 385\).
Loop / Algebraic Invariant: At each DFS node with partial partition \((L_1, \dots, L_j)\), prod[M] holds \(\prod_{i=1}^j \widehat{P}_{L_i}(M)\), and at leaves (\(\sum L_i = n\)), the alternating sum over \(M\) extracts the exact disjoint-union coefficient \([\mathbf{x}^V] \prod_i P_{L_i}(\mathbf{x})\).
Failure Modes & Edge Cases: Because the problem requires exact \(64\)-bit integers without a modulus, do not reduce modulo \(998244353\); use int64_t (long long) or uint64_t throughout (safe since \(\sum_w A_w = 18! \approx 6.40 \times 10^{15} < 2^{63} - 1\)), and note that a contiguous segment of \(L\) vertices corresponds to \(L - 1\) consecutive 1-bits in the \((n - 1)\)-bit mask \(w\).









Advanced 2 (#207) — [集训队互测2015] 胡策的统计

Source: UOJ 94 — 胡策的统计
Prerequisites: Pointed Vertex-by-Vertex Biconnected SPS \(\ln\), SPS \(\exp\) & Divided Powers (§24.3, Callout #9)


Problem Statement
You are given a simple undirected graph \(G = (V, E)\) with \(n\) vertices and \(m\) edges. A non-empty induced or spanning subgraph \(H = (S, E_H)\) (\(S \subseteq V, E_H \subseteq E[S]\)) is called biconnected if it is connected and contains no articulation point (no vertex \(v \in S\) whose removal disconnects \(H\); in particular, a single vertex \(|S| = 1\) and a single edge \(|S| = 2\) are biconnected).

First, for every non-empty subset \(S \subseteq V\), compute the number of biconnected spanning subgraphs \(B_S\) on \(S\).
Second, compute the total weight over all ordered partitions of \(V\) into \(k \ge 1\) vertex-disjoint biconnected spanning subgraphs (equivalently, \([\mathbf{x}^V] \frac{1}{1 - B(\mathbf{x})}\) in \(\mathcal{R}_n\)), modulo \(998244353\).



Constraints

\(1 \le n \le 15\)
\(0 \le m \le \frac{n(n-1)}{2}\)
Modulus: \(p = 998244353\)
Time limit: \(2.0\text{ s}\), Memory limit: \(256\text{ MB}\)

Sample Trace (\(n = 3\), triangle \(K_3\) with \(3\) edges):

Total subgraphs \(F_S = 2^{e(S)}\): \(F_1 = 1\), \(F_2 = 2\), \(F_{\{1,2,3\}} = 8\).
Connected subgraphs \(C = \ln F\): \(C_1 = 1\), \(C_2 = 1\), \(C_{\{1,2,3\}} = 4\) (the triangle plus \(3\) paths of \(2\) edges).
Sequential pointed \((n-1)\)-variable \(\ln\) for \(v = 1, 2, 3\):

At \(v = 1\): \(C^{(1)} = 1 + x_2 + x_3 + 4 x_2 x_3\). Taking \(\ln C^{(1)}\) in \(\mathcal{R}_{\{2,3\}}\) subtracts \(x_2 \cdot x_3\) (the path \(2 - 1 - 3\) where \(1\) is a cut vertex!), updating \(C_{\{1,2,3\}} \leftarrow 4 - 1 = 3\).
At \(v = 2\): subtracts the path \(1 - 2 - 3\), updating \(C_{\{1,2,3\}} \leftarrow 3 - 1 = 2\).
At \(v = 3\): subtracts the path \(1 - 3 - 2\), updating \(C_{\{1,2,3\}} \leftarrow 2 - 1 = 1\) (only the \(3\)-cycle \(K_3\) remains!).

Thus \(B_1 = 1, B_2 = 1, B_{\{1,2,3\}} = 1\). Finally, \([\mathbf{x}^V](1 - B(\mathbf{x}))^{-1} = 1(B_{\{1,2,3\}}) + 2!\cdot 3(B_2 B_1) + 3!\cdot 1(B_1^3 / 3!) = 1 + 6 + 6 = 13\).



Hint 1 — Diagnostic Signal & Combinatorial Model

To find the number of biconnected spanning subgraphs \(B_S\) for every \(S \subseteq V\) on a fixed graph \(G\) (\(n \le 15\)), start with \(F_S = 2^{e(S)}\), take the \(n\)-variable SPS logarithm \(C(\mathbf{x}) = \ln F(\mathbf{x})\) to isolate connected subgraphs, and then ask: how do we strip away connected subgraphs that have an articulation point?



Hint 2 — Algebraic Setup & Reverse-Engineering Scratchpad

Fix a vertex \(v \in V\). In any connected graph \(H\) on \(T \cup \{v\}\) (\(T \subseteq V \setminus \{v\}\)), deleting \(v\) partitions \(T\) into connected pieces \(T_1 \sqcup \dots \sqcup T_k = T\) that were attached to \(v\) and had no edges between distinct \(T_i\) and \(T_j\). That means the pointed \((n-1)\)-variable SPS \(C^{(v)}(\mathbf{x}) = \sum_{T \subseteq V \setminus \{v\}} C_{T \cup \{v\}} \mathbf{x}^T \in \mathcal{R}_{V \setminus \{v\}}\) is the exponential of connected graphs on \(T_i \cup \{v\}\) where \(v\) is not an articulation point!



Hint 3 — Coefficient Extraction & Complexity Contract


Compute \(C = \ln F\) in \(\mathcal{R}_n\) in \(O(n^2 2^n)\).
For each \(v = 0, 1, \dots, n - 1\): extract the \((n-1)\)-variable SPS \(C^{(v)}(\mathbf{x})\) on masks \(T \subseteq V \setminus \{v\}\) (note \(C^{(v)}_\varnothing = C_{\{v\}} = 1\)), replace \(C^{(v)}\) with \(\ln C^{(v)}\) in \(\mathcal{R}_{V \setminus \{v\}}\) in \(O(n^2 2^{n-1})\), and write the coefficients back into \(C_{T \cup \{v\}}\).
After all \(n\) vertices are processed, \(B_S = C_S\) holds the exact number of biconnected spanning subgraphs on \(S\). Compute \((1 - B(\mathbf{x}))^{-1}\) in \(\mathcal{R}_n\) in \(O(n^2 2^n)\) to obtain \([\mathbf{x}^V](1 - B(\mathbf{x}))^{-1}\).








NoteComplete Derivation & Solution






Mathematical Derivation
Let \(F_S = 2^{e(S)}\) be the number of spanning subgraphs on \(S \subseteq V\). Taking the Set Power Series logarithm in \(\mathcal{R}_n\):
\[
C(\mathbf{x}) = \ln F(\mathbf{x}) \quad \text{in } \mathcal{R}_n
\]
yields \(C_S\), the number of connected spanning subgraphs on \(S\).
Now we must eliminate all connected subgraphs that contain at least one articulation point (cut vertex). Order the vertices \(V = \{0, 1, \dots, n-1\}\). Suppose that after step \(v - 1\), \(C_S\) counts connected spanning subgraphs on \(S\) in which none of the vertices in \(S \cap \{0, \dots, v-1\}\) is an articulation point.
Consider how a graph \(H\) counted by \(C_{T \cup \{v\}}\) (where \(T \subseteq V \setminus \{v\}\)) behaves when we delete vertex \(v\):

Deleting \(v\) splits \(H \setminus \{v\}\) into \(k \ge 1\) connected components on disjoint vertex subsets \(T_1 \sqcup T_2 \sqcup \dots \sqcup T_k = T\).
For each piece \(T_i\), the induced subgraph \(H[T_i \cup \{v\}]\) is connected, \(v\) is not an articulation point of \(H[T_i \cup \{v\}]\), and furthermore no vertex \(u \in T_i \cap \{0, \dots, v-1\}\) can be an articulation point of \(H[T_i \cup \{v\}]\) if and only if \(u\) was not an articulation point of \(H\)!
Conversely, gluing \(k\) such \(v\)-blocks \(H_i\) on \(T_i \cup \{v\}\) at vertex \(v\) creates no new cycles between distinct \(T_i\), so a vertex \(u \neq v\) is an articulation point of the union \(H\) if and only if \(u\) is an articulation point of its own piece \(H_i\)!

Therefore, in the \((n-1)\)-variable Set Power Series ring \(\mathcal{R}_{V \setminus \{v\}}\), the pointed series
\[
C^{(v)}(\mathbf{x}) = \sum_{T \subseteq V \setminus \{v\}} C_{T \cup \{v\}} \mathbf{x}^T \quad \big(\text{with } C^{(v)}_\varnothing = C_{\{v\}} = 1\big)
\]
is the exact subset exponential of the subgraphs on \(T \cup \{v\}\) in which \(v\) is not an articulation point! Updating
\[
C^{(v)}(\mathbf{x}) \leftarrow \ln_{\mathcal{R}_{V \setminus \{v\}}} C^{(v)}(\mathbf{x})
\]
and writing its coefficients back to \(C_{T \cup \{v\}}\) strips away all graphs where \(v\) is an articulation point. After repeating this for \(v = 0, 1, \dots, n-1\), no vertex in \(V\) can be an articulation point, so \(B(\mathbf{x}) = C(\mathbf{x})\) is the exact SPS of biconnected spanning subgraphs! Finally, an ordered sequence of \(k\) disjoint biconnected components partitioning \(V\) has generating function \(\sum_{k \ge 0} B(\mathbf{x})^k = (1 - B(\mathbf{x}))^{-1}\) in \(\mathcal{R}_n\).
vector<mint> C = sps_ln(F, n); // Step 1: connected subgraphs on V
for (int v = 0; v < n; ++v) {  // Step 2: strip cut vertex v via (n-1)-var SPS ln
    vector<mint> Cv(1 << (n - 1));
    for (int T = 0; T < (1 << (n - 1)); ++T) {
        int full_T = (T & ((1 << v) - 1)) | ((T >> v) << (v + 1)) | (1 << v);
        Cv[T] = C[full_T];
    }
    Cv = sps_ln(Cv, n - 1); // C_{\{v\}} = 1 is the constant term Cv[0]
    for (int T = 0; T < (1 << (n - 1)); ++T) {
        int full_T = (T & ((1 << v) - 1)) | ((T >> v) << (v + 1)) | (1 << v);
        C[full_T] = Cv[T];
    }
}
vector<mint> ans_sps = sps_inv_one_minus(C, n); // Step 3: (1 - B(x))^{-1}


Algorithm Contract

Input & Exact Index Boundaries: \(1 \le n \le 15\), undirected edge list \(E\) of size \(m\).
Preconditions: \(F_\varnothing = 1\) and \(C_{\{v\}} = 1\) for all \(v \in V\); \(1, \dots, n \in \mathbb{F}_p^\times\) (\(p = 998244353\)).
Postconditions (Output): Returns \([\mathbf{x}^V](1 - B(\mathbf{x}))^{-1} \bmod 998244353\).
Time & Space Complexity: \(O(n^3 2^n)\) time (\(15\) calls to \(14\)-variable SPS \(\ln\), \(\approx 15 \cdot 14^2 \cdot 2^{14} \approx 4.8 \times 10^7\) ops) and \(O(n 2^n)\) space.
Loop / Algebraic Invariant: After iteration \(v \in [0, n-1]\), for every non-empty \(S \subseteq V\), C[S] equals the number of connected spanning subgraphs on \(S\) whose set of articulation points is disjoint from \(\{0, 1, \dots, v\}\).
Failure Modes & Edge Cases: In the pointed \((n-1)\)-variable logarithm at vertex \(v\), the empty subset \(T = \varnothing \subseteq V \setminus \{v\}\) corresponds to the single-vertex subgraph \(\{v\}\) with \(C^{(v)}_\varnothing = C_{\{v\}} = 1\) (so \(\ln C^{(v)}\) is well-defined with constant term \(0\)), and both \(|S| = 1\) (single vertex) and \(|S| = 2\) (single edge \(K_2\)) have no articulation points and remain biconnected (\(B_S = 1\)).









Mastery 1 (#231) — 幂数 (Powerful Numbers)

Source: LibreOJ 6729 — 幂数
Prerequisites: Dirichlet Ring \(\mathcal{D}_f\), Bell Series Division & Powerful Number Perturbation (§24.4)


Problem Statement
Let \(f, g : \mathbb{Z}_{\ge 1} \to \mathbb{F}_p\) be two multiplicative functions such that \(f(1) = g(1) = 1\) and \(f(p) = g(p)\) at every prime \(p\). Given a positive integer \(N \le 10^{11}\), an \(O(1)\) (or \(O(\sqrt{x})\)-cached) prefix-sum oracle for \(G(x) = \sum_{n=1}^x g(n) \bmod p\), and prime-power evaluators for \(f(p^k)\) and \(g(p^k)\) (\(k \ge 1\)), compute the prefix sum
\[
S(N) = \sum_{n=1}^N f(n) \bmod p
\]
in \(O(\sqrt{N})\) time by expressing \(f = h *_D g\) in the Dirichlet ring \(\mathcal{D}_f\), proving via Bell series that \(h = f *_D g^{-1}\) vanishes outside the \(O(\sqrt{N})\) powerful numbers \(d \le N\) (\(p \mid d \implies p^2 \mid d\)), and summing \(h(d) G(\lfloor N / d \rfloor)\) over all powerful numbers \(d \le N\).


Constraints

\(1 \le N \le 10^{11}\) (or up to \(10^{13}\))
Number of powerful numbers \(\le N\) is \(\le \frac{\zeta(3/2)}{\zeta(3)} \sqrt{N} \approx 2.17 \sqrt{N}\) (\(\le 6.8 \times 10^5\) at \(N = 10^{11}\))
Modulus: \(p = 998244353\) or \(10^9 + 7\)
Time limit: \(2.0\text{ s}\), Memory limit: \(256\text{ MB}\)

Sample Trace (\(N = 12\), \(f(p) = 1\), \(f(p^k) = 2\) for \(k \ge 2\), and \(g(n) = 1\) for all \(n\)):

At every prime \(p\): \(B_p(f; x) = 1 + x + 2x^2 + 2x^3 + \dots\) and \(B_p(g; x) = \frac{1}{1 - x}\) (with prefix sum \(G(x) = x\)).
Bell series quotient: \(B_p(h; x) = B_p(f; x)(1 - x) = (1 + x + 2x^2 + 2x^3 + \dots)(1 - x) = 1 + x^2\).
Thus \(h(p) = 0\), \(h(p^2) = 1\), and \(h(p^k) = 0\) for \(k \ge 3\). The powerful numbers \(\le 12\) with \(h(d) \neq 0\) are \(d \in \{1, 4, 9\}\) with \(h(1) = h(4) = h(9) = 1\).
Prefix sum: \(\sum_{n=1}^{12} f(n) = h(1) G(12) + h(4) G(3) + h(9) G(1) = 12 + 3 + 1 = 16\) (matching direct evaluation where \(f(n) = 1\) except at \(n \in \{4, 8, 9, 12\}\) where \(f(n) = 2\)).



Hint 1 — Diagnostic Signal & Combinatorial Model

When \(f\) and \(g\) are multiplicative and agree on all primes (\(f(p) = g(p)\)), their Bell series at every prime \(p\) agree up to degree \(1\): \(B_p(f; x) \equiv B_p(g; x) \pmod{x^2}\). What does that imply about the degree-1 term of their quotient \(B_p(h; x) = B_p(f; x) B_p(g; x)^{-1}\)?



Hint 2 — Algebraic Setup & Reverse-Engineering Scratchpad

Because \(B_p(f; x) = 1 + f(p) x + f(p^2) x^2 + \dots\) and \(B_p(g; x) = 1 + g(p) x + g(p^2) x^2 + \dots\) with \(f(p) = g(p)\), their ratio \(B_p(h; x) = B_p(f; x) / B_p(g; x)\) has \([x^1] B_p(h; x) = f(p) - g(p) = 0\)! Since \(h\) is multiplicative and \(h(p) = 0\) for every prime \(p\), \(h(n) = \prod_{p^k \parallel n} h(p^k) = 0\) whenever any prime divides \(n\) to the first power (\(k = 1\)).



Hint 3 — Coefficient Extraction & Complexity Contract


Sieve all primes \(p \le \sqrt{N}\).
For each prime \(p \le \sqrt{N}\) (or in \(O(\log^2 N)\) globally if \(h(p^k)\) is a polynomial in \(p^k\)), compute \(h(p^k)\) for \(2 \le k \le \lfloor \log_p N \rfloor\) via the \(O(k^2)\) Bell series recurrence \(h(p^k) = f(p^k) - \sum_{j=1}^k g(p^j) h(p^{k-j})\).
DFS over all powerful numbers \(d = \prod p_i^{k_i} \le N\) (choosing only exponents \(k_i \ge 2\) on primes \(p_i \le \sqrt{N / d_{\text{cur}}}\)), accumulating \(h(d) G(\lfloor N / d \rfloor) \bmod p\).








NoteComplete Derivation & Solution






Mathematical Derivation
Since \(f\) and \(g\) are multiplicative with \(f(1) = g(1) = 1\), both are units in the Dirichlet ring \(\mathcal{D}_f\), and their Dirichlet quotient \(h = f *_D g^{-1}\) is also multiplicative. At each prime \(p\), the Bell series satisfy:
\[
B_p(h; x) = \frac{B_p(f; x)}{B_p(g; x)} = \frac{1 + f(p) x + f(p^2) x^2 + \dots}{1 + g(p) x + g(p^2) x^2 + \dots} \quad \text{in } \mathbb{F}_p[[x]].
\]
Extracting \([x^1]\) from \(B_p(h; x) B_p(g; x) = B_p(f; x)\) gives:
\[
h(p) + g(p) h(1) = f(p) \implies h(p) = f(p) - g(p) = 0.
\]
For higher prime powers \(k \ge 2\), the truncated polynomial inversion recurrence in \(\mathbb{F}_p[x]/(x^{E+1})\) gives:
\[
h(p^k) = f(p^k) - \sum_{j=1}^{k-1} g(p^j) h(p^{k-j}) - g(p^k).
\]
Because \(h\) is multiplicative and \(h(p) = 0\) for every prime \(p\), any integer \(n = \prod p_i^{e_i}\) with at least one exponent \(e_i = 1\) has \(h(n) = \prod h(p_i^{e_i}) = 0\). Thus \(\operatorname{supp}(h)\) is contained in the powerful numbers:
\[
\mathcal{P}(N) = \left\{ d \le N : p \mid d \implies p^2 \mid d \right\}.
\]
Every powerful number \(d\) can be written uniquely as \(d = a^2 b^3\) with \(b\) square-free, so \(|\mathcal{P}(N)| \le \sum_{b=1}^{\lfloor N^{1/3} \rfloor} \sqrt{N / b^3} = O(\sqrt{N})\). Expanding \(f = h *_D g\) on the prefix sum \(\sum_{n=1}^N f(n)\) yields:
\[
\sum_{n=1}^N f(n) = \sum_{n=1}^N \sum_{d \mid n} h(d) \, g\!\left(\frac{n}{d}\right) = \sum_{\substack{d \in \mathcal{P}(N)}} h(d) \, G\!\left(\left\lfloor \frac{N}{d} \right\rfloor\right).
\]
// DFS over all O(sqrt(N)) powerful numbers d <= N, accumulating h(d) * G(N / d)
void dfs_pn(int idx, ll d, mint hd) {
    ans += hd * G_prefix(N / d);
    for (int i = idx; i < (int)primes.size(); ++i) {
        ll p = primes[i];
        if (d > N / (p * p)) break;
        ll pk = p * p;
        for (int k = 2; d <= N / pk; ++k) {
            if (h_pk[i][k].val() != 0) dfs_pn(i + 1, d * pk, hd * h_pk[i][k]);
            if (pk > N / p) break;
            pk *= p;
        }
    }
}


Algorithm Contract

Input & Exact Index Boundaries: Integer \(1 \le N \le 10^{11}\), prime-power evaluators for \(f(p^k), g(p^k)\) with \(f(p) = g(p)\), and fast prefix-sum oracle \(G(\lfloor N/d \rfloor)\).
Preconditions: \(f(1) = g(1) = 1 \in \mathbb{F}_p^\times\) and \(f(p) = g(p)\) for all primes \(p \le \sqrt{N}\).
Postconditions (Output): Returns \(\sum_{n=1}^N f(n) \bmod p\).
Time & Space Complexity: \(O(\sqrt{N})\) time and \(O(\sqrt{N})\) space to sieve primes up to \(\sqrt{N}\), precompute \(h(p^k)\) via Bell series division, and traverse all powerful numbers \(d \le N\).
Loop / Algebraic Invariant: Each DFS state (idx, d, hd) visits a unique powerful number \(d\) whose prime factors have indices \(< \text{idx}\) (or is extended by \(p_i^k\) with \(i \ge \text{idx}\) and \(k \ge 2\)), with hd \(= \prod_{p^k \parallel d} h(p^k)\).
Failure Modes & Edge Cases: When stepping prime powers pk *= p in the recursive DFS over powerful numbers \(d \le N\), always guard against 64-bit integer overflow using division (if (d > N / (p * p)) break; and if (pk > N / p) break;) before multiplying, since \(p^k\) or \(d \cdot p^k\) can exceed \(2^{63} - 1\) when \(N = 10^{11}\) and \(p \approx 3 \times 10^5\).









Mastery 2 (#038) — A Nameless Counting Problem

Source: AtCoder Beginner Contest 288 Ex — A Nameless Counting Problem
Prerequisites: Bitwise XOR Cancellation, Parity Decomposition, Digit DP & EGF-to-OGF Hyperbolic Substitution (§24.1, §24.3)


Problem Statement
Given three non-negative integers \(M, N, X\), find the number of non-decreasing sequences of \(N\) integers \(0 \le A_1 \le A_2 \le \dots \le A_N \le M\) such that their bitwise XOR sum equals \(X\):
\[
A_1 \oplus A_2 \oplus \cdots \oplus A_N = X.
\]
Output the answer modulo \(998244353\).


Constraints

\(0 \le M < 2^{30}\)
\(1 \le N \le 200\)
\(0 \le X < 2^{30}\)
Modulus: \(p = 998244353\)
Time limit: \(4.0\text{ s}\), Memory limit: \(1024\text{ MB}\)

Sample Trace (\(M = 2, N = 2, X = 1\)):

Non-decreasing pairs \(0 \le A_1 \le A_2 \le 2\) with \(A_1 \oplus A_2 = 1\):

Unordered pairs of distinct elements in \([0, 2]\) with XOR \(1\): only \(\{0, 1\}\) (since \(0 \oplus 1 = 1\), \(0 \oplus 2 = 2\), \(1 \oplus 2 = 3\)).
Since any duplicate pair \((v, v)\) cancels under XOR (\(v \oplus v = 0\)), every non-decreasing sequence of length \(N = 2\) with XOR \(1\) must consist of \(k = 2\) odd-multiplicity values \(\{0, 1\}\) and \(0\) even-multiplicity pairs!
Thus \((A_1, A_2) = (0, 1)\) is the unique solution (answer \(= 1\)).




Hint 1 — Diagnostic Signal & Combinatorial Model

In any multiset of \(N\) integers \(\{A_1 \le A_2 \le \dots \le A_N\}\), the bitwise XOR \(A_1 \oplus \dots \oplus A_N\) depends only on the parity of the frequency of each value \(v \in [0, M]\)! Specifically, if \(k\) distinct values \(v_1 < v_2 < \dots < v_k\) appear an odd number of times and all other values appear an even number of times, then \(N \equiv k \pmod 2\) and the remaining \((N - k)/2\) pairs of identical elements can be assigned freely to any values in \([0, M]\)!



Hint 2 — Algebraic Setup & Reverse-Engineering Scratchpad

Compare two generating functions in the XOR group algebra \(\mathbb{F}_p[\mathbb{Z}_2^{30}]\):

The OGF of multisets (what the problem asks for): each value \(v \in [0, M]\) contributes \(1 + x^v u + u^2 + x^v u^3 + \dots = \frac{1 + x^v u}{1 - u^2}\), giving \(\prod_{v=0}^M \frac{1 + x^v u}{1 - u^2} = (1 - u^2)^{-(M+1)} \prod_{v=0}^M (1 + x^v u)\).
The EGF of ordered tuples \(T_j\) in \([0, M]^j\) (easy to count via Digit DP): each value \(v \in [0, M]\) contributes \(\cosh(z) + x^v \sinh(z) = \cosh(z)(1 + x^v \tanh(z))\), giving \(\cosh(z)^{M+1} \prod_{v=0}^M (1 + x^v \tanh(z))\).




Hint 3 — Coefficient Extraction & Complexity Contract


Use MSB-to-LSB Digit DP in \(O(N^2 \log M)\) to compute \(T_j\) for \(0 \le j \le N\): the number of ordered \(j\)-tuples in \([0, M]^j\) with XOR \(X\).
Substitute \(z = \operatorname{artanh}(u) = \sum_{m \ge 0} \frac{u^{2m+1}}{2m+1}\) into the EGF \(\sum_{j=0}^N T_j \frac{z^j}{j!} \bmod u^{N+1}\). Since \(\cosh(\operatorname{artanh}(u)) = (1 - u^2)^{-1/2}\), multiplying the composed polynomial by \((1 - u^2)^{-(M+1)/2}\) produces \([x^X] \prod_{v=0}^M \frac{1 + x^v u}{1 - u^2}\)! Extract \([u^N]\) in \(O(N^2)\) polynomial operations.








NoteComplete Derivation & Solution






Mathematical Derivation
Every non-decreasing sequence \(0 \le A_1 \le A_2 \le \dots \le A_N \le M\) is uniquely identified by the multiplicity \(c_v \ge 0\) of each value \(v \in [0, M]\), where \(\sum_{v=0}^M c_v = N\). Because \(v \oplus v = 0\) in the XOR group \((\mathbb{Z}_2^{30}, \oplus)\), a value \(v\) with multiplicity \(c_v\) contributes \(x^v\) to the XOR product if \(c_v\) is odd, and \(x^0 = 1\) if \(c_v\) is even.
Therefore, in the formal power series ring \(\mathbb{F}_p[\mathbb{Z}_2^{30}][[u]]\) over the XOR group algebra, the bivariate OGF of non-decreasing sequences is:
\[
\Phi(x, u) = \prod_{v=0}^M \left(1 + x^v u + u^2 + x^v u^3 + \dots\right) = (1 - u^2)^{-(M+1)} \prod_{v=0}^M \left(1 + x^v u\right),
\]
and we seek \([x^X u^N] \Phi(x, u)\).
On the other hand, let \(T_j\) be the number of ordered \(j\)-tuples \((B_1, \dots, B_j) \in [0, M]^j\) (with repetition allowed) such that \(B_1 \oplus \dots \oplus B_j = X\). By the exponential formula for labeled sequences, the EGF of ordered tuples in \(\mathbb{F}_p[\mathbb{Z}_2^{30}][[z]]\) is:
\[
\begin{aligned}
\Psi(x, z) &= \sum_{j=0}^{\infty} \left(\sum_{v=0}^M x^v\right)^j \frac{z^j}{j!} = \exp\!\left(\sum_{v=0}^M x^v z\right) = \prod_{v=0}^M \exp(x^v z) \\
&= \prod_{v=0}^M \left(\sum_{m \ge 0} \frac{z^{2m}}{(2m)!} x^0 + x^v \sum_{m \ge 0} \frac{z^{2m+1}}{(2m+1)!}\right) \\
&= \prod_{v=0}^M \big(\cosh(z) + x^v \sinh(z)\big),
\end{aligned}
\]
where the last equality holds because \((x^v)^2 = x^{v \oplus v} = 1\) in \(\mathbb{F}_p[\mathbb{Z}_2^{30}]\)! Factoring out \(\cosh(z)\) from each of the \(M + 1\) terms yields:
\[
\Psi(x, z) = \cosh(z)^{M+1} \prod_{v=0}^M \big(1 + x^v \tanh(z)\big).
\]
Now substitute \(z = \operatorname{artanh}(u) = u + \frac{u^3}{3} + \frac{u^5}{5} + \dots \in \mathbb{F}_p[[u]]\) (valid up to \(u^N\) since \(N \le 200 < p\)). Using the identity \(\cosh(\operatorname{artanh}(u)) = (1 - u^2)^{-1/2}\) and extracting \([x^X]\) on both sides gives:
\[
\sum_{j=0}^{\infty} T_j \frac{\operatorname{artanh}(u)^j}{j!} = (1 - u^2)^{-\frac{M+1}{2}} [x^X] \prod_{v=0}^M \left(1 + x^v u\right).
\]
Comparing this with \(\Phi(x, u) = (1 - u^2)^{-(M+1)} \prod_{v=0}^M (1 + x^v u)\), we need only multiply by an extra factor of \((1 - u^2)^{-\frac{M+1}{2}}\) to obtain the exact OGF of our problem:
\[
\text{Ans} = [u^N] \left((1 - u^2)^{-\frac{M+1}{2}} \sum_{j=0}^N T_j \frac{\operatorname{artanh}(u)^j}{j!}\right) \pmod{998244353}.
\]
To compute \(T_0, \dots, T_N\) in \(O(N^2 \log M)\): run a Digit DP from bit \(b = 29\) down to \(0\) tracking how many of the \(j\) elements remain tight to \(M\). Even simpler: classify the \(j\) elements by the highest bit \(b\) where at least one element drops strictly below \(M_b = 1\); below bit \(b\), that loose element’s bits are completely free in \(\{0, 1\}\), so the XOR of bit \(b' < b\) is automatically satisfied in exactly \(2^{j-1}\) ways per bit!
// Given T[0..N] (ordered j-tuples in [0, M]^j with XOR = X from O(N^2 log M) Digit DP):
vector<mint> A(N + 1), B(N + 1); // B(u) = artanh(u) = u + u^3/3 + u^5/5 + ...
for (int i = 1; i <= N; i += 2) B[i] = inv_small[i];
vector<mint> pw(N + 1, 0); pw[0] = 1;
for (int j = 0; j <= N; ++j) {
    mint c = T[j] * ifac[j];
    for (int i = 0; i <= N; ++i) A[i] += c * pw[i];
    pw = poly_mul_trunc(pw, B, N); // O(N^2) truncated multiplication
}
// Multiply A(u) by (1 - u^2)^{-(M+1)/2} and extract A[N]


Algorithm Contract

Input & Exact Index Boundaries: \(0 \le M, X < 2^{30}\), \(1 \le N \le 200\), modulus \(p = 998244353\).
Preconditions: \(1, 2, \dots, N \in \mathbb{F}_p^\times\) (\(N \le 200 < 998244353\)).
Postconditions (Output): Returns \([u^N]\big((1 - u^2)^{-(M+1)/2} \sum_{j=0}^N T_j \frac{\operatorname{artanh}(u)^j}{j!}\big) \bmod p\).
Time & Space Complexity: \(O(N^2 \log M + N^3)\) time and \(O(N^2)\) space.
Loop / Algebraic Invariant: Because \(\prod_{v=0}^M (\cosh z + x^v \sinh z)\big|_{z = \operatorname{artanh}(u)} = (1 - u^2)^{-(M+1)/2} \prod_{v=0}^M (1 + x^v u)\), multiplying by \((1 - u^2)^{-(M+1)/2}\) produces \(\prod_{v=0}^M \frac{1 + x^v u}{1 - u^2}\), whose \([x^X u^N]\) coefficient is the exact count of \(N\)-element multisets in \([0, M]\) with XOR \(X\).
Failure Modes & Edge Cases: Because \(M < 2^{30}\) can be much larger than \(N \le 200\), when computing the generalized binomial coefficients of \((1 - u^2)^{-(M+1)/2}\), reduce the exponent \((M + 1) \bmod p\) before multiplying rising factorial terms, and ensure \(2^{-1} \bmod p\) is used when halving \((M + 1)\) in \(\mathbb{F}_p\).

When solving problems at the end of a specific textbook chapter, you benefit from chapter-title leakage: if a problem appears at the end of Chapter 07 (Roots of Unity, Multiplicative Indexing, 3-Prime NTT & Chirp-\(Z\)), you already know before reading a single sentence that you should look for a roots-of-unity filter, primitive-root discrete log, or Chirp-\(Z\) transform. In a live ICPC regional or high-rated online contest, no such label exists. A problem asking for a sum over \(2^q\) bracket completions, a bilinear form with \(c^{i^2 j^3}\), or a count of permutations with a prescribed win-loss margin arrives completely unadorned.

section: The 3-Axis Part II Diagnostic Rubric (No Spoilers)
text:
The 3-Axis Part II Diagnostic Rubric (No Spoilers)
When faced with an unlabeled counting or summation problem, run it through three orthogonal diagnostic axes before writing down any algebra:

Axis 1: Constraint & Query Scale (\(N, K, S\) vs. Modulus \(P\))
The raw numerical magnitudes of the input parameters eliminate impossible techniques immediately:

Tiny Dimension + Astronomical Target (e.g., \(n \le 20\), target degree \(\ge 10^{12}\)):

Dense polynomial arithmetic up to the target degree is impossible. Look for a sparse product of \(n\) factors that expands into \(2^n\) monomials, paired with an \(O(n)\) closed-form coefficient extraction on the remaining dense series.

Moderate Dimension (\(N \le 2000\)) + Arbitrary / Non-NTT Prime (\(10^9+7, 10^9+9\)):

\(O(N^2)\) dynamic programming or \(O(N^2)\) precomputed binomial sums fit comfortably within 1 second without needing NTT. Look for a 2D combinatorial state space or a double sum that either runs in \(O(N^2)\) directly or collapses to \(O(N)\) via binomial absorption.

Quasilinear Scale (\(N \le 10^5\) or \(10^6\)) + Prime Modulus:

\(O(N^2)\) is strictly TLE. Any double sum \(\sum_{i,j}\) must be decoupled into a 1D convolution \(\sum_{u+v=w} A_u B_v\) or collapsed in \(O(N)\) linear time via an algebraic identity.

Huge Evaluation Point (\(N \le 10^9\)) + Moderate Parameter (\(K \le 10^6\)):

Iterating up to \(N\) is impossible, yet \(K\) is small enough for \(O(K)\) linear space and time. Check whether the target quantity \(F(N)\) is a polynomial or rational function in \(N\) of degree \(O(K)\) that can be reconstructed from \(O(K)\) small sample values.








NoteOptional Pre-Flight Reference: The 3-Axis Diagnostic Decision Tree (Consult After Stage 1 Cold Read)






Axis 2: Algebraic Coupling Shape
Look at how the summation indices \((i, j, k)\) interact inside the summand:








Coupling Pattern
Structural Signature
Candidate Decoupling Tool




Difference + Index
\(\sum_k f(j-k) g(k)\) or \(\binom{j}{k} (-1)^{j-k} k^i\)
Factor \(\binom{j}{k} = \frac{j!}{k!(j-k)!}\) and apply 1D NTT Cauchy Convolution.


Complementary Upper Indices
\(\sum_k \binom{x}{k-L} \binom{y}{k-R}\)
Flip one binomial via \(\binom{y}{k-R} = \binom{y}{y+R-k}\) so lower indices sum to \(y+R-L\), then apply Vandermonde’s Identity.


Bilinear Exponent
\(\sum_{i,j} a_i b_j c^{\phi(i)\psi(j)} \pmod p\)
Bucket \(I = \phi(i) \bmod (p-1)\), \(J = \psi(j) \bmod (p-1)\) and apply Bluestein’s Chirp-\(Z\) Identity \(IJ = \binom{I+J}{2} - \binom{I}{2} - \binom{J}{2}\).


Upper-Triangular Binomial Kernel
\(g_j = \sum_{m=j}^n \binom{m}{j} f_m\)
Invert via Binomial Inversion \(f_k = \sum_{j=k}^n (-1)^{j-k} \binom{j}{k} g_j\).


Prescribed Multiplicities in a Sequence
Sequence of length \(L\) where item \(i\) appears \(c_i\) times
Extract \([x^L] L! \prod_{i=1}^n \frac{x^{c_i}}{c_i!} = \frac{L!}{\prod_{i=1}^n c_i!}\) via Multinomial EGF.





Axis 3: Combinatorial Obstruction Keyword
Translate verbal constraints in the problem statement directly into algebraic operators:

“At most \(f_i\) items from box \(i\)”: Bounded geometric series \(\frac{1 - x^{f_i+1}}{1 - x}\).
“Exactly \(K\) occurrences / wins / matches”: Usually intractable to count directly because forbidding the remaining \(N-K\) positions from accidentally matching creates global dependencies. Relax to “designate at least \(j \ge K\) occurrences” (\(g_j\)), complete the remaining \(N-j\) elements freely, and recover \(f_K\) via Binomial Inversion.
“Number of labeled trees with prescribed degrees \(d_1, \dots, d_n\)”: Biject via Prüfer sequences to words of length \(n-2\) over alphabet \(\{1, \dots, n\}\) where label \(i\) appears \(d_i - 1\) times.
“Maximum nested depth of a bracket subsequence”: By split-point duality, equals \(\max_{0 \le i \le n} \min(\text{count of } \texttt{(} \text{ in } s[1..i],\, \text{count of } \texttt{)} \text{ in } s[i+1..n])\), occurring at the unique split point \(i\) where prefix \(\texttt{(}\) count equals suffix \(\texttt{)}\) count.

    Start["Unlabeled Counting or Summation Problem"] --> Q1{"What is the primary obstruction?"}
    
    Q1 -->|"Explicit Double Sum or Polynomial Evaluation"| SumBranch{"Inspect Index Coupling & Scale"}
    Q1 -->|"Combinatorial Constraints ('At most', 'Exactly K', 'Degrees')"| CombBranch{"Inspect Constraint Keyword"}
    
    SumBranch -->|"Huge N <= 10^9, Degree K <= 10^6"| Lagrange["Polynomial in N of degree O(K): Sieve y_0..y_{K+1} + O(K) Lagrange Interpolation"]
    SumBranch -->|"Stirling / Binomial Sum, N <= 10^5"| StirlingNTT["Expand falling/Stirling basis, swap sums, decouple via 1D NTT"]

    SumBranch -->|"Bilinear Exponent c^(f(i)g(j)) mod P"| Bluestein["Bucket exponents mod (P-1), apply Bluestein CZT IJ = C(I+J,2)-C(I,2)-C(J,2)"]
